Overview 


This document contains technical information and specifications for customers to understand 
the system functionality and to process transactions through the Single Message System. 
System specifications are based on Mastercard's adoption of the International Organization for 
Standardization (ISO) 8583:1987 message formats. 


Audience 


This document is intended for parties using the Mastercard Network to process transactions 
through the Single Message System. This includes acquirers, issuers, processors, and Network 
Enablement Partners.

How to use this guide 


Chapter 1 How to use this guide 


This guide navigates users through the foundation of the Single Message System, its functions, 
applicable messages, and their intended use. 


Structure of the guide 


The material presents each topic with a high-level overview followed by additional details as the 
document progresses. 


The initial chapters provide guidance for implementation of the Single Message System specifications 
to support Mastercard account operations. The guide then describes the details of how Mastercard 
aligns with the ISO 8583:1987 messaging standards. This guide also includes Mastercard data 
validations and supplemental reports. 


The appendices provide supporting information to the chapters, including a glossary and basic 
information about Mastercard products and services available to customers. 


This document provides the acronym phrase or word definition when the user hovers their mouse over 
a highlighted word. Links within the document allow for the user to navigate directly to a related 
section, which provides supporting information for that topic. 


NOTE: Link and hover features are available in select formats only.

High-level overview 


Fundamentals of Mastercard processing 


Mastercard processing supports the four-party model (cardholders, acceptors [merchant, sponsored 
merchant, Automated Teller Machine (ATM) owner, or other party], cardholder bank and acceptor 
bank). This process is explained by three main functions and the subsequent flow diagram. 


• 
Authorization: Real-time communication between acquirers and issuers to approve or decline the 
use of a Mastercard card, access device, or account to conduct a transaction. Approval from the 
issuer creates a financial obligation from the issuer to the acquirer (for a transaction that debits 
funds from a cardholder's account) or from the acquirer to the issuer (for a transaction that 
credits funds to a cardholder's account). 
• 
Clearing: Multiple clearing batch processes per day (that is, clearing cycles) determine and 
calculate processing costs, resulting in one net amount per acquirer and issuer per clearing cycle. 
• 
Settlement: Aggregation of financial positions from all clearing settlement information into one 
overall daily net settlement amount for each acquirer and issuer. Advisements (notifications) are 
created and distributed to acquirers and issuers along with Transfer Funds Orders to settlement 
banks for amounts to be transferred to or collected from acquirers and issuers. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



High-level overview 
Introduction to Mastercard switches for processing 


Figure 1: Authorization, Clearing, and Settlement flows 


Process flow displaying the three main functions. 



Introduction to Mastercard switches for processing 


Mastercard leverages its Dual Message Switch and Single Message Switch for the global 
processing of transaction data over the Mastercard Network. 


The Dual Message Switch completes processing for Authorization, Clearing, and Settlement 
functions using both online and batch systems. Authorization processes as a real-time message, 
while Clearing and Settlement functions are achieved through a batch process. 


The Single Message Switch completes processing for Authorization, Clearing, and Settlement 
functions leveraging a single online message. Authorization processes as a real-time message 
and automatically enables Clearing and Settlement functions through an internal batch process. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



High-level overview 
Introduction to Mastercard Single Message System processing 


Introduction to Mastercard Single Message System processing 


The Mastercard Single Message System is a global, real-time message processing system and is 
a component of the Mastercard Network. The Mastercard Network supports real-time 
authorization processing followed by batch reconciliation leading to settlement of funds 
between acquirers and issuers. 


Mastercard acquirers and issuers leverage the Single Message System to exchange financial 
transaction data captured at the point-of-interaction (POI) device. The Single Message System, 
through a single financial message interaction, fulfills authorization processing, reconciliation, 
and settlement functions. 


The Single Message System consists of both hardware and software components. The physical 
computing infrastructure includes servers, routers, switches, and cabling. This hardware is 
configured with Mastercard proprietary technology, which makes it a Mastercard interface 
processors and is physically set up and connected with an acquirer or issuer processing system in 
their data centers. 


For more information on system access, refer to System access information. 


Single Message System features 


The Single Message System provides many features, including but not limited to the following. 


• 
Access for all acquirers and issuers 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. 
The Mastercard Network operates on a continuous basis, helping to ensure that cardholders 
can use Mastercard cards and access devices anytime and that acquirers, issuers, and 
acceptors always have access to Mastercard authorization processing capabilities. 
• 
Real-time authorization processing. 
The design of the Mastercard Network enhances processing by routing transactions along the 
shortest communication path to the destination. The network's design consists of alternate 
paths guaranteeing that there are always two or more paths to a given destination. If part 
of the network is unavailable, the multi-routing capability ensures that transactions continue 
toward their destinations following the shortest possible path, minimizing network 
congestion. 
• 
Support for alternate routing and authorizing paths. 
At times, acquirers or issuers may experience internal communication problems, scheduled 
down times, or network problems. The system provides backup authorization alternatives 
ensuring that an authorization response occurs for every transaction. 
• 
Security and fraud management services. 
The Single Message System provides services that help make Mastercard transactions safe 
and secure. 
• 
Currency conversion capabilities. 
The Single Message System provides currency conversion to acquirers and issuers to enable 
processing of online transaction messages in the acquirer or issuer's preferred currency. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



High-level overview 
Participants in Mastercard Network processing 


• 
Reconciliation processing. 
The Single Message System, in addition to authorization processing, also calculates 
interchange fees, calculates acquirer and issuer settlement amounts, and reconciles for 
acquirers and issuers. 
• 
Supplemental reports. 
Mastercard produces various authorization-related reports that display acquirer and issuer 
authorization activity and help acquirers and issuers to manage their back-office processes. 
• 
The Single Message System also supports interfaces to enable non-Mastercard account 
processing.

Mastercard Network processing involves various functions and types of participants. This list 
includes the most common participants involved in processing, along with simplified 
descriptions.

Single Message System basics 


Single Message System basics 


The following diagram illustrates the basic Single Message System flow. 


Figure 3: Basic Single Message System flow 



1. 
The cardholder presents a Mastercard payment instrument to the acceptor to pay for goods 
or services or withdraw money from an ATM. 
2. 
Transaction data is entered into the POI of the acceptor. The acceptor sends a request for an 
authorization decision to the acquirer. 
3. 
The acquirer receives the request, appends additional data as needed, and sends the 
message to the Mastercard Single Message System. 
4. 
The Single Message System receives the message and validates format and content. 
Mastercard includes additional data as needed and sends the issuer the request message. 
5. 
The issuer receives the message and evaluates the transaction data and the account itself 
before making an authorization decision. The issuer generates a request response message 
indicating its decision and sends the response message to Mastercard. 
6. 
Mastercard receives the message and validates format and content. Mastercard includes 
additional data as needed and sends the response message to the acquirer. 
7. 
The acquirer receives the response message and notifies the acceptor of the decision. 
8. 
The acceptor receives the response to the decision and completes the transaction with the 
cardholder. 
9. 
The issuer posts the completed transaction to the cardholder's account. 
10. 
At the end of the processing day, Mastercard generates reporting and settles with the 
acquirer and issuer for the transaction. 
NOTE: Mastercard reserves the right to record, store, and use all data transmitted by the Mastercard 
Single Message System in online electronic transactions, subject to Mastercard privacy and security 
compliance policies and applicable laws and regulations, without further notice.

Introduction to messages 


Overview 


The Single Message System format is based on ISO 8583:1987 standards, which is comprised of code 
values, data elements, and message types. Systems use the ISO 8583:1987 protocol for the 
electronic exchange of transaction data for the purchase of goods or services. 


The ISO standard defines the purpose of the message and origination through the Message Type 
Indicators. The following table defines the valid MTI values. 


Table 4: ISO-defined MTI codes and related usage 


Code 
Meaning 
Usage 
00xx 
Reserved by ISO 
N/A 
01xx 
Authorization messages 
Authorization messages are used 
by the acquirers to obtain approval 
or guarantee funds from the 
issuers. These messages are not 
intended for use in posting to the 
cardholder’s account. 
02xx 
Financial messages 
Financial messages are used by the 
acquirer to obtain approval or 
guarantee funds from the issuer. 
These messages allow the 
approved transaction to post to the 
cardholder’s account. 
03xx 
File action messages 
File action messages are used to 
add, change, delete, or inquire into 
a file or record (for example, to 
report lost or stolen cards). 
04xx 
Reversal messages 
Reversal messages are used to 
partially or completely negate the 
effects of a previous financial or 
authorization transaction. 
05xx 
Reconciliation messages (not used 
by Mastercard) 
Reconciliation messages provide 
financial totals between an acquirer 
and an issuer. 
06xx 
Administrative messages 
Administrative messages are used 
for the exchange of non-financial 
information between network 
participants. 
07xx 
Reserved by ISO 
N/A

Mastercard message classifications 


The Mastercard Network allows for the exchange of electronic data that may or may not contain 
account holder information or result in a financial transaction. The remaining message types are 
used to support administrative functions. 


The message types adopted for use by the Single Message System, as a broad classification, falls 
into three functional categories. 


Table 7: Message type functional categories 


Financial message function 
This message type function results in a financial 
impact to a cardholder's account. It includes 
instructions or data related to payments, transfers, 
debits, or credits. 


Non-financial message function 
This message type function allows acquirers and 
issuers to validate account information prior to the 
submission of a financial message without 
financial impact to an account. 


Supporting message function 
This message type function allows acquirers and 
issuers connected to the Mastercard Network to 
complete administrative functions, such as file 
updates and network management.

the originating parties for each message type. The Single Message System may not support all 
message types for each Mastercard program or service.

described in the following table and may be liable for the impacts of transmitting erroneous 
messages.

About message definitions 


This section provides details on message definitions. 


Financial Transaction/02xx messages 


The phrase financial transaction applies when there is sufficient data contained within the 
individual transaction message to allow the issuer to post to the cardholder account. 


The Mastercard Network uses Financial Transaction/02xx messages for: 


• 
Financial Transaction Request/0200 
• 
Financial Transaction Request Responses/0210 
• 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220 
• 
Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 
The Mastercard Network processes all Financial Transaction/02xx messages assuming that 
upon successful completion the system does not require subsequent information to complete 
settlement and cardholder account posting. There may be exceptions when additional may be 
required to complete the transaction. 


About Address Verification System 


Chip card transactions at an ATM must contain a PIN for online authorization. The Mastercard 
Network declines Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages from an acquirer for offline chip 
card transactions at an ATM with a DE 39 (Response Code) value of 12 (Invalid Transaction). 


Address Verification Service (AVS) is a fraud deterrent service that provides greater security to 
merchants and cardholders. It helps protect against fraudulent use of cards by verifying the 
cardholder’s billing address. This functionality is supported during the process of obtaining 
authorization for a transaction. For more information on this service, please refer to 
#unique_130. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
Financial Transaction/02xx messages 


About Financial Transaction Advice Messages 


The Mastercard Network uses a guaranteed advice message delivery concept for all advice 
messages transmitted through the network. When the Single Message System processes an 
advice message, the system acknowledges receipt of the advice message to the initiator with an 
advice response message and forwards the advice message to the intended recipient. 


If the Single Message System cannot deliver an advice message immediately (for example, due 
to a system or communication failure at the receiving destination), the Single Message System 
stores the message within the store-and-forward (SAF) queue. SAF processing automatically 
delivers the message to the destination when communication is restored.

Reversal Advice/04xx messages 


Reversal Advice/04xx messages reverse the impact of a previous Financial Transaction/02xx 
message. 


These messages come under the general category of advice messages; therefore, they are 
subject to the Guaranteed Advice Delivery procedures that are standard for all advice messages. 


If, for any reason, the Single Message System cannot immediately deliver these messages to 
their intended destination, the Single Message System assumes responsibility for storing and 
forwarding them to the proper destination when communication is restored. 


The Reversal Advice Messages include: 


• 
Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message 
• 
Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 message 
• 
Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 message 
• 
Issuer Reversal Advice Response/0432 message 
The reversal advice message and its response can be designated acquirer (0420/0430 
sequence) or issuer (0422/0432 sequence), and the Single Message System enables several 
usages within these categories. 


For settlement purposes, this message contains force-post information. Thus, the Mastercard 
Network processes the reversal regardless of message receipt acknowledgment. 


The Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message has five uses: 


• 
Standard reversal advice: corrects or cancels the amount dispensed or authorized from the 
original terminal request. 
• 
Time-out-induced reversal advice: acquirer (before settlement): available to acquirers when 
the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 does not arrive back to the acquirer in the 
required time. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
Reversal Advice/04xx messages 


• 
Time-out-induced reversal advice, system-generated: informs issuers the Mastercard 
Network did not receive a Financial Transaction Response/0210 from the issuer in the 
required time interval (time-out condition) or that the message failed edit checks. 
• 
Acquirer reversal advice-exception, system-generated (after settlement): Authorized 
representatives of an acquirer, an issuer, or Mastercard uses the Single Message Transaction 
Manager (SMTM) to submit an adjustment, chargeback, or representment, which the 
Mastercard Network passes on to the issuer in the form of an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 
message. 
• 
Online exception: the following apply: 
– 
After settlement: Available to acquirers to submit adjustments and representments after 
the settlement day of the original transaction. using this abbreviated Acquirer Reversal 
Advice/0420 message. 
– 
For Payment Transactions, the Single Message System will support same-day reversals in 
online exceptions.

Administrative Advice/06xx messages 


Administrative Advice messages transmit free-form and proprietary data between parties 
connected to the Mastercard Network. 


The Single Message System routes messages from an originator to a destination and, in general, 
does not distinguish whether the originator or destination is an issuer or an acquirer. 


Administrative Advice messages include: 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
Administrative Advice/06xx messages 


• 
Administrative Advice/0620 message 
• 
Administrative Advice Response/0630 message 
• 
Administrative Advice/0644 message 
The Administrative Advice/06xx messages used by the Single Message System fall under the 
general category of advice messages and are subject to the Guaranteed Advice Delivery 
procedures. 


If, for any reason, the intended destination does not immediately receive these messages, the 
Mastercard Network assumes responsibility for storing and forwarding them to the proper 
destination when the network delivery point re-establishes communication. 


The Mastercard Network uses Administrative Advice/0620 messages to return indecipherable 
messages to a message originator with an appropriate error condition code that indicates the 
point at which the Mastercard Network terminated message parsing or message processing. 
The types of messages returned in an Administrative Advice/0620 message would either have 
improperly coded or garbled Message Type Indicator fields or improperly coded bit maps. In all 
cases, the advice reason code within the Administrative Advice/0620 message determines the 
specific reason for the advice message.

Network Management/08xx messages 


Network Management/08xx messages coordinate network events or tasks and can also be used 
to communicate network status conditions. 
These messages are used by participants on the Single Message System and the system itself. 
Network Management/08xx messages include: 


• 
Network Management Request/0800 message 
• 
Network Management Request Response/0810 message 
• 
Network Management Advice/0820 message 
Typical uses of Network Management/08xx messages include: 
• 
Sign-on/sign-off from the Single Message System 
• 
Inquire on customer systems or Single Message System status 
• 
Perform encryption key management 
• 
Perform network connection status inquiry (also known as echo tests) 
• 
Store-and-forward (SAF) requests 
• 
Advise of Store-and-forward (SAF) end-of-file (EOF) conditions 
The Single Message System routes all Network Management/08xx messages from an originator 
to a destination and, in general, does not distinguish whether the originator or destination is an 
acquirer or issuer.

Standard Debit Mastercard transaction 


Standard Debit Mastercard transaction 


This message flow describes the message flow for a Debit Mastercard financial transaction. The 
approval may be for the full or partial amount. 


Figure 5: Standard Debit Mastercard transaction flow 



1. 
The acquirer sends the Authorization Request/0100 for a Debit Mastercard transaction to 
the Mastercard Network. 
2.

ATM Terminal Failure 


This message flow describes exception procedures when the acquirer is not able to complete the 
cardholder's ATM transaction. This situation may develop due to a terminal failure that results 
in partial or non-dispense of cash, communication failure within the acquirer's own network, or 
cardholder cancellation of the transaction before receiving a response.

The figure does not illustrate the error condition for processing Reversal Advice/04xx messages. 
The acquirer should retransmit a reversal advice message that did not transmit successfully. 
Issuing and acquiring processors must assume the responsibility for identifying any message as 
a possible duplicate transaction. 


The Mastercard Network uses Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 and Acquirer Reversal Advice 
Response/0430 messages with Financial Transaction/02xx messages when encountering 
transaction flow exception (error) situations during financial transaction processing. For specific 
exception conditions, the Mastercard Network may directly generate Acquirer Reversal Advice/ 
0420 messages. Refer to the Financial Transaction/02xx message flow schematics to determine 
proper use of Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 and Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 
messages in these exception-processing situations.

Maestro preauthorization and completion standard message 


Maestro preauthorization and completion standard message 


This message flow describes a POS preauthorization and completion transaction. 


Figure 8: Maestro preauthorization and completion message flow 



© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
Maestro preauthorization and completion standard message 


1. 
The acquirer initiates a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the Mastercard 
Network. The message indicates this is a preauthorization request. 
2. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the 
issuer. 
3. 
If approved, the issuer puts a conditional hold on the cardholder's account and returns a 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message to the Mastercard Network. 
4. 
The Mastercard Network returns the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message to the acquirer. 
5. 
Within 20 minutes of the original Financial Transaction Request/0200 message, the acquirer 
must send a Financial Transaction Advice/0220 completion message to the Mastercard 
Network. The acquirer must provide this completion message with the actual completed 
amount of the transaction for the issuer to post to the cardholder's account. The acquirer 
must provide this completed amount in DE 95 (Replacement Amounts). DE 61 (Point of 
Service [POS] Data), subfield 7 (POS Transaction Status Indicator), and DE 4 (Amount, 
Transaction) will contain the same values as in the original Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 message. 
6. 
The Mastercard Network responds with a Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 
message to the acquirer. 
7. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message to the 
issuer. 
8. 
The issuer responds with a Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 message. 
If the Mastercard Network does not receive a Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message from 
the acquirer, the Mastercard Network assumes that the acquirer did not complete the 
transaction, and no further message processing occurs. 


The Mastercard Network treats the Maestro preauthorization and completion cycle as a single 
transaction. This is unlike the Debit Mastercard preauthorization and completion cycle, which 
the Mastercard Network treats as two separate transactions. This difference is because the 
Mastercard Network completes the Maestro processing cycle within 20 minutes on the same 
settlement day, while the Mastercard Network typically processes the Debit Mastercard 
completion message within 5 calendar days of the preauthorization message. 


The Financial Transaction Request/0200 message must contain the value 4 in DE 61 (Point of 
Service [POS] Data), subfield 7 for Maestro preauthorization transactions. The Financial 
Transaction Advice/0220 message will contain DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] Data), subfield 7, 
value 4 for a Maestro preauthorization completion. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026

Maestro preauthorization with multiple completion messages 


Maestro preauthorization with multiple completion messages 


This message flow describes the flow of messages when a Maestro Financial Transaction 
Request results in multiple Financial Transaction Advice or completion messages. 


Figure 9: Maestro preauthorization with multiple completion messages flow 



© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
Maestro preauthorization with multiple completion messages 


1. 
The acquirer initiates a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the Mastercard 
Network. The request message indicates that this is a preauthorization message where the 
preauthorization is in effect for 7 days. 
2. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the 
issuer. 
3. 
The issuer generates a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message and sends it 
to the Mastercard Network. 
4. 
The Mastercard Network returns the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message to the acquirer. 
5. 
The acquirer generates a Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message and sends it to the 
Mastercard Network. The amount in the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 advice message 
is only for a portion of the amount in the preauthorization. The acquirer includes an advice 
reason which informs the issuer that this message is only a partial completion and there will 
be multiple completions for the original authorization. 
6. 
The Mastercard Network sends the acquirer a Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 
message to acknowledge receipt of the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 advice message. 
7. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message to the 
issuer. 
8. 
The issuer responds with a Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 message. 
9. 
The acquirer generates another Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message and sends it to 
the Mastercard Network. The amount in the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 advice 
message is the remainder of the amount from the preauthorization. The acquirer will include 
an advice reason which informs the issuer that this message is only a partial completion and 
this is the final completion message. The acquirer can split the preauthorization into 
additional completion messages. The last Financial Transaction Advice/0220 advice 
message in the series must indicate it is the final clearing completion. 
10. 
The Mastercard Network sends the acquirer a Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 
message to acknowledge receipt of the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 advice message. 
11. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message to the 
issuer. 
12. 
The issuer responds with a Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 message.

© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
Response Failure from an issuer host to the issuer MIP 


1. 
The acquirer initiates a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the Mastercard 
Network. 
2. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the 
issuer MIP. 
3. 
The issuer MIP sends the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the issuer host. 
4. 
The issuer host generates the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message and 
cannot deliver the response to the issuer MIP because of a communication failure. The issuer 
must assume that the Mastercard Network or the acquirer will take appropriate action and 
should immediately reverse the impact to the cardholder's account if the issuer has 
approved the request. 
5. 
The Mastercard Network detects a time-out condition because of the issuer communication 
failure on the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message. The Mastercard 
Network generates a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message to the 
acquirer, indicating a request denial. The Mastercard Network creates an Acquirer Reversal 
Advice/0420 message indicating the acquirer did not receive the Financial Transaction 
Request Response/0210 message. The Mastercard Network places this message in the SAF 
queue for later delivery to the issuer. 
6. 
The Mastercard Network initiates a Network Management Request/0800 message from 
the configured production sites at regular intervals to verify connection with the issuer. This 
message is delivered to the issuer MIP. 
7. 
The issuer MIP sends the network-status request message to the issuer host. 
8. 
The issuer host responds with a Network Management Request Response/0810 message to 
the issuer MIP. 
9. 
The issuer MIP sends the Network Management Request Response/0810 message to the 
Mastercard Network. 
10. 
The Mastercard Network sends an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message advising the 
issuer that the transaction was not received within the time limit. It is delivered to the issuer 
MIP. 
11. 
The issuer MIP forwards the Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message to the issuer host. 
12. 
The issuer host responds with an Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 message to the 
issuer MIP. 
13. 
The issuer MIP sends the Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 message to the 
Mastercard Network. 
14. 
The Mastercard Network sends a Network Management Advice/0820 message to the issuer 
MIP to indicate the SAF facility has reached an end-of-file (EOF) condition. 
15. 
The Network Management Advice/0820 message is delivered to the issuer host.

Failure: issuer late response without Stand-In Authorization 


This message flow describes the transaction flow when an issuer sends a late Financial 
Transaction Request Response/0210 message. 


Figure 31: Failure: Issuer late response without Stand-In Authorization flow 



1. 
The acquirer initiates a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the Mastercard 
Network. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
Reversal advice messages 


2. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the 
issuer. The Mastercard Network detects a time-out condition since the Financial Transaction 
Request Response/0210 message was not received within the time limit. 
3. 
The Mastercard Network then generates a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message to the acquirer, indicating a request decline. The Mastercard Network also creates 
an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message indicating the issuer did not send the Financial 
Transaction Request Response/0210 message. The Mastercard Network places this 
message in the SAF file for later delivery to the issuer. 
4. 
The Mastercard Network receives an unsolicited (late) Request Response/0210 message 
from the issuer. 
5. 
If the late Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message indicates an approval 
from the issuer, the Mastercard Network responds with an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 
message indicating to the issuer that this Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message is late and rejected. The issuer must assume the Mastercard Network or acquirer 
will take appropriate action at this point and should immediately reverse any impact to the 
cardholder's account. This step also applies to approved transfer transactions. If the late 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message has a response code indicating a 
decline, then the Mastercard Network will not send the Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 
message. 
6. 
The issuer responds with an Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 message to the 
Mastercard Network. The Mastercard Network initiates a Network Management Request/ 
0800 echo test message from the configured production sites at regular intervals to verify 
or establish communication with the issuer. The issuer responds with a Network 
Management Request Response/0810 message. 
7. 
The Mastercard Network sends the Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message advising the 
time-out error from the SAF queue to the issuer. The Mastercard Network sends any 
remaining messages stored in the SAF queue to the issuer. 
8. 
The issuer responds with an Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 message to the 
Mastercard Network. The Mastercard Network sends a Network Management Advice/0820 
message to indicate the SAF facility has reached an EOF condition.

Standard reversal advice: same day before settlement 


Standard reversal advice: same day before settlement 


This message flow describes when a standard reversal advice is used to correct or cancel the 
amount dispensed or authorized from the original terminal request. This can be done on the 
same day as the transaction prior to settlement. 


Figure 32: Standard Reversal Advice: same day before settlement flow 



1. 
The acquirer identifies the need to correct the transaction amount or cancel the transaction 
completely prior to the end-of-day when settlement would occur. The acquirer sends an 
Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message containing the appropriate values indicating the 
action being taken. If the amount is being adjusted, the new amount will be reflected in the 
advice message. 
2. 
The Mastercard Network responds with an Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 
message to the acquirer. 
3. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the reversal advice message received to the issuer. The 
issuer should make the appropriate adjustments to the cardholder’s account. 
4. 
The issuer responds to the Mastercard Network with an Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/ 
0430 message.

Single Message Transaction Manager-generated adjustment 


This message flow describes when an acquirer uses Single Message Transaction Monitor to 
correct the amount from a previously settled transaction. 


Figure 33: Single Message Transaction Manager-generated adjustment flow 



1. 
An acquirer or an authorized representative of an acquirer uses Single Message Transaction 
Manager to create an adjustment. 
2. 
After the Mastercard Network generates an adjustment based on the data entry, it 
forwards the appropriate messages to the issuer and the acquirer. The acquirer always 
receives an Issuer Reversal Advice/0422; the issuer always receives an Acquirer Reversal 
Advice/0420. The Advice Reason Code provided in DE 60 (Advice Reason Code) of the 
message identifies the purpose of the reversal advice. 
3. 
Both the Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 and Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 messages contain 
DE 90 (Original Data Elements) with the same data elements as the original transaction to 
identify the financial transaction impacted by the reversal advice. All reversal advices 
contain settlement amount and transaction fee data that affect reconciliation and 
settlement.

This message flow describes standard transaction processing when changing or unblocking a 
PIN. 


Figure 42: Standard PIN management request flow 



1. 
The cardholder initiates a PIN management request (PIN change or PIN unblock) at an ATM. 
The ATM requests data from the chip card and forwards the data in the request to the 
acquirer. 
2. 
The acquirer sends a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message containing the 
appropriate values to indicate a PIN Management request to the Mastercard Network. 
3. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the 
issuer. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
PIN-management request failure from acquirer 


4. 
The issuer sends a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message to the 
Mastercard Network approving or declining the request. The issuer will make updates within 
the issuer host system to reflect the PIN change or PIN unblock. 
5. 
The Mastercard Network forwards the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message to the acquirer. 
6.

provides the result to the ATM to complete the transaction.

Network connection status request customer-generated 


1. 
The acquirer processing system or the issuer processing system originates the Network 
Management Request/0800 message for signing-on to the Mastercard Network. 
This can either be a general sign-on request or an issuer sign-on request. If it is an issuer 


sign-on request, the Mastercard Network will cease Stand-In processing for the issuer. 


The processor could also initiate a sign-off request which could be a general sign-off or an 
issuer sign-off request.

Request Response/0810 message, which contains the same value in DE 70 (Network 
Management Information Code) the Mastercard Network received in the Network 
Management Request/0800 message. 
The Single Message System does not use any sign-on or sign-off process for the Network 
Management Advice/0820 message. 


NOTE: The figure does not illustrate the error condition message flow for Network Management/08xx 
messages. Retransmit unsuccessful Network Management Request/0800 message transmissions. 


Network connection status request customer-generated 


This message flow describes how the acquirer or issuer can initiate an echo test from a 
configured production site to the Mastercard Network, and the Mastercard Network can initiate 
an echo test to the acquirer or issuer. 


The echo test is a means of establishing a connection between an acquirer or issuer and the 
Mastercard Network to confirm availability for processing messages. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Introduction to messages 
Network connection status request customer-generated 


Figure 53: Network connection status request customer-generate 



1. 
The acquirer processing system or the issuer processing system initiates a Network 
Management Request/0800 message indicating an echo test request and sends it to the 
Mastercard Network. 
2. 
The Mastercard Network responds to the Network connection status request customergenerate 
request with a Network Management Request Response/0810 message, which 
contains the same value in DE 70 (Network Management Information Code) as that 
received from the acquirer or issuer in the Network Management Request/0800 message. 
Receipt of the Network Management Request Response/0810 message by the acquirer or 
issuer indicates that the Mastercard Network is operating and can process message traffic. 
This ends the acquirer- or issuer-generated Network connection status request customergenerate 
test flow. 


Using the Network connection status request customer-generate test Mastercard requests the 
acquirer or issuer to send any SAF messages the acquirer or issuer has for the Mastercard 
Network. The Mastercard Network will send the appropriate response to each request. When 
the acquirer or issuer sends these messages, the acquirer or issuer does not have to end the 
session by delivering a Network Management Advice/0820 message.

PIN Encryption Key exchange request: customer generated 


Customers must be capable of sending a Network Management Request/0800: PEK exchange 
customer-generated message to the Mastercard Network requesting a new PEK. The 
Mastercard Network immediately initiates a PEK exchange with the customer identified in DE 
33 (Forwarding Institution Identification Code) of the Network Management Request/0800: 
PEK exchange On Demand message. Customers should use this feature when systems problems 
occur and a re-synchronization of the PEK is necessary. Mastercard exchanges PEKs with 
customers every 24 hours.

Overview 


This describes how the data attributes and notations are documented for use in the Mastercard 
Network's Single Message System. This information provides details necessary to build or receive the 
messages supported by the system as described in Data element definitions and details. 


The notations used to describe the data elements and message formats are: 


•

•

•

•

Data length 


Notation 
Description

special characters 


Special characters are any non-numeric or non-alphabetic characters (for example, 
@, #, &, and $), including spaces. 


The data encoding conventions have been adapted for all Mastercard Network messages as 
follows: 


• 
The system aligns all message data element fields on byte boundaries; for example, a data 
field cannot begin with the low order nibble or any bit other than the high-order bit of any 
byte. 
• 
All data types listed in the data representation table are encoded for transmission between 
the Mastercard Network and processor systems using EBCDIC display character 
representation. 
• 
The ASCII to EBCDIC character set table indicates alpha, numeric, and special characters 
sent to the Mastercard Network. When received, the Mastercard Network passes these 
characters through as they are received. The Extended ASCII Character Sets table presents 
the mapping of decimal to hexadecimal character sets when received by the Mastercard 
Network. Any characters not shown in the tables are mapped as a space. 
• 
All numeric (attribute n) data elements are right-justified with leading zeros unless otherwise 
specified in the individual data element definitions. All other data elements are left-justified 
with trailing blanks unless otherwise specified. 
• 
All Track-2 or Track-3 (attribute ans) data elements are encoded as EBCDIC representations 
of the hexadecimal data specified in ISO specification 7811 and 7812. Thus, a hex D (binary 
1101) is encoded as an EBCDIC character D, and so on. The LLVAR or LLLVAR length 
specification of each data element specifies the field length in number of bytes. 
• 
The system encodes all length subfields as numeric EBCDIC, right-justified with leading zeros 
unless otherwise specified.

Presence notations indicate if and how data is present. These notations appear in the originator 
(Org), Mastercard Network (Sys), and destination (Dst). 


Mastercard uses these notation codes to indicate how message senders and receivers must 
understand the use of data in a message.

Notation 
Description 


M Mandatory. The data element is required in the message. 


C Conditional. The data element is required in the message if conditions described in 
the accompanying text apply. 


O Optional. The data element is not required, but may be included in the message at 
the message initiator’s option. 


ME 
Mandatory Echo. The data element is required in a response message and must 
contain the same value (echoed) from the original request or advice message. 


CE 
Conditional Echo. The data element is required in a response message if it was 
present in the original request or advice message, and it must contain the same 
value (echoed) from the original message. 


OE 
Optional Echo. The data element is not required in a response message if it was

Bit map information 


Bit map information 


All Mastercard Network messages are variable-length, with a bit map scheme used as the first 
data elements of the message following the Message Type Identifier (MTI) to indicate the 
presence or absence of additional data elements in the message. 


Each bit map is a 64-bit string contained within an eight-byte data element. 


The Mastercard switching systems use a maximum of two-bit maps: a Primary and a Secondary 
Bit Map. Bits set to 1 or 0 in the Primary Bit Map indicate the presence or absence of DE 2 
(Primary Account Number [PAN]) through DE 64 (Message Authentication Code [MAC]). Bits 
set to 1 or 0 in the Secondary Bit Map indicate the presence or absence of DE 66 (Settlement 
Code) through DE 128 (Message Authentication Code [MAC]). 


All bit positions are interpreted from left to right within each bit map. For example, within the 
Primary Bit Map the left-most bit is bit number 1 and the right-most bit is bit number 64. The 
first bit in each bit map is 1 or 0 to indicate the presence or absence of another (immediately 
following) bit map data element. 


Bit number 1 in the Primary Bit Map and bit number 65 in the Secondary Bit Map (that is, the 
first bit in each bit map) have no corresponding data elements; these bits indicate the presence 
or absence of additional bit map data elements in the message. If bit number 1 is 1, it indicates 
that the Secondary Bit Map is present and that selected data elements in the range DE 65 (Bit 
Map, Extended) through DE 128 (Message Authentication Code [MAC]) also are present in the 
message as indicated by bit positions in the Secondary Bit Map. Mastercard currently uses a 
maximum of two-bit maps (Primary and Secondary) in Mastercard Network messages, with a 
maximum number of message data elements ranging from DE 1 (Bit Map, Secondary) through 
DE 128 (Message Authentication Code [MAC]). Consequently, DE 65 (Bit Map, Extended) (the 
first bit in the Secondary Bit Map) must always be 0. 


Each message must contain the Primary Bit Map. The Secondary Bit Map must be included in a 
message only when data elements in the range DE 65 (Bit Map, Extended) through DE 128 
(Message Authentication Code [MAC]) are present in the message.

Optional Issuer Financial Transaction Advice/0220 Service for Partial Approvals 


Issuers may choose to receive a Financial Transaction Advice/0220, System-generated message 
when the settlement amount has changed on a partial approval. This service will be particularly 
useful when the issuer responds with a partial approval and the transaction currency and 
settlement currency are the same but the cardholder billing currency is different for a partial 
approval when populating the cardholder billing amount. In this situation, Mastercard then 
adjusts the transaction and settlement amounts in DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) and DE 5 
(Amount, Settlement). Issuers can request to receive this message for partial approval 
transactions by contacting their Global Customer Service representative. 


If the issuer has opted in for the service, Mastercard will send a Financial Transaction Advice/ 
0220, System-generated message to the issuer when the settlement amount has changed due 
to a partial approval.

Application notes 


When a U.S. region Mastercard or Debit Mastercard, including prepaid, issuer receives a Reversal 
Advice/0420 message, the Single Message System requires the issuer to match the reversal to a 
previous Financial Transaction Request/0200 or Financial Transaction Advice/0220 Debit 
Mastercard force post message and release any applicable hold placed on cardholder funds 
within 60 minutes.

Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: time-out-induced, acquirergenerated 


This is the message layout for the Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: time-out-induced, acquirergenerated 
message. 


For an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: Exception, Time-out-of Financial Transaction Request 
Response/0210 to Acquirer message, also known as an unsolicited message reversal, the data 
elements, and usages are the same as for the Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: time-out induced, 
acquirer-generated message except for DE 15 (Date, Settlement) and DE 63 (Network Data). 
The Single Message System enters this data. 


NOTE: The acquirer should permit no more than five failures of this type before concluding its 
communication is not reaching the Single Message System, and attempting to recover the connection.

respectively) of each data element. The Single Message System interprets the bit map from left 
to right. The left-most bit represents DE 1 in the Primary Bit Map and DE 65 in the Secondary

Application notes 


All bit positions are interpreted from left to right within each bit map; such as within the 
Primary Bit map the left-most bit is DE 1, (Bit Map, Secondary) and the right-most bit is DE 64, 
(Message Authentication Code [MAC]). 


• 
ISO 8583:1987 messages are variable length, with a bit map scheme that indicates the 
presence or absence of additional fields in the message. 
• 
The first bit in each bit map is set to “1” indicating the presence or “0” indicating the absence 
of an additional 64-bit bit map field that immediately follows the preceding bit map field. 
• 
ISO 8583:1987 message format uses a maximum of 2-bit maps: a “Primary” and a 
“Secondary” bit map. 
• 
Bits set to “1” or “0” in the Primary Bit map indicate the presence or absence of DE 2 through 
DE 64. 
• 
Bits set to “1” or “0” in the Secondary Bit map indicate the presence or absence of DE 66 
through DE 128. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
DE 1 (Bit Map, Secondary) 


• 
Bit No. 1 in the Primary Bit Map and Bit 1 in the Secondary Bit Map (such as the first bit in 
each bit map) do not have corresponding data elements. These bits indicate the presence or 
absence of additional bit map fields in the message. 
– 
If bit No. 1 is set to “1”, it indicates that the Secondary Bit Map is present, and selected 
data elements in the DE 66 through DE 128 range are also present in the message (as 
indicated by bit positions in the Secondary Bit Map). 
– 
Bit No. 65 must always be set to “0” because there are no additional bit maps defined 
beyond the Secondary Bit Map in the ISO 8583:1987 message specification. 
• 
All ISO 8583:1987 messages must contain a Primary Bit Map. 
• 
The Secondary Bit Map is only included in a message when data elements in the range DE 66 
through DE 128 are present in the message. 
• 
Although additional bit maps are accommodated in ISO Standard 8583 (such as setting the 
first bit in any bit map to “1” to indicate the presence of a following extended bit map), the 
ISO 8583:1987 implementation uses a maximum of two bit maps (Primary and Secondary), 
with a maximum number of message data elements in the range DE 1 through DE 128. 
Consequently, DE 65 (the first bit in Bit Map, Secondary) must always be set to zero. 
• 
Bits corresponding to mandatory data elements for a specific message type must be set to 
“1” to indicate the presence of the data element in the message. Otherwise, the message will 
be rejected by the Single Message System through the appropriate response message or 
through an Administrative Advice (Reject)/0620 message. 
DE 1 (Bit Map, Secondary) 


DE 1 is a series of 64 bits used to identify the presence or absence of each data element in the 
second segment of a message. 


For example, the second segment of a message is within DE 65 (Bit Map, Extended) through DE 
128 (Message Authentication Code [MAC]). 


• 
Presence is a value of 1. 
• 
Absence is a value of 0.

Application notes 


DE 2 contains the primary account number (PAN) in Authorization/01xx, Financial Transaction/ 
02xx, and Reversal Advice/04xx messages for all PANs up to 19 digits in length. DE 2 may 
contain a subset of this data within Network Management/08xx messages. 


PAN data consists of three primary components: 


• 
Issuer identification number (IIN) 
• 
Individual account identification number 
• 
PAN check digit 
All PANs and card prefixes used in Mastercard Network messages must conform to the 
standard PAN encoding requirements as documented in the ISO 7812 and 7813 specifications.

Application notes 


When the Account Type value processing code in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 
message indicates no account specified, the issuer may specify an Account Type in the Financial 
Transaction Request Response/0210 message. For example, when an acquirer sends processing 
code 010000 (withdrawal, no account specified), the issuer may send a Financial Transaction 
Request Response/0210 message containing processing code 012000 (withdrawal, checking 
account). 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Subfield 3 (Cardholder Account Type [To]) 


Mastercard supports Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages containing DE 3 
(Processing Code), subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code), value 20 (Refund Correction) 
without a PIN. 


The Single Message System allows acquirers to process same-day reversals for Payment 
Transaction (DE 3, subfield 1, [Cardholder Transaction Type Code] has a value of 28, Payment). 
The Single Message System mandates issuers receive the Payment Transaction. 


When the acquirer submits a reversal for a Maestro Europe acquired refund, the Single Message 
System will change the value in DE 3 (Processing Code) from 20 (Refund/Correction) to 00 
(Purchase) and send the issuer a Financial Transaction Advice/0220 force post message. The 
issuer will apply the refund reversal as a debit to the cardholder. The refund reversal will use DE 
60 (Advice Reason Code) with a value 260, Advice Reason Detail code 0092. 


The Single Message System can now support PIN Management transactions for Chip and 
magnetic stripe cards. 


When used with magnetic stripe cards and DE 22, subfield 1 = 02 or 90, then DE 3 can only use 
a value of 92 (PIN Change) because the Single Message System does not allow PIN Unblock 
with magnetic stripe cards. 


When the Single Message System receives and successfully processes PIN Management 
transactions, issuers will return the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message that 
includes DE 39, value of 85. 


Mastercard supports Debit Mastercard and Maestro Cash Back without Purchase for India 
intracountry transactions. Mastercard will identify India intracountry Cash Back without 
Purchase transactions in Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages that include DE 3, 
subfield 1, value 09 and an acquiring and issuing country code of India (356). 


Acquirers can use DE 3, subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code), value 09 (Purchase with 
Cash Back) for healthcare-related transactions with PIN if the issuer participates in the optional 
unrestricted purse service. 


Acquirers and prepaid card issuers in the U.S. region must support the POS balance inquiry 
transaction type and functionality for all prepaid Mastercard credit, Debit Mastercard, and 
Maestro card account ranges. 


If the Issuer doesn't support Processing Code 17, Single Message System will switch the 
processing code to 010000. 


Passing account information in processing code 


The bridging path is the Mastercard process to pass account information in DE 3 (Processing 
Code), subfield 2 (Cardholder Account Type [From], and subfield 3 (Cardholder Account Type 
[To]) on transactions acquired on the Dual Message Authorization System and bridged to the 
Single Message System.

• 
Debit Mastercard transactions for issuers connected to the Single Message System. 
• 
Transactions with Maestro cards acquired in the Europe region and issued outside of the 
Europe region. 
Currently, Mastercard will begin passing the information when receiving value 10 (Savings 
Account) or 20 (Checking Account) in DE 3, subfield 2, or subfield 3. Otherwise, Mastercard will 
pass the value 00 (No account specified). 


Although this change does not affect the specifications of any fields or messages on either 
system, issuers must be able to support these values in: 


• 
Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages. 
• 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages. 
DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) 


DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) is the amount of funds requested by the cardholder in the local 
currency of the acquirer or source location of the transaction. 


In the event that more than one exception is created, the amounts in data elements 4, 5, and 6 
will change to the new completed amount from the first exception. After the first exception, the 
values in these data elements will be different from the original amount.

Application notes 


The acceptor must specify the local currency of the acceptor, that is, the currency used by the 
cardholder and merchant at the point of service, using DE 49 (Currency Code, Transaction). The 
Single Message System refers to this currency as the currency of the acquirer or the currency of 
the transaction at the point of service. 


For a Purchase Amount Only, No Cash Back Allowed transaction, the Single Message System 
will provide the purchase only approval amount to the issuer in the Financial Transaction 
Request Advice/0220 message. 


For Recurring Payment Transactions, when the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message 
contains DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] Data), subfield 4 (POS Cardholder Presence), value 4 
(Standing order/recurring transactions), and DE 61, subfield 7 (POS Transaction Status 
Indicator), value 4 (Preauthorized Request), then DE 4 must contain a value of zero. 


Acquirers that choose to levy an ATM access fee must send both the transaction amount and 
direct charging fee in DE 4 and the direct charging fee amount in DE 28.

Data element definitions and details 
DE 5 (Amount, Settlement) 


The Single Message System will insert this data element into Financial Transaction/02xx and 
Reversal Advice/04xx messages as a currency conversion service under multiple conditions. 


NOTE: Issuers need to be aware that they may see Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages with 
DE 5 with a zero amount, when there is a currency conversion involved which results in a zero amount 
in DE 5 even though the interchange fee is a nonzero amount from the currency conversion. Issuers will 
need to review the Interchange Fee field of the FREC in the 250-byte Batch Data File for details of the 
actual nonzero interchange amount. 


For international Single Message System transactions, issuers must prepare their systems to: 


• 
receive Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message with zero in DE 5 due to currency 
conversion rates, and 
• 
accept the 250–byte Batch Data File containing these types of transactions. The Financial 
Record (FREC) Interchange Fee field will contain the nonzero interchange amount. 
The settlement amount includes the transaction amount plus the Currency Conversion 
Assessment amount, if applicable. 


For multiple currency processing and settlement transactions, the value in DE 5 in an online 


message to the issuer includes the settlement amount plus any applicable fees. 
The system expresses amounts without a decimal separator. For currencies that support 
exponents, users and systems are responsible for placing the decimal separator appropriately. 


Refer to the Quick Reference Booklet for a listing of currencies and their exponents. 
The following table provides examples of decimal separator placement.

DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) 


If the message is an Account Status Inquiry (Payment or Purchase), the Single Message System 
fills DE 5 with zeros in the request and response message as account status inquiries are 
nonfinancial transactions. 


Exception for acquirers 


If the response message from the issuer contains a denial, the Single Message System fills DE 5 
with zeros and inserts into the response message returned to the acquirer. 


If an acquirer-generated message contains a format error, the message that the acquirer 
receives as a result will not contain the settlement amount. 


DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) 


DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) is the transaction amount converted to the cardholder billing 
amount, exclusive of Currency Conversion Assessment. 


In the event that more than one exception is created, the amounts in data elements 4, 5, and 6 
will change to the new completed amount from the first exception. After the first exception, the 
values in these data elements will be different from the original amount.

Application notes 


The issuer must always specify the currency of this data element using DE 51 (Currency Code, 
Cardholder Billing). The Single Message System calculates DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) for 
all issuers. 


The Single Message System calculates the value of DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) based on 
the amount of DE 4 (Amount, Transaction). Then the Single Message System calculates DE 5 
(Amount, Settlement) from the amount in DE 6. 


When this field is present in a message, DE 10 (Conversion Rate, Cardholder Billing), DE 16 
(Date, Conversion), and DE 51 (Currency Code, Cardholder Billing) must also be present. 


For a purchase with cash back transaction, the issuer must provide the purchase only amount in 
DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) of the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message in the issuer's cardholder billing currency. 


For purchase with cash back transactions, the Single Message system will provide the purchase 
only approval amount to the issuer in the Financial Transaction Request Advice/0220 message.

DE 7 (Transmission Date and Time) 


Issuers that support partial approvals can provide a partial approval amount in DE 6 of the 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message that is less than or equal to the original 
transaction amount requested in DE 6 of the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message. 


Issuers that support partial approvals can provide a partial approval amount in DE 6 of the 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message that is greater than, less than, or equal 
to, the original transaction amount requested in DE 6 of the Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 message when DE 18 contains a value of 5542 indicating the cardholder initiated the 
transaction at an Automated Fuel Dispenser (AFD). 


Issuers that have enrolled in the optional Issuer Currency Conversion Rate (ICCR) service or 
Cross-Border Fee Manager (CBFM) service will have their mark-up added to the DE 6 (Amount, 
Cardholder Billing) amount for transactions with currency conversion. The Single Message 
System provides this mark-up amount separately within DE 8 (Amount Cardholder Billing Fee).

DE 7 (Transmission Date and Time) is the date and time that a processing entity transmitted a 
message, expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Application notes 


The UTC timestamp is the date and time that a processor, including the Mastercard Network, 
transmits any message (as opposed to the initiation of an entire transaction), containing this 
data element, to another processor. 


Mastercard recommends that processors do not include the values of this data element as part 
of their message key if they expect this data element to contain the original acquirer 
transmission timestamp. 


If processors want to use the original acquirer timestamp as part of their message key, 
Mastercard recommends that they use DE 12 (Time, Local Transaction) and DE 13 (Date, Local 
Transaction). 


Upon receipt of the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message, with limited exceptions, the 
Single Message System updates DE 7 with its internal time stamp before sending the message 
to the issuer. The issuer may return this time to the Single Message System in the Financial 
Transaction Request Response/0210 message, or the issuer may send its own transmission time 
in the data element. 


When sending the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message to the acquirer, the 
Single Message System reinserts the acquirer's time stamp from the request message in this 
data element.

ICCR optional service 


The Issuer Currency Conversion Rate (ICCR) is an optional issuer service that charges 
cardholders a mark-up called ICCR within DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing), when the 
transaction currency is different from the cardholder billing currency. Mastercard inserts this 
data and sends to the issuer, who provides this mark-up amount separately within DE 8 
(Amount Cardholder Billing Fee). Issuers set the rate for this mark-up by BIN ranges. ICCR 
applies to POS and ATM transactions acquired worldwide. The Mastercard Network does not 
apply ICCR to Payment Transactions DE 3 (Processing Code) value of 28. 


Cross-border fee manager (CBFM) optional service 


The Cross-Border Fee Manager (CBFM) service is the next generation of Issuer Currency 
Conversion Rate (ICCR) and modifies DE 6 and DE 8 in the same manner. CBFM offers far 
greater flexibility in mark-ups issuers can assign. 


For a complete view of CBFM service capabilities, refer to the Cross Border Fee Manager Service 
Program Guide.

Application notes 


The Mastercard Network provides currency conversion as a service for customers that 
participate in international interchange and will supply the conversion rate in this data element. 


When this data element is present in a message, DE 5 (Amount, Settlement), DE 16 (Date, 
Conversion), and DE 50 (Currency Code, Settlement) must also be present. 


DE 9 values 


The format is right-justified with leading zeroes, with the exception of the decimal indicator 
which is the left-most digit. The left-most digit denotes the number of positions that the Single 
Message System moves the decimal separator from the right. The left-most digit must be in the 
range zero to seven. For example, a field value of 76887050 indicates a conversion rate of 
0.6887050. 


Exceptions for acquirers 


If an acquirer-generated message contains a format error, the message that the acquirer 
receives as a result will not contain the conversion rate.

DE 10 (Conversion Rate, Cardholder Billing) is the factor used in the conversion from transaction 
to cardholder billing amount. DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) is multiplied by DE 10 to determine 
DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing).

DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) 


DE 10 values 


The format is right-justified with leading zeroes with the exception of the left-most digit. The 
left-most digit denotes the number of positions that the Mastercard Network moves the 
decimal separator from the right. The left-most digit must be in the range zero to seven. For 
example, a field value of 69972522 is interpreted as a conversion rate of 9.972522.

Application notes 


A number assigned by the originator of the message and echoed in the response to identify a 
specific transaction. A transaction in this context is a message pair, such as a financial 
transaction request and its response, a financial transaction advice and its response, or a 
reversal/adjustment and its response. See the "Maestro Card-not-present transactions" notes 
below for specific DE 11 information related to this type of transaction. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) 


DE 11 cannot contain a value of all zeros, or the Single Message System declines the transaction 
with a format error 30 in DE 39 (Response Code). 


This identifier, DE 11, when combined with other data elements should be unique for each 
transaction that occurs within an originator's day. Each originator must base the day on 
coordinated universal time (UTC). 


To ensure a unique identifier for each transaction message pair, Mastercard recommends 
combining DE 11 with one or more identifiers, such as: 


• 
DE 32 (Acquiring Institution Identification Code). 
• 
DE 33 (Forwarding Institution Identification Code). 
• 
DE 2 (Primary Account Number [PAN]). 
• 
DE 37 (Retrieval Reference Number). 
DE 11 may contain a different value from the original Financial Transaction Request/0200 and 
its Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 when used with either: 


• 
A Financial Transaction Advice/0220 and Financial Transaction Advice Response/230. 
• 
A Reversal Advice/042x and Reversal Advice Response/043x. 
In these message flows, the original trace number (DE 11) from the Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 and its Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 must be contained in DE 
90 (Original Data Elements) subfield 2 (System Trace Audit Number). 


Processors must return the value received in DE 11 of the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 
message or the Reversal Advice/042x and Reversal Advice Response/043x in the Financial 
Transaction Advice Response/0230 or the reversal/adjustment response/043x. 


For Maestro refund transactions (DE 3, subfield 1 = 20), originated from a dual message 
acquirer, DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number), and DE 90 (Original Data Elements) will be 
present in the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 to the issuer, however the values for the trace 
number, transmission date, and time in these data elements may contain all zero values. This is 
due to the rules that do not require an original authorization for a refund transaction acquired 
on the Dual Message System. Issuers can also identify these types of refund transactions with 
the DE 60 (Advice Reason Code) value of 260 0092. The zero values may also apply in the event 
of a reversal of these refund transactions when the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message 
contains DE 3, subfield 1 = 00 (Purchase) and DE 60 = 260 0092. 


Maestro card-not-present transaction 


Acquirers: For transactions with a single preauthorization and one or multiple financial 
completions, acquirers should use the same DE 11 value in all the financial 0220 completion 
advices that was sent in the single preauthorization. When sending a hold cancellation message 
(0420 advice with DE60 equal to 452), the DE11 value should also match the single 
preauthorization. 


For transactions with an original preauthorization plus one or more incremental 
preauthorizations, and one financial completion, while each of the preauthorizations can have a 
different DE11 value, acquirers should use the DE11 value from the most recently approved 
preauthorization in the one financial 0220 completion advice. When sending a hold cancellation 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
DE 12 (Time, Local Transaction) 


message (0420 advice with DE60 equal to 452), the DE11 value should be the same as the 
most recently approved preauthorization. 


NOTE: While the Mastercard Single Message System will accept a DE 11 value in an 0220 completion 
advice that is different from the DE 11 value in its associated preauthorization/incremental 
preauthorization, this could have implications in dispute processing and the T464 250-byte Batch Data 
File/Settlement reconciliation process, if the acquirer uses DE 11 in their matching criteria for these 
business functions. This is why Mastercard strongly recommends acquirers use the guidance provided 
above when assigning a DE 11 value for Maestro card-not-present transactions. 


Issuers: While issuers can opt to receive a new SMS generated DE11 value in transaction 
messages instead of the official DE11 value logged in the Single Message System, Mastercard 
recommends issuers should not take this option. Opting for a new SMS generated DE11 value 
could have implications in the T464 250-byte Batch Data File/Settlement reconciliation process. 
However, this decision is at the issuer’s discretion. 


Enhanced Delivery Option 


In Debit Mastercard Financial Advice/0220 clearing messages, the Mastercard Network 
distinguishes messages depending on whether they originate from the store-and-forward (SAF) 
file through the SAF process or directly from the main processing module, through the Enhanced 
Delivery option. 


The values for the STAN in these cases are: 


• 
999999 Store and Forward. 
• 
999998 Enhanced Delivery.

DE 17 (Date, Capture) 


The Single Message System will always provide DE 16 (Conversion Date) in any request or 
response message sent to either an issuer or an acquirer if either DE 9 (Settlement Conversion 
Rate) or DE 10 (Cardholder Billing Conversion Rate) is present in the message. 


The Mastercard Network includes the conversion date using the effective date from the T057 
file created by the Mastercard Global Clearing Management System (GCMS). 


Exceptions for acquirers 


If an acquirer-generated message contains a format error, the message that the acquirer 
receives as a result will not contain the conversion date unless the original message contained 
DE 16. 


DE 17 (Date, Capture) 


DE 17 (Date, Capture) is the month and day the acquirer processed the transaction data. 


NOTE: The Single Message System does not use this data element.

Application notes 


This data element is a four-digit indicator used to classify a merchant's product or service, 
selected from a standard list of classification codes referred to as acceptor business codes 
(MCCs). The acquirer includes the MCC in Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages and 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220 completion messages. 


Debit Mastercard issuers connected to the Mastercard Network through the Single Message 
System should note that with DE 18 (Merchant Type), value of 5542 (Fuel Dispenser, 
Automated), an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message follows the preauthorization contained 
in the Financial Transaction Request/0200. For a successfully completed transaction, the 
Acquirer Reversal Advise/0420 message will contain the final amount of the transaction and a 
DE 60 (Advice Reason Code), subfield 1 (Advice Reason Code), value of 450, subfield 2 (Advice 
Reason Detail Code), value 0018, subfield 3 (Advice Reason Detail Text Description), value Zero 
dispense/Over dispense card returned, POI failure. 


Debit Mastercard issuers may choose to receive DE 18: 


• 
In Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages to assist in identifying a transaction as an AFD 
completion message. 
• 
In ATM cash transactions. 
Debit Mastercard issuers must contact their Customer Service representative if they choose to 
receive DE 18 in Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages. 


DE 18 values 


Refer to the Quick Reference Booklet for a list of MCCs and transaction category codes (TCCs). 


For ATM cash withdrawals, this data element must contain a value of 6011 (Automated Cash 
Disbursement). For manual cash withdrawals, this data element must contain a value of 6010 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
DE 19 (Acquiring Institution Country Code) 


(Manual Cash Disbursement). In these instances, the Single Message System, unless otherwise 
directed by the issuer's configuration file, removes DE 18 from the message before sending the 
message to the issuer. 


For Mastercard Send Transactions (Funding Transactions, Mastercard Send Payment 
Transactions, and Gaming and Gambling Payments Transactions) the Single Message System 
includes the following MCCs in DE 18: 


• 
For Mastercard Send Payment Transactions, MCC 6536 (Mastercard Send Intracountry), or 
6537 (Mastercard Send Intercountry). 
• 
For Funding Transactions, MCC 4829 (Money Transfer), MCC 6538 (Funding Transactions), 
and MCC 6540 (Funding Transactions). 
• 
For Gaming and Gambling Payments Transactions, MCCs 7800 (Government-owned 
Lottery), 7801 (Internet Gambling, U.S. Region Only), 7802 (Government Licensed 
Horse/Dog Racing, U.S. Region Only), 7994 (Video Game Arcades/Establishments), 7995 
(Gambling Transactions), and 9406 (Government-Owned Lottery, Global, Excluding U.S. 
Region). 
Other MCCs may be supported for Mastercard Send Transactions. For a full list of valid MCCs, 
refer to the Mastercard Move - MoneySend and Funding Transactions Program Standards Addendum 
for Coding Standards. 


Mastercard reserves the right to decline online financial request messages when the acceptor 
business code (MCC) value in the Merchant Type field (DE 18) equals 0000. Acquirers should 
anticipate receiving a format error when a Financial Transaction/02xx message contains a value 
of 0000 in DE 18. 


NOTE: Special conditions apply, such as for the release of hold amounts, for Automated Fuel Dispenser 
(AFD) transactions, identified by a value of 5542 (Fuel Dispenser, Automated), processed by Debit 
Mastercard issuers in the United States and Canada regions. For additional information, refer to the 
Mastercard Rules.

DE 21 (Forwarding Institution Country Code) 


Application notes 


The Mastercard Network retrieves this data from configured data of the issuer and provides it 
back to the acquirer in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 when the acquirer 
uses the Mastercard Enhanced Issuer Identification (EII) service. 


The Mastercard Network requires including DE 20 within any message whenever the associated 
PAN (in DE 2 [Primary Account Number] or DE 34, [Primary Account Number Extended]) is 
present and begins with a 59 prefix. The Mastercard Network does not guarantee PANs 
beginning with a 59 prefix to be unique without the use of this associated Country Code. 


NOTE: DE 20 (PAN Country Code) will not be present in Financial Transaction Advice/0220: Debit 
Mastercard Stand-In messages.

Consider these conditions for these transaction types: 


• 
ATM transactions: 
–

–

• 
ATM terminals that support contactless: 
–
