– 
Issuers should receive values 07x or 91x. 
• 
ATM terminals that are chip capable: 
– 
Subfield 1 (POS Terminal PAN Entry Mode), position 1-2, should contain 05, 79, or 80. 
– 
Issuers should receive values 05x, 79x, or 80x. 
• 
For ATM transactions subfield 2 (POS Terminal PIN Entry Mode), position 3 should contain 1. 
• 
If acquirers submit DE 55 (Integrated Circuit Card [ICC] System-Related Data) in the 
message, then DE 22, subfield 1 must be 05 PAN Auto-Entry, 07 PAN Auto-Entry via 
contactless M/Chip, 09 PAN entry through electronic commerce, including remote chip, or 81 
E-Commerce. If DE 55 is present in the message, then the Single Message System will 
decline the transaction if the acquirers do not include 05, 07, 09, or 81 in subfield 1 of DE 22. 
• 
If an acquirer sends a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message that contains DE 22, 
subfield 1 with a value of 80 and the service code in DE 35, Track 2 Data is not 2xx or 6xx, 
indicating that it is not a chip card transaction, then the Single Message System will modify 
DE 22, subfield 1 to a value of 90 and forward this value to the issuer. For such transactions, 
the Single Message System will notify the acquirer of this downgrade by populating DE 48, 
subelement 74 (Additional Processing Information) in the Financial Request Response/0210 
message where: 
– 
Subfield 1 = 90 (Chip Fallback Transaction Downgrade Process). 
– 
Subfield 2 = C (Completed Successfully).

DE 23 values 


NOTE: DE 23 may also be sent when DE 22 does not equal 05x or 07x. 


Values for acquirers: 


DE 23 must be three positions in the numeric range 000–099. For contact chip or contactless 
chip transactions where DE 22 subfield 1 is 05 or 07 respectively, DE 23 must contain the value 
of the Application PAN Sequence Number (EMV tag 5F34) as personalized on the chip. 
Considering that the Application PAN Sequence Number (EMV tag 5F34) is defined as a onebyte 
numeric value in the EMV specification, the terminal or the acquirer software must convert 
this one-byte numeric value to a three-byte value with leading zeros in DE 23. For example, if 
the value of EMV tag 5F34 on the chip card is 2, then the value of DE 23 is 002. For chip or 
contactless chip transactions, if EMV tag 5F34 is not personalized (not present) on the chip, DE 
23 cannot be present in the authorization message. When DE 23 (Card Sequence Number) is 
present in a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message and the value is not in the range of 
000–099, then the Single Message System forwards the Financial Transaction Request 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
DE 23 (Card Sequence Number) 


Response/0210 where DE 39 = 30 (Format Error) and DE 44 (Additional Response Data) = 023. 
If the account range is registered for the Authentication Indicator Type 1 Service, then DE 23 
should be present. 


Values for issuers: 


The Single Message System does not cross-edit the presence or absence of DE 23 and the value 
in DE 22 (Point-of-Service [POS] Entry Mode) in Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages. 
However, if DE 22 has a value 05 (PAN auto-entry via chip) or 07 (PAN auto-entry via 
contactless M/Chip) and if DE 23 is present in the Financial Transaction Request/0200, DE 23 
contains the card sequence number from the chip. If DE 22 has a value other than 05 or 07 and 
DE 23 is present, then DE 23 may contain wrong information unrelated to the chip transaction. 
Because of the potential for DE 23 to be present in Financial Transaction/02xx messages, chip 
issuers must prepare to receive store-and-forward (SAF) records containing DE 23. Issuers must 
not return DE 23 in a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210. If an issuer does so, 
Mastercard will delete DE 23 before passing the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
to the acquirer. 


Application notes 


DE 23 must be present in all ICC transactions, where DE 22 = 05x or 07x that include EMVcompliant 
ICC system-related data (DE 55) and where the IC card provides the System PAN 
Sequence Number (EMV tag 5F34) of the terminal. 


DE 23 will be present in the Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages if it was present in the 
related Financial Transaction Request/0200 or Financial Transaction Advice/0220. 


DE 23 applies to Maestro processing of Visa Debit tokens. 


MDES application note 


The following feature only applies to tokens that use a secure element or cloud token type. 


Note the following regarding usage of DE 23 with the Mastercard Digital Enablement Service 
(MDES): 


• 
Mastercard Digital Enablement Service (MDES) treats DE 23 differently than other 
Mastercard programs and services. 
• 
If present, MDES regards the value coming in from the acquirer in DE 23 as a Token 
Sequence Number, not a Card Sequence Number, and only uses it as part of the overall 
crypto validation process. Mastercard passes the Token Sequence Number through to the 
issuer if the issuer opts to receive it. 
Additional information on MDES is available in the MDES guides available on the Technical 
Resource Center through Mastercard Connect® 
.

Application notes 


This data element may be present in a message whenever the operating rules of a bank card 
product permit an online transaction fee. 


The credit or debit indicator, which is the first position of the data element, applies to the 
message recipient. Within acquirer-generated message types, a D (debit) fee amount indicates 
the fee will be a debit to the message recipient, the issuer, and therefore a credit to the 
message originator, the acquirer. 


For intracountry ATM transaction within Australia, acquirers no longer will receive an ATM 
interchange fee for Australian intracountry transactions. Instead, an acquirer may charge 
another institution's cardholder a direct ATM access fee for Cash Withdrawal, Balance Inquiry, 
PIN Change, and PIN Unblock transactions conducted at its ATM. 


Acquirers that choose to levy an ATM access fee must send both the transaction amount and 
direct charging fee in DE 4 and the direct charging fee amount in DE 28. 


Issuers must receive the original transaction amount and the direct charging fee in DE 4, and 
the direct charging fee amount in DE 28. 


Acquirers can assess fees on cross-border ATM transactions (transactions where the card is 
used at an ATM outside the issuing country). Acquirers must provide the ATM access fee in DE 4 
(Amount, Transaction) and DE 28 (Amount, Transaction Fee) of the Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 message. 


For intracountry ATM transactions within Australia, the Single Message System will not include 
DE 28 in Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 and Financial Transaction Advice 
Response/0230 messages. 


For applicable regions or countries, Mastercard convenience fee program for education and 
government merchants. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
DE 29 (Amount, Settlement Fee) 


For issuers processing purchase with cash back transactions and responding with a response 
code of 87 (purchase only, no cash back), issuers should subtract the value in DE 28 from the 
total amount. If there is a currency conversion involved, issuers must convert the value in DE 28 
using the conversion factor in DE 10 since DE 28 is in the acquirer currency. 


The Single Message System supports the use of DE 28 (Amount, Transaction Fee) to report 
separately the convenience fee amount included in the transaction amount. Issuers must 
represent the combined transaction amount and convenience fee amount in DE 4 (Amount, 
Transaction). 


Issuers must be aware that acquirers may assess a convenience fee to cardholders. 


Debit Mastercard issuers connected to the Single Message System must receive the sum of the 
transaction amount and the convenience fee in DE 4 and the convenience fee amount in DE 28 
in Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages. 


When DE 28 is not provided in a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message, the 
system populates the DE 28 value from the original Financial Transaction Request/0200 
message in the response message before sending to the acquirer. 


DE 28 values 


This data element must contain valid numeric data with an appropriate indicator (C or D) in the 
first character position. 


For acquirers approved to levy ATM and POS transaction fees, this data element must contain 
the fee amount, and acquirers must add this amount to the requested amount contained in DE 
4 (Transaction Amount).

Application notes 


This data element, along with DE 32 (Acquirer ID Code) and DE 2 (PAN), must be present in all 
Financial Transaction/02xx, and Reversal/04xx messages. These three data elements must be 
properly encoded to ensure accurate routing for the original transaction and any subsequent 
reversals, chargebacks, adjustments, or representments. 


Debit Mastercard issuers will receive Financial Transaction/02xx messages with values for 
Processor ID in addition to 084 to indicate Debit Mastercard in DE 33. 


Debit Mastercard issuers will continue to receive only Processor ID value 084 to indicate Debit 
Mastercard in DE 33 in Reversal Advice/04xx and Financial Transaction Advice/0220 (Force 
Post) messages.

Data element definitions and details 
DE 34 (Primary Account Number, Extended) 


Debit Mastercard issuers must receive values for Processor ID in Financial Transaction/02xx 
messages that will not equal the Processor ID value in Reversal/04xx and in Financial 
Transaction Advice/0220 (force post) messages. 


DE 33 values 


When present in a message, this data element must contain the processor ID. 


The processor ID is a ten-digit number of the format: 9000xxxxxx, where the Single Message 
System-assigned processor ID will be up to the last six digits xxxxxx. 


This data element must always contain a length value of 10 followed by ten characters of 
numeric data in the associated variable-length data field. 


DE 34 (Primary Account Number, Extended) 


DE 34 (Primary Account Number, Extended) identifies a customer account or relationship. It is 
used only when a PAN is longer than 19 digits in length or contains special characters, and 
therefore cannot be placed into DE 2 (Primary Account Number). 


NOTE: The Single Message System does not use this data element.

and Longitudinal Redundancy Check (LRC) characters.

© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Subfield 8 (Longitudinal Redundancy Check [LRC]) 


Whenever the POS automatically captures Track 2 data, this field must contain whatever is 
encoded on Track 2 of the card, regardless of if the card has been properly encoded with 
information in accordance with ISO specifications. 


For manually keyed Maestro and Debit Mastercard transactions, the Single Message System 
builds DE 35 (Track 2 Data) using DE 2 (Primary Account Number [PAN]) and DE 14 (Expiration 
Date) only when Track 2 is not available and the expiration date is valid. If DE 35, DE 45 and DE 
14 data are not available or invalid, the Single Message System will build or include Track 2 
Data. 


For Debit Mastercard transactions where the acquirer sends DE 45 (Track 1 Data) without DE 
35 (Track 2 Data), the Single Message System builds Track 2 from the PAN, field separator, 
expiration date, service code, and first 13 positions of the discretionary data. 


The Single Message System will not include DE 35 (Track 2 Data) for Maestro point-of-sale 
(POS) transactions unless the acquirer supplies valid DE 35 or DE 14 (Expiration Date) data. 


In addition, the Single Message System includes DE 35 for Debit Mastercard POS transactions 
when the acquirer supplies valid DE 35, DE 45, or DE 14 data. 


The Single Message System will generate DE 35 from other available data, including a generic 
value of 4912 or 0000 for the expiration date, when the original message does not contain the 
following: 


• 
Maestro POS: valid DE 14 or DE 35 data 
• 
Debit Mastercard: valid DE 14, DE 35, or DE 45 data 
For e-commerce requests that do not contain DE 35, the Single Message System builds Track 2 
using DE 2, DE 14 if available, and a Service Code value of 101. E-commerce requests contain 
DE 22 (Point of Service Entry Mode) value of 81x or a value of 05x with DE 48 subelements 40, 
42, and 43 present. 


For chip transactions, DE 35 carries data read from the chip as EMV tag 57 (Track 2 Equivalent 
Data). All ICCs issued by Mastercard customers must support EMV tag 57 (Track 2 Equivalent 
Data). 


For MDES tokenized transactions, issuers may opt in through MDES Manager to receive track 
data in DE 35 (Track 2 Data) on Single Message System transactions. 


Special notes 


The maximum length of the discretionary data is dependent upon the length of the PAN. For 
example, if the PAN has a length of 12 digits, the discretionary data may have a maximum 
length of 17 digits. The overall length of DE 35 cannot be greater than 37 digits. 


The field separator character, (binary 1101), is represented as the EBCDIC character D. 
However, because many ATM and POS devices perform nonstandard character translation while 
reading binary coded decimal (BCD)-encoded magnetic stripe data, the acquirer may also use 
the EBCDIC character = to represent the field separator character in magnetic stripe data 
forwarded to the Single Message System. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Data element definitions and details 
DE 36 (Track 3 Data) 


If the Single Message System must create Track 2 data from Track 1 information, the issuer 
must accept ANY character sent from the acquirer in Track 1 data. 


Track 2 data is not present in the 0220 messages for Maestro non-preauthorization, Maestro 
issuer bound preauthorization completion, or Cirrus transactions. It is present in the issuer 
bound 0220 message for Chip Clearing 0220 messages, if present in the 0220 message from 
the acquirer. 


NOTE: Maestro issuers may request to receive DE 35 in Financial Transaction Advice/0220 completion 
message for a Maestro preauthorization. However, DE 35 will be present only when supplied by the 
acquirer in the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 completion (Maestro 0220 Preauthorization) 
message. 


DE 36 (Track 3 Data) 


DE 36 (Track 3 Data), as represented in the ISO 8583 specification, is the information encoded 
on Track 3 of the card magnetic stripe as defined in ISO 4909:1986. This includes field 
separators, but excludes beginning and ending sentinels and Longitudinal Redundancy Check 
(LRC) characters as defined therein. 


NOTE: The Single Message System does not use this data element. 


DE 37 (Retrieval Reference Number) 


DE 37 (Retrieval Reference Number) is a document reference number supplied by the system 
retaining the original source document of the transaction. Customers may locate a source 
document, or copy of that document, using the value in DE 37.

Application notes 


This data element is reserved for use by the acquiring institution (or an affiliated merchant 
organization) for the purpose of recording a document retrieval reference number. The number 
can be used to locate original cardholder transaction information in subsequent retrieval request 
or any subsequent chargeback action.

must return DE 37. The acquirer should print the retrieval reference number on a customer's 
ATM or POS receipt.

Application notes 


Response codes indicate the disposition of a previous message or indicate approval or denial of a 
transaction. When an issuer or Mastercard declines an authorization, the response code will 
indicate the reason for rejection and may indicate an action the acceptor or POS terminal device 
should take. For example, to capture the card. 


This data element must be present in all response messages. In addition, it will also be present in 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220 Stand-In messages to indicate the DE 39 value provided in 
the response to the original Financial Transaction Request/0200 message. 


For File Update Request Response/0312 messages, the response code will indicate whether the 
system successfully updated the account record or the messages resulted in an error. 


The Mastercard Network will invoke Stand-In Authorization, and may approve the transaction 
for participating issuers if the system detects a format error on incoming Financial Transaction 
Request Response/0210 messages for all brands, regardless of the response code provided by 
the issuer in DE 39. 


In addition, the Mastercard Network will invoke Stand-In Authorization, for issuers that 
subscribe to Stand-In, and may approve the transaction, for all brands if a participating issuer 
responds to a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message with a Financial Transaction 
Request Response/0210 message with one of the following values in DE 39 (Response Code) 
that indicates a system error, the transaction was unable to route, or the issuer is unavailable: 


• 
DE 39, value of 80 (Decline: System not available). 
• 
DE 39, value of 91 (Decline: Destination processor [Customer or INF] not available). 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 and Financial Transaction Advice/0220 response 
codes (excluding Debit Mastercard Stand-In transactions) 


• 
DE 39, value of 92 (Decline: Unable to route transaction). 
• 
DE 39, value of 96 (Decline: System error). 
If the issuer does not respond, then the acquirer will receive a Financial Transaction Request 
Response/0210 message with Response Code 91 (Decline). The issuer will receive an Acquirer 
Reversal/0420 message from the Single Message System with DE 39 =00 and DE 60, Advice 
Reason Code = 402, Advice Reason Detail Code = 0090 (Network advice: issuer timeout error 
not acceptable from acquirer). 


For Cirrus and Maestro transactions only, Mastercard will invoke Stand-In Authorization for 
response code 80 (System not available), and may approve the transaction. 


For Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 or Acquirer Reversal Response/0430 messages, 
the value 10 is not valid for DE 39. The Single Message System will populate a value of 00 
(Approved or completed successfully) in DE 39 for Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 
or Acquirer Reversal Response/0430 messages returned to the acquirer for a partial approval 
transaction. 


The Single Message System declines transactions that contain a value of 85 in DE 39 that are 
not PIN Management or Account Status Inquiry Service requests.

Processing rules 


The Acceptor Terminal ID must be present in all transactions. 


Acceptor Terminal ID must uniquely identify each point-of-sale terminal and ATM terminal at 
the acceptor location. For electronic commerce, phone/mail order, or other card-not-present 
environments, the value must uniquely identify each payment gateway or other device used to 
capture account data to effect a transaction at the acceptor location.

The Single Message System does not require DE 41 for MDES predigitization messages.

Data element definitions and details 
Subfield 1 (Acceptor Name) 


Application notes 


The Single Message System uses this data element to satisfy national regulatory requirements 
concerning merchant identification within Financial Transaction/02xx messages. It is a required 
data element within Financial Transaction Request/0200 and Financial Transaction Advice/ 
0220 messages. 


If DE 43 contains blanks, the Single Message System will decline the transaction with DE 39 
(Response Code), value of 30. DE 44 (Additional Response Data) will indicate that DE 43 is 
blank. 


Issuers may opt in to receive DE 43 (Acceptor Name and Location) in Acquirer and System 
Reversal Advice/0420 messages, and must register and test with Mastercard. Issuers that want 
to participate should contact their Customer Implementation Specialist. 


The following table describes the subfields in DE 43. 


DE 43 values 


Customers must use Country Codes from the Quick Reference Booklet. 


If customers use a country code, it must be the ISO 3-character alphabetic (not numeric) 
Country Code. If used, a State or Province Code should be right-justified in this subfield with one 
leading blank space. 


Delimiter fields must be the blank character. The system requires this because most cardholder 
statement rendering systems in operation today are not designed to perform printer output 
editing or formatting of the acquirer-supplied data contained within DE 43. The acquirer must 
preformat DE 43 exactly as they want it printed on the cardholder's statement. 


Customers must not use all zeros, all low values (binary zeros), or all high values (binary Fs) 
when formatting DE 43. 


Subfield 1 (Acceptor Name) 


DE 43 (Acceptor Name/Location), subfield 1 (Acceptor Name) contains the name of the 
acceptor that should be recognizable by the cardholder and may include other descriptors, such 
as a store number.

Processing rules 


The Acceptor Name must be present for all transactions and contain a valid merchant/ATM 
owner/entity name that is most recognizable to the cardholder. 


The acceptor must place Unique identifiers, invoice numbers, or additional descriptors after the 
merchant, ATM owner, or entity name. 


When a merchant is a part of a chain or franchise, the acceptor must provide the name most 
recognizable to the cardholder at the beginning of the field, followed by a store number or other 
unique identifier for each location. For a chain or franchise issued a Mastercard Assigned ID, all 
submitted transactions must contain the Mastercard Assigned ID data element. 


For any MCC in the 3000-3350 range (Airlines), the acceptor must provide the Abbreviated 
Airline listed in Chapter 3 of the Quick Reference Booklet in positions 1-9 of the field followed by 
the Airline Ticket Number. 


For any MCC in the 3351-3500 range (Automobile/Vehicle Rentals), the acceptor must provide 
the first nine characters of the Description listed in Chapter 3 of the Quick Reference Booklet in 
positions 1-9 of the field and then followed by a unique identifier for each location. 


For any MCC in the 3501-3999 range (Hotels and Motels), the acceptor must provide the first 
nine characters of the Description listed in Chapter 3 of the Quick Reference Booklet in positions 
1-9 of the field and then followed by a unique identifier for each location. 


The acceptor must use the (ISO)/IEC 8859-1:1998 (Latin Alphabet No. 1) character set. 


Program rules 


Payment facilitator-enabled transactions: The acceptor must provide the full or abbreviated 
payment facilitator name, followed by an asterisk, *, and the sponsored merchant name. All 
submitted transactions must contain the Payment Facilitator ID and Sponsored Merchant ID 
submitted in the Additional Merchant data element. 


Staged digital wallet operator: The acceptor must provide the staged digital wallet operator 
name. If issuer authorization for the transaction is occurring at the time of the consumer's 
purchase of products or services, then the acceptor must provide the staged digital wallet 
operator name, followed by an asterisk, *, and the retailer name. If the retailer is identified with 
an MCC in the 3000-3999 range, then the acceptor must provide the appropriate industry MCC 
value, rather than individual retailer MCC, if assigned. 


Installment provider: The acceptor must provide the installment provider name or abbreviated 
name, followed by an asterisk, *, and the retailer name. All submitted transactions must contain 
transaction type identifier (TTI) P10 (Purchase repayment). 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Subfield 2 (Space) 


Business payment service provider (BPSP): The acceptor must provide the BPSP full or 
abbreviated name, followed by an asterisk, *, and the supplier name. All submitted transactions 
must contain the BPSP address, MCC 7399, and transaction type identifier (TTI) P11 (Businessto-
business payment). 


Mastercard® rePower™ transactions must have the value MC repower following the 
merchant/ATM owner/entity name providing the service. 


Payment Transactions must contain the name of the payment provider. The acceptor must 
provide the payee information in the Additional Transaction Reference Data and Mastercard 
Send Receiver Data, data elements. 


Country rules 


Mexico-acquired transactions must contain only: 


• 
Uppercase alpha characters (A-Z) (cannot contain accent characters). 
• 
Numeric characters (0–9). 
• 
Ampersand (&). 
• 
Asterisk (*). 
• 
Space (cannot be the first character or contain more than one space between words).

DE 43, subfield 3 values 


Acceptor City Name must contain the name of the city, town, or village as defined by country 
postal standards. 


For U.S. region transactions, the Acceptor City Name must match the U.S. Postal Service list of 
acceptable cities and spelling by postal code. 


Processing rules 


The Acceptor City Name must be present for all transactions and contain a valid location for the 
acceptor. The location of the acceptor will generally be the physical location where the 
transaction occurred or the business/operations location for transactions that occur virtually. 


Staged digital wallet operator: For funding transactions, the acceptor must provide the staged 
digital wallet operator city name. If issuer authorization for the transaction is occurring at the 
time of the consumer's purchase of products or services, then the acceptor must provide the 
retailer city name. 


Installment provider: The acceptor must provide the installment provider city name. 


Business payment service provider (BPSP): The acceptor must provide the BPSP city name.

Application notes 


This data element may be present in any response message when the Single Message System 
sets DE 39 (Response Code) to 30, indicating that the system detected a Format Error 
condition in the preceding message. The first three bytes of DE 44, if present, will contain a 
three-digit numeric value indicating the ISO data element number where the Single Message 
System encountered the format error.

DE 45 (Track 1 Data) 


DE 45 (Track 1 Data) 


DE 45 (Track 1 Data) is the information encoded on Track 1 of a bankcard magnetic stripe as 
defined in ISO 7813, including field separators. However, this excludes beginning and ending 
sentinels and LRC characters, as defined therein.

Application notes 


Point-of-service applications use DE 45 where the POS terminal equipment reads and transmits 
Track 1 data instead of or in addition to the Track 2 information encoded on the card magnetic 
stripe. 


When the Single Message System receives DE 45 as a part of a financial authorization request 
for Debit Mastercard only, the Single Message System will build DE 35 (Track 2 Data) from DE 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026

Subfield 1 (Start Sentinel) 


45 if valid data is not present in DE 35. The Single Message System also sends DE 45, when 
present. 


If the Single Message System must create any Track 2 data using Track 1 data, the processors 
must prepare to accept any character that would have been present in the Track 1. 


For MDES tokenized transactions, issuers may opt in through MDES Manager to receive track 
data in DE 45 (Track 1 Data) on Single Message System transactions. 


Special notes 


The Single Message System represents the field separator character, binary 1101, as the 
EBCDIC character D. However, because many ATM and POS devices perform nonstandard 
character translation while reading binary coded decimal (BCD)-encoded magnetic stripe data, 
the acceptor may also use the EBCDIC character = to represent the field separator character in 
magnetic stripe data forwarded to the Single Message System.

Application notes 


Mastercard may introduce new DE 48 subelements and subfields between releases to facilitate 
special processing within a country, region, or among pilot participants. Mastercard requires 
customers to be able to successfully process various online messages that may contain new 
unannounced DE 48 subelements and subfields. 


DE 48 and DE 119 contain different subelement definitions. Subelements defined for DE 48 
must be sent in DE 48, not DE 119. 


For information on other uses of DE 48, refer to General message layout information. 


Special notes 


Acquirers and issuers must be able to send and receive all DE 48 subelements. Responding to DE 
48 subelements is conditional, or optional, per individual subelement. 


Responding to DE 48 subelements may depend on brand, purpose of the request, and 
conditional to the individual program or service agreement between the Single Message System 
and the issuer. 


DE 48 encoding scheme 


Mastercard organizes DE 48 into a group of encoded subelements and subfields. 


Transaction category code (TCC) 


If the first character in DE 48 is an alphabetic character, the Single Message System reads that 
character as the transaction category code (TCC). Acquirers should send a TCC = Z for ATM 
transactions if other DE 48 subelements are present or other values for POS transactions as 
defined in the Quick Reference Booklet. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use) 


Refer to the Quick Reference Booklet for other TCC values. 


If the first character in DE 48 (TCC) is not present, missing, or is present and contains a space 
character then the Single Message System processes it as acquirer unprovided. Therefore, 
following the rules below, the Single Message System forwards the message to the issuer with a 
space (hexadecimal 40 in EBCDIC) or a derived TCC value in the first character of DE 48 when 
required. 


Inclusion of the TCC received from the acquirer in DE 48 of the Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 request, into the outbound Financial Transaction Request/0200 message sent by the 
Single Message System to the issuer, adheres to the following rules: 


• 
The Single Message System will send the acquirer-supplied Transaction Category Code in DE 
48 for each non-ATM Financial Transaction Request/0200, Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420, 
and Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message. If the acquirer does not provide a valid 
Transaction Category Code in the non-ATM Financial Transaction Request/0200, Acquirer 
Reversal Advice/0420, and Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages, the Single Message 
System will determine the correct value, and will insert it in the first position of DE 48. 
• 
If DE 48 subelements are present in an ATM Financial Transaction Request/0200, Acquirer 
Reversal Advice/0420, Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message, the Single Message 
System will insert a value of Z in the first position. If there are no other DE 48 subelements 
present in an ATM transaction, the Single Message System does not send the TCC to the 
issuer. 
Cirrus purchases are considered non-ATM transactions; therefore, non-ATM inclusion rules for 
TCC will be applicable for Cirrus transactions. The following tables illustrate the structure of DE 
48 subelements.

Subelement descriptions 


These tables provide formats and descriptions for the subelements in DE 48. The subelement 
sequence does not have to be in the order of ID value. For example, subelement 11 does not 
have to precede subelement 40, which does not have to precede subelement 41, and so on.

DE 48, subelement 07, subfield 02 values 


The clear email address or hashed email address collected during checkout. 


Application notes 


Hashing helps the issuer verify the cardholder's email without the merchant or wallet provider 
providing the full email for privacy and security reasons. 


When the merchant or wallet provider provides a hashed email address, Mastercard receives the 
hash email address and includes it in the data sent to the issuer. The issuer may apply the hash 
to an email address on file for the cardholder and attempt to match it with the hashed email 
address provided by the merchant or wallet provider. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Subfield 02 (Email Address) 


When the hash computed by the issuer matches the hash of the one received from the 
merchant or wallet provider, the comparison with the hash value may be used by the issuer to 
assist in determining the transaction authorization decision. 


The field contains the hash resulting from the following 'emailAddressHash' algorithm, rightpadded 
with spaces. 'emailAddress' is the lower case UTF-8 bytes of the email address. 


The following two functions define the hash algorithm: 


public String emailAddressHash (String emailAddress) {

 String random8Bytes = 123CCB2F30BA420B

 return random8Bytes + leastSignificant24bytes(strongerHash(emailAddress + 

random8Bytes)) 

} 

public String strongerHash (String dataToHash) {

 String currentHash = dataToHash;

 for (int i = 0; i < 5000; i++) {

 currentHash = sha256(currentHash);

 }

 return sha256(sha256(dataToHash) + currentHash); 

} 

NOTE: String random8Bytes = 123CCB2F30BA420B is a fixed value for all merchants and wallet 
providers.

Application notes 


Authentication Service Type 1 applies to designated cards within an account range that are 
participating in the Cardholder Authentication Service and identified by DE 23 (Card Sequence 
Number) value 01x where 1 indicates the participation in the service, and the numeric value in x 
distinguishes among separate cards having the same PAN in DE 2. If the account range is 
registered for Service Type 1, then DE 23 should be present. 


Authentication Service Type 2 applies to all cards within an account range and does not carry a 
special formatting/designation in DE 23.

Data element definitions and details 
Subfield 1 (Fraud Notification Service Date) 


Application notes 


When an issuer sends a First/Second chargeback with the fraud-related reason codes such as 
70 and 74 for Single Message System to Single Message System transactions, and 37, 40, 63 
and 70 for Single Message Debit Mastercard branded transactions, Mastercard applies FNS 
Blocking on each chargeback that exceeds the FNS Date and FNS counter criteria set in the 
system. Mastercard blocks the Chargeback if either or both of: 


• 
The original transaction settlement date is greater than FNS Date from FNS Service reply, 
DE 44, Debit Mastercard Error Code 0249 (FNS Date Exceeded). 
• 
FNS Service reply for FNS Count is greater than FNS counter criteria of 15 counts in 
aggregate for the qualifying fraud-related charge back reason code: DE 44, Debit 
Mastercard Error Code 0250 (FNS Counter Exceeded). 
Accepting or rejecting a reversal chargeback depends on the corresponding original chargeback 
status. If Mastercard accepts the original chargeback, then Mastercard also accepts the 
corresponding reversal chargeback without validating FNS counter and FNS date criteria. If 
Mastercard rejects the original chargeback, then Mastercard rejects the corresponding reversal 
chargeback without validating FNS counter and FNS date criteria. The edit updates the FNS 
date and counter for all Single Message System transactions regardless of the rejecting or 
accepting. 


When the FNS request fails to obtain the FNS date and counter information, the chargeback 
gets accepted and processed. Rather than rejecting, Mastercard accepts and forwards these 
chargebacks. Exceeding FNS criteria and not responding to FNS data on time is rare. The issuer 
receives a notification message through response message when Mastercard applies blocking on 
ineligible chargebacks. For online transactions, Mastercard sends a response through Issuer 
Reversal Advice Response/0432: Exception, system-generated. For Single Message Transaction 
Manager transactions, the Single Message Transaction Manager screen displays the response 
message. 


Mastercard sends subfields 1 and 2 to the acquirer as part of the fraud-related chargeback to 
indicate representment rights to the acquirer. Mastercard sends both of these subfields only on 
or after the second fraud-related chargeback has occurred on the account. 


The acquirer sends Subfield 3 on representments going to the issuer, to let the issuer know they 
are receiving a representment based on the information provided by the Fraud Notification 
System, identified by the value FNS. 


Subfield 1 (Fraud Notification Service Date) 


Subfield 1 contains the date of the second fraud-related chargeback on the account.

Acquirers must be aware that DE 48, subelement 19, subfield 2 (Fraud Notification Service 
Counter) may contain a value of 00 (Unable to perform service). In this case, the acquirer may 
call their Customer Operations Support Representative and request a Fraud Notification Service 
Lookup. The acquirer must provide the Fraud Notification Service data associated with the 
specific chargeback: PAN, Expiration Month, Expiration Year (CCYY), Chargeback Settlement 
Date, and Chargeback Switch Serial Number (if the Chargeback Switch Serial Number is not 
available, then provide the Original Switch Serial Number). Mastercard will provide the correct 
Fraud Notification Service date and counter to the requestor within three to five business days 
of the request for a Fraud Notification Service Lookup.

fraud-related chargeback reason code: DE 44, Debit Mastercard Error Code 0250 (FNS Counter 
Exceeded).

Application notes 


The Message Format Version Code: Acquirer must be present in all transactions and contain a 
valid value. 


AN 6022 Introduction and Standardization of Transaction Data Elements introduced changes to 
the formatting, alignment, and population criteria of acceptor (Merchant/ATM Owner) name, 
location, and related data elements and introduced additional data elements to capture fully 
critical Acceptor data. As there may be varying adoption timelines for upstream acquirer, 
processor, and Merchant/ATM Owner systems, acquirers must use this code to identify the 
standard application at the transaction level. Mastercard will rely on this code to modify, realign, 
and append data into the message format standard defined in AN 6022, allowing downstream 
Mastercard and customer (issuer) systems to operate consistently throughout the transition 
period and avoid any processing or cardholder disruption. 


Value A indicates that the transaction does not comply with the new standards as it contains 
acceptor data in the pre-23Q2 release version format.

Application notes 


The values in DE 48, subelement 23, subfield 1 will contain an indication of the form factor. 
Acquirers may continue to use existing values from 00–19, and the meanings remain unchanged. 


Device type values from 20–99 will exclusively indicate the form factor only without also 
indicating the storage technology. Mastercard subdivides this grouping because the existing 
device type values from 00 to 19, as currently defined, convey a combination of different 
information to specify the physical form factor, such as, wristband, and sometimes, an 
indication of the storage technology, such as Trusted Execution Environment [TEE] or Secure 
Element. With the constant evolution of digital technology, Mastercard anticipates further 
proliferation of new form factors for payments, and new storage technologies. 


Mastercard introduced a distinct storage technology field in DE 48, subelement 33 (PAN 
Mapping File Information), subfield 8 (Storage Technology). Values from 20–33 in anticipation 
of new form factors for payments. Values 34–99 reserved for future use. 


Mastercard will define new values for new types of form factors when introduced into the 
marketplace. Mastercard will not announce these introductions with a release announcement or 
bulletin announcement. New values may start to appear in form factors and will appear in the 
transaction data before official service introduction.

Application notes 


Wallet ID cannot contain all zeros, spaces, or special characters. There is no specified format for 
Wallet ID and can use any combination of numeric or alphanumeric values. 


Mastercard requires the submission of the Wallet ID on Masterpass Wallet transactions or other 
Staged/Pass-through wallets. The Masterpass Wallet sends this Wallet ID that can vary from 
transaction to transaction. While Mastercard initially introduced values 101 and 102, 
Masterpass Wallet may transmit values other than 101 and 102 to the merchant or acquirer. 
Mastercard will not publish these values. Acquirer and processor systems should pass whatever 
value the Masterpass Wallet provides unaltered in the transaction record. 


Mastercard may provide New Wallet Identifier values in this field without prior written notice. 


The following tables indicate the presence of the Wallet Identifier in Masterpass and MDES 
transactions.

Subelement 32 (Mastercard Assigned ID) 


Acquirers use Subelement 32 (Mastercard Assigned ID) to provide unique Mastercard Assigned 
ID (MAID) data. 


Mastercard creates the MAID and provides to merchants for use with the: 


• 
Maestro IIAS Healthcare Program. Mastercard uses the program when merchants submit 
the value, to validate the merchant's certification with SIGIS for IIAS healthcare-related 
transactions. 
NOTE: Exempt merchants under the 90 percent rule must prepare to send the Acquirer ID and 


Member ID in DE 124. 


• 
Maestro Recurring Payments Program. Merchants use the program to identify UCAF e-
commerce transactions without the use of Mastercard Identity Check. Merchants send DE 
48, subelement 32 in a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message along with the static 
AAV UCAF data in DE 48, subelement 43 to validate Maestro Recurring Payments Program 
transactions.

Application notes 


When performing the Contactless PAN Mapping Service, the issuer receives the contactless PAN 
and contactless PAN expiration date in this subelement within financial request/advice/reversal 
messages. The value of P (Contactless Primary Account Number) in DE 48, subelement 33, 
subfield 1 identifies that the PAN within this subelement is a Contactless PAN. The acquirer 
receives the cardholder PAN in financial response messages. The value of M (Primary Account 
Number) in DE 48, subelement 33, subfield 1 identifies that the PAN within this subelement is a 
primary account number. 


When performing the Mastercard In Control Service, the issuer receives the virtual card number 
and virtual card number expiration date in this subelement within financial request/advice/ 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Subelement 33 (PAN Mapping File Information) 


reversal messages. The value of V (Virtual Card Number) in DE 48, subelement 33, subfield 1 
identifies that the PAN within this subelement is a virtual card number (PAN). 


When performing the Mastercard Digital Enablement Service, the issuer receives the token and 
token expiration date in this subelement within financial request/advice/reversal messages: 


• 
The value of C (Mastercard Digital Enablement Service Secure Element Token) or H 
(Mastercard Digital Enablement Service Cloud-Based Payments Token) in DE 48, subelement 
33, subfield 1 identifies that the PAN within this subelement is a token. 
• 
The acquirer receives the cardholder PAN in financial response messages. 
• 
The value of F (Mastercard Digital Enablement Service) is present in DE 48, subelement 33, 
subfield 1. 
• 
The value of M (Primary Account Number) in DE 48, subelement 33, subfield 1 identifies that 
the PAN within this subelement is a primary account number. 
Issuers that issue contactless cards or devices that provide a primary account number (PAN) 
within a transaction different than what is embossed on the card, must provide in Financial 
transaction Request Response/0210 messages when responding to MCC 4111, 4131, 4784, 
and 7523 transactions: 


• 
The value E in DE 48, subelement 33, subfield 1 (Account Number Indicator). 
• 
The embossed number in DE 48, subelement 33, subfield 2 (Account Number). 
• 
The card expiration date of the embossed number in DE 48, subelement 33, subfield 3 
(Expiration Date). 
All Acquirers processing transactions for merchant categories 4111, 4131, 4784, and 7523 must 
pass the PAN Mapping information back to the merchants who requests this information. 


Token-related data element reminder 


Acquirers must prepare to receive DE 48 (Additional Data), subelement 33 (PAN Mapping File 
Information) in: 


• 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 messages. 
• 
Issuers Reversal Advice/0422 messages. 
Acquirers should prepare to receive this data element regardless of the value for a BIN in the 
Mastercard Digital Enablement Service Flag field (position 52) of the 80-byte Financial 
Institution Table (FIT) file.

Subfield 1 (ATC Value) 


Application notes 


The authorization platform inserts the ATC information for all MDES device transactions when 
it is available. Customer should note that ATC information will not be present on declined 
advices. 


Mastercard provides this ATC information in Dual Message Authorization System and Single 
Message Financial Transaction requests and advices to issuers for MDES transactions initiated 
with a device token, when available: 


• 
DE 48, subelement 34, subfield 1 (ATC Value) 
• 
DE 48, subelement 34, subfield 2 (ATC Discrepancy Value) 
• 
DE 48, subelement 34, subfield 3 (ATC Discrepancy Indicator) 
Mastercard does not provide ATC information in declined advices. 


The Single Message System inserts the ATC information for all MDES device transactions when 
it is available. Customer should note that ATC information will not be present on declined 
advices or when Mastercard applies DE 48, subelement 71 (On-behalf Service [OBS]), subfield 1 
(OB Service) value 61 (MDES Cloud-Based Payments Chip Pre-Validation Service/MDES Cloud-
Based Payments Magnetic Stripe Pre-Validation Service).

DE 48, subelement 34, subfield 2 values 


ATC discrepancy value is either or:

when the transaction ATC is above the latest highest ATC.

when the transaction ATC is below the latest highest ATC.

DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 1 values 


The Service Provider ID field must always contain a value assigned by Mastercard. The same 
value must be used in both the Dual Message Authorization System and Dual Message Clearing 
System messages associated with the same transaction. This ID is the Company ID assigned 
during the time of registration with Mastercard for a Service Provider. 


The acquirer must provide the value when involving a registered service provider in a transaction, 
right justified with leading zeros. For example, if the company ID is 123456, DE 48, subelement 
37, subfield 1 should be 00000123456. The seller ID may optionally be present for Staged 
Digital Wallet Operator acquired transactions and must uniquely identify each retailer and its 
location.

DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 2 values 


The Service Provider role must always be a value defined by Mastercard and is the same value in 
both the Dual Message Authorization and Dual Message Clearing systems. 


The acquirer must provide this value when involving a payment facilitator, staged wallet or 
independent sales organization in a transaction, right justified with leading zeros. For example, 
for a payment facilitator, if the company ID is 123456, DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 1 should 
be 00000123456, and subfield 2 should be 90000000001. For an independent sales 
organization, if the company ID is 123456, DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 1 should be 
00000123456, and subfield 2 should be 90000000005.

DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 4 values 


If present, DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 4 must contain a valid ISO numeric country code. 
When territories have a defined country code in Chapter 2 of the Quick Reference Booklet, use 
that country code. 


For example, embassies are physically located in countries that are not their “home country” 
(that is, the embassy of Mexico may be physically located in Singapore; however, the “home 
country” is Mexico). 


Requirements 


DE 48, SE 37, subfield 4 must contain the location information of the government entity, not 
the location of the merchant. 


When providing DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 4, this field must contain a valid three byte ISO 
numeric country code in Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages and Financial 
Transaction Advice/0220 messages.

DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 5 values 


The Merchant Payment Gateway ID is a value assigned by Mastercard. Mastercard assigns the 
Merchant Payment Gateway ID to Merchant Payment Gateway's provider at the time of their 
registration with Mastercard by their acquirer. Merchant Payment Gateway service providers 
wholly owned by the acquirer must use the value 00000999998. If the service provider does not 
use the Merchant Payment Gateway, then use the value 00000999997. The value must be 
right-justified with leading zeros. For example, if the Merchant Payment Gateway ID is 123456, 
then DE 48, subelement 37, subfield 5 contains 00000123456.

Data element definitions and details 
Subelement 41 (Electronic Commerce Certificate Qualifying Information) 


Subelement 41, subfields 1–10, and 12–18 reserved for future use. Subelement 41, subfield 11 
may contain National ID information. 


Citizen's ID for Maestro POS 


For Maestro POS transactions, the Single Message System accepts a Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 message with data present in DE 48 subelement 41 subfield 11 (National ID) 
from participating acquirers. The Single Message System will not log the actual data and only 
recognizes the presence of the data. Issuers have the option of echoing back the data. Citizen's 
ID has no effect on settlement or financial value. This means no changes to adjustment/ 
chargeback processing, no special fees/no intracurrency impact. Citizen's ID does not apply to 
ATM transactions.

Subelement 42 (Electronic Commerce Indicators) 


DE 48, subelement 42 (Electronic Commerce Indicators) for e-commerce purchases, the 
acquirer can send a level of security in DE 48, subelement 42 of the Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 message. Subelement 42 must be present in all financial messages for e-
commerce transactions. When available, Mastercard will provide this information in the 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message, force post messages. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Subelement 42 (Electronic Commerce Indicators) 


DE 48 (Additional Data), subelement 42, subfield 1 (Electronic Commerce Security Level 
Indicator and UCAF Collection Indicator) indicates the electronic commerce security level and 
UCAF collection in positions 1, 2, and 3. 


Mastercard supports the Maestro Recurring Payment Program using the existing values of DE 
48, subelement 42, subfield 1, position 3 (UCAF Collection Indicator), value 3 (merchant 
supports UCAF data collection). 


Mastercard supports value 2 (UCAF data collection supported by merchant) in the UCAF 
Collection Indicator field in DE 48, subelement 42, subfield 1, position 3 for mail/fax order 
transactions to comply with the mandate from the Reserve Bank of India. 


Position 1 of 9 is no longer valid. Mastercard will downgrade any SLI value not starting with 21*, 
22*, and 24* to SLI 210 (nonauthenticated). 


NOTE: In the following, subfield 1 contains valid combinations of positions 1, 2, and 3 for the e-
commerce security level indicator and UCAF Collection Indicator data. The Security Level Code 
consists of values in positions 1 and 2. The Universal Cardholder Authentication Field™ (UCAF) Data 
Status contains a value in position 3.

for acquirer Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 messages.

(Universal Cardholder Authentication Field [UCAF]). 


Mastercard validates or modifies the Security Level Indicator (SLI) value when incorrect for e-
commerce transactions initiated with Mastercard Digital Enablement Service (MDES) tokens. 


Subelement 42 must be present in all Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages for 
electronic commerce transactions. 


For acquirer Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 messages if Security Level Indicator 
[SLI] values have been modified, the data representation is n-19 and the data field is contents 
of subfields 1, 2, and 3.

All acquirers must prepare to receive DE 48, subelement 42, subfields 1, 2, and 3 in the Financial 
Transaction Request Response/0210 message. When Mastercard modifies the subfield 1 value 
originally provided by the acquirer in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message, they will 
receive the modified SLI, the original SLI, and the reason for the modification in subfields 1, 2 
and 3 respectively. Otherwise, they will only receive subfield 1.

(Universal Cardholder Authentication Field [UCAF]). 


DE 48, subelement 42, subfields 2 and 3 are only present in the Financial Transaction Request 
Response/0210 message provided by Mastercard to the acquirer if an SLI downgrade occurred.

Subelement 43 (Universal Cardholder Authentication Field [UCAF]) 


NOTE: Always submit DE 48, subelement 42, subfields 2 and 3 together. 


Subelement 43 (Universal Cardholder Authentication Field [UCAF]) 


DE 48, subelement 43 (Universal Cardholder Authentication Field [UCAF]) contains encoded 
Identity Check issuer or cardholder-generated authentication data collected by the merchant 


from Identity Check. 


This includes fully authenticated or attempt transactions, data for Visa, JCB, Diners Club, or 
American Express transactions associated with the 3-D Secure Electronic Commerce 
Verification Service (if collected), or the static AAV assigned by Mastercard for Maestro 
Recurring Payments Program, or Mastercard Utility Payment Program, or Mastercard Digital 
Secure Remote Payment UCAF data. 


For e-commerce purchases, this subelement can carry UCAF data. This subelement is present 
when a UCAF-enabled merchant has collected authentication data from the cardholder and 
passed it to the acquirer for inclusion in the Financial Transaction Request/0200, or when the 
UCAF data contains a static AAV (Accountholder Authentication Value) assigned by Mastercard. 
This subelement may contain an attempt Accountholder Authentication Value (AAV), as 
evidence that the merchant attempted to authenticate the transaction. 


All Mastercard fully authenticated or attempted transactions require the AAV. Authorizations 
without an AAV or appropriate AAV leading indicator associated with the SLI value will 
downgrade to a nonauthenticated SLI value (48.42) of 210. 


Mastercard accepts e-commerce Payment Transactions that do not contain a cryptogram. DE 
22 (Point of Service Entry Mode), subfield 1 (POS Terminal PAN Entry Mode), value 81 (PAN/ 
Token entry through e-commerce with optional Identity Check-AAV) identifies these tokenized 
e-commerce transactions. DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type 
Code), value 28 (Payment Transaction) that do not contain a cryptogram in this UCAF field, DE 
48, subelement 43, identifies Payment Transactions.

Subelement 48 (Digital Commerce Solutions Indicators) 


NOTE: Mastercard defines control byte kQ for AAV Refresh with SLI = 212, and kF for Attempts Only 
with SLI = 211. Attempts Only indicates that the merchant attempted authentication but the issuer 
and Mastercard Identity Check Smart Authentication Stand-In solution did not perform 
authentication. 


Application notes 


NOTE: Issuers must pass the correct ECI value with the corresponding AAV control byte during 
cardholder authentication. Mastercard EMV 3-D Secure protocol, Identity Check Program Rules, and 
DW Integrity Edits do not allow sending Fully Authenticated AAVs for Attempted Authentications or 
Attempted AAVs for Fully Authenticated Authentications. 


This is an example of a properly coded DE 48, subelement 43 for Mastercard Identity Check for 
Fully Authenticated Authorization including AVS request. 


T420701032124328kBMAAAAAKRIacwR0SdLcB5eBIJjW 


Refer to the Mastercard Identity Check Program Guide and the SPA2 AAV for the Mastercard 
Identity Check Program guide for more information. 


Mastercard supports attempts AAV. The acquirer should forward to Mastercard any attempts 
AAV it receives so that Mastercard can pass to the issuer. 


NOTE: Issuers should not perform Identity Check validation on static AAVs in DE 48, subelement 43 or 
on attempts, Smart Authentication, or Insights AAV generated by Mastercard. 


The UCAF field (DE 48, subelement 43) is a variable length field up to a maximum of 32 
positions. The Mastercard Identity Check AAV is 28 characters in length. There must be no 
trailing spaces in the UCAF field. 


Mastercard will continue to modify the SLI value in Mastercard Digital Enablement Service 
(MDES) transactions based on the AAV contained in DE 48, subelement 43. Therefore, acquirers 
and issuers should expect to see Mastercard Identity Check SLI values in MDES transactions.

Application notes 


Subfield 03 is only present when subfield 01 and subfield 02 are present. 
When a transaction belongs to a single program type, subfield 03 will contain two characters: 


• 
The first character indicates the program type 
• 
The second character indicates the program subtype 
A value of zero in the second character indicates the absence of a subtype. For example, a 
subfield 03 value of 10 indicates the transaction type is Mastercard Merchant Presented QR: 
SRC (SQR) with no subtype. 


For Mastercard QR: X QR and Mastercard QR: Pay by Link program types, two distinct subtypes 
will be applicable: 


• 
A second character value of 1 will specify the subtype as Merchant Presented 
• 
A second character value of 2 will specify the subtype as Consumer Presented 
For example, a subfield 03 value of 61 indicates the transaction type is Mastercard QR: X QR 
and subtype is Merchant Presented. Similarly, a subfield 03 value of 62 indicates the transaction 
type is Mastercard QR: X QR and subtype is Consumer Presented. 


When a transaction belongs to more than one program type: 


• 
Subfield 02 will have a value of 0 (Multi-Program) 
• 
Subfield 03 will have four characters to indicate each type and subtype the transaction 
belongs to

Subfield 04 (Digital Commerce Check-In Details) 


DE 48, subelement 48, subfield 04 (Digital Commerce Check-In Details) is an open text field.

NextGen POI. For an Agent Pay transaction, this field carries Order Intent details. 


This field identifies entity type, entity name and the methods a check-in entity applies to 
validate cardholder presence. All entities eligible for this subfield must be integrated with the 
Mastercard Next Gen POI API.

charges by making it visible in cardholder billing statements, online account tools, mobile apps, 
or other methods designed to inform cardholders of their purchases.

Subfield 1 (Security Services Indicator) 


Application notes 


Mastercard will require all issuing and acquiring processors to code for, support, and integrate 
into their systems the data elements, subelements, and values associated with this item. 


For additional information about the requirement, refer to the Global Safety and Security 
Standards Roadmap. 


NOTE: Mastercard does not require issuers or acquirers to enroll in these optional products and 
services, but they must code their systems to support these fields to use such products and services in 
a timely manner in the event of a security issue. 


The LL length field of LLVAR must be an integral multiple of 6, not to exceed 96.

Merchant Risk Predict 


Merchant Risk Predict provides predictive, real-time, AI-generated merchant fraud detection 
scores to acquirers on single message system transactions. The seven scores sit within the 
authorization message to acquirers and provide feedback on merchant health, compliance, and 
chargeback risks.

Subelement 61 (POS Data, Extended Condition Codes) 


DE 48, subelement 61 (POS Data, Extended Condition Codes) contains values used for three 
different types of transactions: partial approvals, cash back, and healthcare. 


For partial approval transactions, this subelement indicates whether the merchant terminal 
supports the receipt of a partial approval response. 


For purchase with cash back, use this subelement to indicate whether the merchant can 
approve purchase with cash back or amount of purchase only (no cash back allowed) 
transactions. 


For healthcare transactions, this subelement indicates if the:

System (IIAS) database.

• 
Merchant submitted the transaction as IIAS, but is actually a non-IIAS-certified merchant. 
This subelement is conditional in Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages, but if present

Application notes 


This field is only applicable to Debit Mastercard transactions acquired by the Dual Message 
System and issued by the Single Message System. Issuers must use this field to identify the 
authorization type adequately to manage the cardholder balance management and open to buy 
amounts in support of the standards for processing authorizations and preauthorizations. 


Final authorization is an authorization request for an amount greater than zero for a known 
final transaction amount, and not canceling the approved in full transaction authorization 
request. 


Normal authorization or undefined finality is an authorization request for an amount greater 
than zero where the known or not known final amount, and not canceling the approved in full 
transaction authorization request.

Subelement 63 (Trace ID) 


Preauthorization is an authorization request for an estimated amount, with an adjusted 
amount of the original authorization if the final transaction amount is different than the 
original authorization amount requested, or an incomplete transaction for reasons other than 
technical failure or lack of full issuer approval.

Application notes 


Single Message acquirers may use DE 48, subelement 63 (Trace ID) to provide a reference to a 
related Financial Transaction in Single Message System Financial Request/0200 for Mastercard 
Send Payment Transactions. 


For Debit Mastercard authorizations: 


• 
DE 48, subelement 63 contains data from DE 63 (Network Data), subfield 1 (Financial 
Network Code) and subfield 2 (Banknet Reference Number), and DE 15 (Date, Settlement) 
mapped from the Authorization Request/0100 message to a Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 message for issuers on the Single Message System. 
• 
The contents of DE 63, subfield 1, populate network data positions 1-3 in the original 
Financial Transaction Request/0200 message. 
• 
The contents of DE 63, subfield 4 (Banknet Reference Number), populate network data 
positions 4-9 in the original Financial Transaction Request/0200 message. 
• 
Value 01 populates the original message indicator (position 14-15) for original Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 messages. For incremental messages sent for the same 
transaction event, this contains two spaces. For Reversal Transactions, this contains value 
02.

Subelement 66 (Authentication Data) 


For DE 48, subelement 66 (Authentication Data), the acquirer populates and passes to the 
issuer to indicate the Program Protocol used, EMV 3-D Secure Version 1.0 (EMV 3-D Secure 1.0)

participating and have previously authenticated using the Mastercard Identity Check program. 
Do not edit this field to ensure providing these elements on the transaction. If provided by the 
acquirer or processor, it must meet the specifications defined.

Subfield 01 (Sanctions Score) 


Subfield 01 (Sanctions Score) 


DE 48, subelement 67, subfield 1 (Sanctions Score) contains the Sanctions Score populated by 
Mastercard. 


Table 528: DE 48, subelement 67, subfield 1 attributes 


AttributeDescriptionData representationn-3; Numeric, FixedData length representationN/AMinimum data length3Maximum data length3JustificationRight with leading zerosChild fieldsNoRecurring data instancesNo
DE 48, subelement 67, subfield 1 values 


Mastercard has suspended the Mastercard Send Sanctions Scoring Service effective 30 April 
2021. Mastercard will advise Customers should Mastercard reinstate the service. 


For issuers who opt in to the Sanctions Scoring service, Mastercard populates a Sanctions Score 
value on all cross-border Mastercard Send Payment Transactions globally and domestic 
Mastercard Send Payment Transactions in Egypt, Canada, across Europe and the United States. 


The Sanctions Scoring service automatically checks the Sender name (consumer, business, 
government, and nongovernment) against select sanctions watchlists such as the OFAC 
Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN List, and EU List. 


Based on the likelihood of a match of the sender's name to a sanctioned individual or entity, 
Mastercard generates and includes a score of 000 or a score from 070 to 099 in DE 48 
(Additional Data), subelement 67 (Mastercard Send Information), subfield 1 (Sanctions Score) 
of the authorization request message delivered to the issuer. 


A higher score indicates a closer match to names on the applicable screening lists, while lower 
scores indicate a less likely match. When Mastercard cannot determine a score, the value will be 


999. A score of 000 indicates that the transaction passes the Sanctions Scoring check. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Subfield 02 (Sanctions Score Additional Information) 


NOTE: If the Sanctions Score is 100 or if the Sanctions Score produced by the Sanctions Scoring 
service is greater than or equal to the Blocking Score set up by the issuer in the opt-in service, then 
Mastercard declines the authorization request. Mastercard sends an advice to the issuer with the 
value of 33F (Mastercard Send Issuer Blocking, Sanctions Score limit exceeded) in DE 48, subelement 
71 (On-behalf Service [OBS]), subfield 1 (On-behalf [OB] Service Indicator) and subfield 2 (On-behalf 
[OB] Result 1).

the (UCAF) data to validate cardholder identity. AAV uses subelement 71 within the On-behalf 
services program infrastructure to accomplish account holder validation.

rules.

and Gambling Payments Transactions) Blocking Service and Mastercard Merchant Presented 
QR Service will not receive DE 48, subelement 71 in Financial Transaction Advice/0220 (force

Debit Mastercard issuers that participate in the Mastercard In Control Real Card Spend Control

Application notes 


Single Message System issuers receive OBS 50 (Mastercard Digital Enablement Service PAN 
mapping) and corresponding result codes in DE 48, subelement 71 indicating the status of PAN 
mapping for both static and cloud tokenized transactions. 


Issuers receive result code T in DE 48, subelement 71, subfield 3 (On-behalf Result 2) to indicate 
that the acquirer submitted dynamic token validation code (DTVC) and the validation outcome 
in On-Behalf Result 1 pertains to DTVC.

DE 48, subelement 72 values 


When the issuer returns DE 48 (Additional Data), subelement 72 (Issuer Chip Authentication) 
and does not send DE 55 (Integrated Circuit Card System Related Data) in the Financial 
Transaction Request Response/0210 message, Mastercard provides the appropriate DE 55, tag 
91 value in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message to the acquirer, 
matching the approval or decline decision of the issuer. 


As Mastercard provides the appropriate DE 55, tag 91 value in the response message, issuers do 
not need to return DE 48, subelement 72 in their response messages. 


Application notes 


Issuers do not need to return DE 48, subelement 72 in their response messages. 
The LL length field of LLVAR must be between 8–16 positions. 


Subelement 74 (Additional Processing Information) 


Acquirers that support Chip Transaction processing must be able to receive DE 48, subelement 
74 (Additional Processing Information) when there is a chip cryptogram validation problem. 


Issuers that support Chip Transaction processing may include this subelement when there is a 
chip cryptogram validation problem to provide acquirers with additional information.

Application notes 


The Single Message System will add DE 48, subelement 74 to the Financial Transaction Request 
Response/0210 message to the acquirer when the transaction is eligible for the Chip Fallback 
Transaction downgrade. In this scenario, subelement 74, subfield 1 value will be 90 and 
subelement 74 subfield 2 value will be C. 


The LL length field of LLVAR must be an integral multiple of 03, not to exceed 30.

Application notes 


The Single Message System inserts this subelement when performing one of the Fraud Scoring 
Services, or when performing both a Fraud Scoring Service and Fraud Rule Manager Service on 
the transaction. 


NOTE: When Mastercard provides a rule adjusted score in subfield 3, Mastercard provides at least one 
or more rule reason code values in subfields 4–5. However, Mastercard may provide rule reason code 
values in subfields 4 or 5 with, or without, a rule adjusted score in subfield 3. 


NOTE: Issuers participating in a scoring service will receive subfields 1–2. If those issuers choose to 
participate in the Fraud Rule Manager Service, then those issuers must also prepare to receive 
subfields 3–5. 


NOTE: Mastercard will not include DE 48, subelement 75 in Financial Transaction Request/0200 
messages to the issuer when Mastercard is unable to perform the Fraud Scoring service. 


Mastercard Decision Intelligence and Expert Monitoring Services evaluate fraud detection 
elements to produce a score that indicates a level of risk in the transaction. Both services use 
the same DE 48, subelement 75 field with financial transaction messages. Issuers can only enroll 
with one of these services through their Mastercard account representative. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 


Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 



Data element definitions and details 
Subelement 75 (Fraud Scoring Data) 


These optional fraud scoring services provide issuers with a real-time score on single message 
financial transaction messages using predictive modeling technology. 


Expert Monitoring (EMS) generates a fraud detection score that accounts for widespread fraud 
monitoring, fraud rules, and transaction fraud models and profiles. 


Decision Intelligence (DI) generates a transaction decision score that accounts for fraud 
detection elements and integrates them with cardholder segmentation data from Mastercard 
Authorization IQ (CNP transaction attributes are for Dual Message System transactions only.) 


Mastercard Safety Net provides issuers with a second line of defense to limit the impact of a 
large-scale fraud attack on one or more of their payment channels. For example, in ATM or e-
commerce for breached payment systems. The service also identifies when large-scale fraud 
attacks are occurring, using insights from the Mastercard Network, so that the issuer can take 
the appropriate action. It does not replace an issuer's primary fraud prevention system. Issuers 
may alternatively enroll in the Safety Net Alert Only feature. 


When the Safety Net service declines a transaction, issuers will receive a Financial Transaction 
Advice/0220 message containing: 


• 
DE 48, subelement 71, subfield 1 = 18 (Fraud Scoring Service). 
• 
DE 48, subelement 71, subfield 2 = C (Fraud Scoring Service successfully performed). 
• 
DE 48, subelement 75, subfield 1 = 998 or 000. 
• 
DE 48, subelement 75, subfield 2 = NM (Network Monitor). 
• 
DE 60, subfield 1 = 120 (Transaction Blocking). 
• 
DE 121 = 000003 (Decline occurred due to an on-behalf service). 
NOTE: The Single Message System does not use DE 121. However, if the issuer includes DE 121 in a 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message, the Single Message System includes DE 
121 in any subsequent reversal activity. 


Single Message System issuers that do not support Financial Transaction Advice/0220 
messages will use the 250-byte Batch Date File, specifically the Financial Records (FREC) 
report. 


Mastercard includes a score in Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages, and Financial 
Transaction Advice/0220, Debit Mastercard Stand-In messages to the issuer when performing 
the Expert Monitoring, Fraud Scoring Service, or Decision Intelligence on a transaction. Issuers 
may also enroll in Fraud Rule Manager to create rules that may adjust these fraud scores. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Application notes 


If DE 3, subfield 1, contains value 28 (Payment Transaction), then DE 48, subelement 77, must 
be present. 


If DE 3, subfield 1 contains value 00 (Purchase of Goods and Services) and DE 18 contains value 
4829 (Money Transfer), 6540 (Funding Transactions), or 6538 in Funding transactions for 
Mastercard Send (per MoneySend and Funding Transactions Program Standards), then DE 48, 
subelement 77 must be present. 


Mastercard limits the use of value C04 to eligible acquirers and issuers in eligible countries. For 
information about Gaming and Gambling Payment Transactions, refer to the Transaction 
Processing Rules. For information about Gaming Payment Transaction supported everywhere, 
refer to the Mastercard Gaming and Gambling Payments Program Standards. 


Mastercard limits the use of values C07, C52–C60, C64–C65, and F07–F65 to eligible countries 
and eligible acquirers, as described in the Mastercard Move - MoneySend and Funding 
Transactions Program Standards. 


Mastercard limits the use of value C67 to Mastercard Merchant Presented QR transactions. 


Mastercard limits the use of value C68 to Mastercard Merchant Presented QR refund 
transactions. 


Usage of value P11 (Business-to-Business Payment) is intended to identify transactions 
between a buyer and a supplier who does not accept card-based payments, via a Business 
Payment Service Provider who remits the payment to the supplier. 


The Single Message System inserts DE 48, subelement 77 in Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 messages for eligible transactions for values that are Mastercard use only. 


Acquirers must not use Mastercard use only values in DE 48, subelement 77 when submitting 
transactions. These values are reserved exclusively for Mastercard. If an acquirer includes a 
Mastercard use only TTI value, the Single Message System will forward the transaction to the 
issuer without the acquirer-provided value in DE 48, subelement 77.

Application notes 


Mastercard requires all issuing and acquiring processors to code for, support, and integrate into 
their systems the data elements, subelements, and values associated with this item. 


NOTE: Mastercard does not require issuers or acquirers to enroll in these optional products and 
services. But they must code their systems to support these fields to use such product and services in a 
timely manner in the event of a security issue.

Application notes 


Issuers should note that when an acquirer transmits both CVC 1 and CVC 2 data, CVC 1 
processing takes precedence over CVC 2 processing. 


If the CVC 1 value is incorrect, issuers should respond with a value of Y (invalid CVC 1) in 
subelement 87 without validating the CVC 2 value. However, if the CVC 1 value is correct, then 
issuers must validate the CVC 2 and send the appropriate CVC 2 response to the acquirer. 


The issuer must provide subelement 87 in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message whenever the acquirer requests CVC 2 verification. 


Subelement 87 is optional from the issuer in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message whenever DE 45 (Track 1 Data) or DE 35 (Track 2 Data) is present in the Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 message and CVC 1 is invalid. 


The issuer optionally provides, and the Contactless On-behalf Service will provide, subelement 
87 in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message when encountering an issue 
during CVC 3 validation.

provided in the Quick Reference Booklet. 


Customers must not use alpha-currency codes.

This data element is mandatory whenever DE 5 is present in a message. For transactions where

automatically inserts this data element into the message. 


When this field is present in a message, DE 9 (Conversion Rate, Settlement) and DE 16 (Date,

DE 50 values
