Application notes 


When used in Administrative Advice/0620 messages having an Advice Reason Code set to “600” 
(Invalid message; rejected by Network), this data element contains the original (rejected) 
message. 


Issuers use the File Update Request/0302 message to request and update an individual account 
file based on the file name specified in DE 101 (File Name). DE 91 (File Update Code), provides 
the file update action to be taken such as an addition, inquiry, change, or deletion. 


Information required in DE 120 is dependent on the type of the file update requested usually 
depicted by a file name beginning with MCC. DE 120 contains the new, actual file record data 
used in a change or add file update. 


Similar functionality is available using Single Message Transaction Manager.

functionality is available to Debit Mastercard issuers.

When an MCC102 update request is successfully completed, an MDS Stand-In Account 
exception file update will generate automatically for any issuer that participates in the 
Mastercard Stand-In program.

Payment cancellation file MCC105 


Payment Cancellation File MCC105 supports the Mastercard Payment Cancellation for card


not-present and recurring Payment Transactions. 


Participating issuers submit blocking criteria to MCC105 using Issuer File Update Request/0302 


messages or Mastercard Account Management on eService. 


This is valid only for Debit Mastercard cards. Issuers may submit payment cancellation requests 
using the Single Message Transaction Manager under HotCard Facility (click Payment 
Cancellation Service File).

DE 120 Usage for Address Verification Service 


DE 120 is used in authorization requests to contain billing address data for the Mastercard 
Address Verification Service (AVS). 


When the Mastercard Network receives an authorization request with this data present, the 
Dual Message System submits DE 120 within a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to 
the issuing processor and the issuer must respond with the same data in DE 120 that it received 
from the Dual Message System. Mastercard then returns the DE 120 to the acquirer. 


For example: 223 NW 31st Street, Apartment #3, in this case the match is 223.The AVS 
condensed format begins with the left-most position and uses up to five numeric values that 
appear before the first alphabetic character or space. Once AVS finds a space or an alphabetic 
character, it stops interrogating the cardholder billing address, and constructs the condensed 
AVS key. 


The following table describes the Record Data values for DE 120 for the AVS usage.

Subfield 001 (Acceptor Street Address) 


Subfield 001 (Acceptor Street Address) 


DE 122, subelement 001, subfield 001 (Acceptor Street Address) contains the street address of 
the acceptor, which should include the street number, street name, and other identifiers of the 
precise location, such as a building or unit number. 


Table 1140: DE 122, subelement 001, subfield 001 attributes 


Attribute 
Description 
Subfield ID 
001

Contents of subfield 001

Left 


DE 122, subelement 001, subfield 001 values 


Acceptor Street Address must contain all Address Line 1 and Address Line 2 information, 
including 


• 
the name of the street or throughfare 
• 
the locality or community 
• 
the building or house number; and 
• 
any apartment, unit, suite, or floor number, if applicable. 
This information must be populated and formatted as defined by country postal standards. 
DE 122, subelement 001, subfield 001 processing rules 


The Acceptor Street Address must be present for all transactions and contain a valid location 
for the acceptor. The location of the acceptor will generally be the physical location where the 
transaction occurred or business location for transactions that occur virtually. 


If the information for Acceptor Street Address does not exist per country postal standards, then 
the value of “Unavailable” must be provided. 


DE 122, subelement 001, subfield 001 program rules 


Payment facilitator-enabled transactions: The sponsored merchant street address must be 
provided.

Subfield 013 (Acceptor Geographic Coordinates)

Table 1152: DE 122, subelement 001, subfield 013 attributes 


AttributeDescriptionSubfield ID013Subfield Length3Data Representationns...020; LLLVARData FieldContents of subfield 013JustificationN/A
DE 122, subelement 001, subfield 013 values 


Acceptor geographic coordinates, when present, must contain valid latitude and longitude 
values, comma-separated, represented in decimal degrees to five decimal places in positions 
001 through 020 with these format standards: 


• 
Length of geographic coordinates is a range of 15 - 20 positions 
• 
Subfield should not contain alpha characters 
• 
The subfield contains up to two '-' 
• 
The subfield contains precisely two '.' 
• 
The subfield contains precisely one ',' 
• 
At least one numeric position is found before the first '.' 
• 
Five numeric positions are found between the first '.' and ',' 
• 
At least one numeric position is found between ',' and the second '.' 
• 
Five numeric positions are found after the second '.' 
• 
Latitude is greater than or equal to -90.00000 and less than or equal to 90.00000 
• 
Longitude is greater than or equal to -180.00000 and less than or equal to 180.00000 
• 
No space character follows the comma separator

Application notes 


DE 124 enables processors to send private data to each other. Use of DE 124 depends on 
message type and product. The following sections provide a summary of this information. DE 
124 is conditional unless stated as required. 


Customers must select all State, Province, and Country Codes from the Quick Reference Booklet. 


If a country code is used, it must be the ISO 3–character alphabetic (not numeric) Country 
Code. If used, a State or Province Code should be right-justified in this subfield with one leading 
blank space. 


Customers must not use all zeros, all low values (binary zeros), or all high values (binary Fs) 


when formatting DE 124. 


The Single Message System passes anything received in DE 124 from either acquirer or issuer to 
the other-end processor. The Single Message System will include the value in DE 124 received 
from the issuer in its 0210 message back to the acquirer, even if the issuer has declined the 
request. The Single Message System will not pass DE 124 to either processor if a message 
format error exists. 


The Single Message System maintains a configuration record for each processor and uses a field 
in this configuration record to enable a processor to use DE 124. 


Mastercard Send Funding and Payment transactions 


Acquirers and issuers are able to exchange DE 124 data in Mastercard Send (funding, refund, 
and payment), Gaming and Gambling, and MPQR Payment Transaction Financial Transaction 
Request/Response messages. 


NOTE: For Single Message System acquirers and issuers, DE 124 is available in Financial Transaction 
Advice/0220 messages during clearing processing for Debit Mastercard and will contain the same 
information as presented in DE 108 (Additional Transaction Reference Data). 


Funding Transactions at the ATM 


DE 124 is available for processors to send and to receive private business-related data in 
selected messages. For Funding transactions at the ATM, DE 124 is mandatory and contains 
biller information. 


When DE 124 is not present in an acquired Financial Transaction Request/0200 message for 
intracountry transactions sent by the Single Message System to the Dual Message System 
(issued) interface, the transaction is declined with DE 39 (Response Code) containing a value of 
30 (Format Error) and DE 44 (Additional Response Data) containing a value of 124 indicating 
the data element in error. This edit is for non Egypt issuers only. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1036 



Data element definitions and details 
Uses and formats of DE 124 ( Member-Defined Data) 


IIAS healthcare transactions 


To support the Inventory Information Approval System (IIAS) for auto-substantiation of 
healthcare-related transactions (such as FSA, HRA or HSA), merchants exempt from the IIAS 
rules identified as 90 percent merchants must include their Acquirer ID and Merchant ID in DE 
124 when DE 48, subelement 61, subfield 3 (Real-time Substantiation Indicator) is = 2 
(Merchant exempt from IIAS based on IRS 90 percent rule).

Application notes

subfield 3.

DE 124 (Member Defined Data [Mexico rePower Use Only]) 


These layouts are for special usage of DE 124 member-defined data for use in Mexico only. 


Subfields 4–5 are used for Mexico domestic activity for Mastercard rePower. 


Application notes 


DE 124 enables processors to send private data to each other. Use of DE 124 depends on 
message type and product. The following table provides a summary of this information. DE 124 
is conditional unless stated as required. 


DE 124 (Member Defined Data [Mexico rePower Use Only]) specifications for POS 
cash out transactions (without purchase) 


• 
The cash out transaction will be a POS cash back without purchase transaction. 
• 
Acquirers in Mexico operating banking agent services on the Single Message System that 
choose to process cash back without purchase transactions initiated at a POS terminal must 
support the following requirements. 
– 
The Financial Transaction Request /0200 message will contain: 
– 
DE 3 (Processing code), subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code) with value 09 
(Purchase with Cash Back) 
– 
DE 54 (Additional amounts), subfield 2 (Amount Type) with value 40 (Cash Back) 
– 
equal values in DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) and DE 54, subfield 5 (Amount), and 
– 
free-form DE 124 used to pass information to the issuer. 
– 
The cardholder will be authenticated using a PIN number. 
– 
The cash back without purchase transaction must be a Mexico intracountry transaction. 
– 
The acquirer may submit same-day reversals in online exceptions for a cash back without 
purchase transactions.

(Balance Inquiry)

DE 124 (Member Defined Data [Uruguay Domestic Maestro POS 
Transactions Use Only]) 


These layouts are for special usage of DE 124 member-defined data for use in Uruguay. 


Absolute positioning of data in DE 124 subfields is required. Subfields not containing values will 
be populated with spaces when they are followed by subfields that contain values. If one or 
more subfields at the end of the data element do not contain a value, the subfield(s) will not be 
present, and the total length of DE 124 will be reduced by the subfield length(s). 


Example: 00012345678900000027150000000022254101000000048959N 


NOTE: If DE 124 contains more than 51 bytes of data, the data will be truncated.

NOTE: Mastercard recommends that the Merchant Tax ID (subfield 1) be sent by acquirers in all 
transactions with or without government incentivized discount information.

For message type: 


• 
0210: The issuer may echo DE 124 to the Single Message System, send a different DE 124 
value to the Single Message System, send DE 124 to the Single Message System without 
having received DE 124, or not send DE 124 at all. The Single Message System passes any 
value to the acquirer. If the issuer returns no value to the Single Message System, the Single 
Message System does not return DE 124 to the acquirer. 
• 
0220: The acquirer can send a different value in the 0220 message than it received in the 
0210 message. 
• 
0230: If the issuer sends DE 124 in the 0230 message, the Single Message System does not 
pass DE 124 in the 0230 message to the acquirer. 
• 
0430: If the issuer sends DE 124 in an 0430 message, the Single Message System does not 
pass DE 124 in the 0430 message to the acquirer. 
DE 124 is not returned to the Maestro acquirer in the Canada Region. 


DE 125 (New PIN Data) 


DE 125 (New PIN Data) for the PIN change function will be passed in DE 125 (New PIN Data), a 
binary data block containing a derived encrypted value calculated from the new PIN introduced 
by the cardholder at an ATM offering PIN change. 


The Single Message System permits PINs from 4 to 12 characters in length. The encrypted PIN 
block is always 64 bits (8 bytes) in length, regardless of the original PIN length.

Data element definitions and details 
Subfield 1 (Settlement Service Data) 


Application notes 


The Single Message System uses DE 126 (Switch Private Data) to contain Network-generated 
private-use information. This data is composed of a specific Mastercard settlement service 
identifier and network symbolic information used by the application for internal system routing. 
DE 126 also contains the Cross-Border Transaction and Currency Indicators. When this data 
element is received in the online message, it must be returned unchanged in the response 
message from the processor. 


NOTE: All processors are required to accept and return the entire contents of DE 126. 


Subelement encoding scheme 


The overall length of the DE 126 is specified in its first three bytes (the “LLL” portion of the data 
element). The overall length of DE 126 is restricted to 050 bytes to accommodate practical 
operational limitations. Processors must be prepared to receive DE 126 with varying lengths.

DE 126, subfield 1 contains settlement service data.

Application notes 


Any message originator (for example, any customer or INF facility communicating directly with 
the Single Message System) may use this data element to contain private-use data up to a 
maximum length of 100 characters. Data placed in this field is not passed through to the 
message receiver, but is stored temporarily by the Single Message System and returned to the 
message originator in any subsequent response or acknowledgement message. 


Typically, this data element is used by a customer or an INF to contain online transaction 
matching or queuing data that can be accessed readily upon receipt of the corresponding 
response to any originating request or advice message. 


Use of this data element is optional. 


If submitted, this data element can contain new data or data from original Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 or Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message and will 
be included in the following messages: 


• 
Same day Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages to the issuer 
• 
Same day Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 messages to the acquirer 
• 
Same day Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 multiple completion messages to the 
acquirer 
• 
Same day Financial Transaction Advice/0220 multiple completion messages to the issuer 
• 
Non-same day Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages to the issuer from the Single 
Message Transaction Manager 
• 
Non-same day Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 messages to the acquirer from the Single 
Message Transaction Manager 
• 
Non-same day Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages to the Single Message System from 
the acquirer 
• 
Non-same day Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 messages to the Single Message System from 
the issuer 
• 
Non-same day Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages to the issuer from the Single 
Message System during online exception processing 
• 
Non-same day Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 messages to the acquirer from the Single 
Message System during online exception processing 
NOTE: Processor Private Data (DE 127) will not be present in Financial Transaction Advice/0220: 
Debit Mastercard Stand-In messages. 


The Single Message System does not return DE 127 in a Network Management Advice/0820 
message when provided in the Network Management Request Response/0810 message.

Transaction Message Validation 
Error notification 


Overview of system validation or editing 


Mastercard performs data editing on submitted messages to enhance accuracy and data quality. An 
edit focuses on specific transaction components, authentication of messages, or program 
requirements. 


Examples of data conditions edited by the system are: 


• 
Presence of mandatory data in a message (such as PAN) 
• 
Proper formatting of a data element or value (such as ensuring the data is alphabetic or numeric) 
• 
Inclusion of data required for a specific product or program, which may be a validation on a single 
element or across multiple elements 
To enforce compliance, additional validation processes occur outside of system message validations. 
The Data Integrity Program is one example of these processes. Refer to the Data Integrity Monitoring 
Program guide for more details. 


Error notification 


The Single Message System informs customers of message processing edit failures through 
response and advise messages. 


Data elements within these messages indicate in which data element or data element plus 
subelement the error occurred and provide information related to error information.

DE 44 may appear in any response message when DE 39 contains the value 30, which signifies a 
format error condition in the related request message. In such cases, DE 44 will contain either: 


• 
A three-digit number representing only the data element number 
• 
A five-digit number indicating both the data element and the subelement numbers, if the 
data element includes subelements 
The Single Message System uses specific error codes for Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 and 
Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 messages when the response to these messages contains a 
response code of 30 in DE 39, indicating a format error. 


Edit errors best practices 


These best practices help minimize edit errors and provide guidance for addressing them when 
they occur. 


Preventing errors 


To prevent errors: 


• 
Review and analyze all release announcements for new or updated data formatting and 
value requirements. 
• 
Perform as much advance data validation and correction as possible before sending 
messages to Mastercard. This could include verifying the BIN or account range for the PAN, 
country codes, currency codes, or other data. 
• 
Customers using parameter data obtained from Mastercard-supplied tables (such as those 
found in the Mastercard Parameter Extract file) as part of their own transaction data 
validations must use the most recent versions of the tables. 
• 
Follow any field encoding schemes as documented in the Mastercard system specifications. 
This includes: 
– 
Populating fields in supported message types, as specified by the Message Type Indicator 
(MTI) 
– 
Complying with field length and format specifications, such as numeric or alphabetic 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1099 



Transaction Message Validation 
Error numbers and messages 


– 
Constructing subelement ID, subelement length, subfield ID, and subfield length fields in 
accordance with the data element-specific encoding schemes found in the Data element 
definitions and details chapter 
– 
Using the Mastercard-defined field values 
• 
Mastercard strongly recommends using Mastercard simulators to validate new or modified 
processing logic. 
Reacting to errors received 


If you receive an edit error: 


• 
Use the value in DE 44 (Additional Response Data) to determine where the error occurred. 
• 
Look at the specifications for the data element or subelement in error and compare them 
against the data submitted in the field. 
• 
Review the application notes for the data element, which may provide additional information 
on requirements for that field.

in DE 39, the reason for the denial is supplied in DE 44.

Account Status Inquiry Service 


Account Status Inquiry Service 


The ASI service is an optional service that allows merchants to validate that a cardholder 
account is open without negatively affecting a cardholder’s funds availability when establishing 
a recurring or bill payment relationship or validating a card-not-present purchase before 
inventory fulfillment. 


Acquirers may submit an ASI transaction for a Payment Transaction to determine whether an 
issuer will post the specified amount to a particular card account before collecting funds from 
the sender. 


Payment ASI transactions are non-financial transactions. Issuers must not credit the receiving 
cardholder account based on the amount provided in the Payment ASI request. When an issuer 
receives a payment transaction of zero, the issuer should confirm that the recipient’s card 
account exists and can be used in the future for receiving funds. When an issuer receives a 
payment ASI transaction for greater than zero, the issuer should confirm that the amount 
specified does not exceed a prepaid load limit or other types of limits they can have for Payment 
Transactions. When the issuer provides an approval response to the payment ASI for the 
receiving account, the issuer is indicating that it is expecting to approve a subsequent payment 
transaction request message when it is received for the account. 


Customer impact 


The ASI service affects acquirers and issuers. 


Acquirers 


• 
Acquirers that choose to support ASI service transactions must prepare their systems to 
send Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages that contain DE 61 (Point of Service 
[POS] Data), subfield 7 (POS Transaction Status), value 8 (Account Status Inquiry Service) 
and DE 4 (Amount, Transaction), value zero (for Purchase Account Status Inquiry) and value 
zero or an amount greater than zero (for Payment Account Status Inquiry) when submitting 
ASI service transaction requests. 
• 
Acquirers cannot submit transactions with a transaction amount greater than zero for 
account status checks. Acquirers can continue to send USD 1 (or local currency equivalent) or 
less status checks for an automated fuel dispenser (AFD) transaction that include DE 18 
(Merchant Type), value 5542 (Fuel Dispenser Automated) and for aggregated Mastercard 
contactless transit transactions generated by the transit authority. 
• 
Account Status Inquiry Service transactions can include requests for Address Verification 
Service (AVS), CVC 2 validation, or Name Validation. 
• 
The acquirer can receive a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message where DE 
39 (Response Code) will typically contain either the value 05 (Do not honor) or 85 (Not 
declined). 
Issuers 


• 
Issuers must prepare their systems to receive Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages 
that contain DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] Data), subfield 7, value 8, and DE 4 (Amount, 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1113 



System functionality and services 
Account Status Inquiry Service 


Transaction) with a transaction amount of zero (for Purchase Account Status Inquiry) and 
value zero or an amount greater than zero (for Payment Account Status Inquiry) for ASI 
service transaction requests. 


• 
Issuers must validate that the account is open and that the account is not listed in the 
Electronic Warning Bulletin. 
• 
Issuers will receive AVS requests containing DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 
82, value 52 and respond with the appropriate value in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), 
subelement 83 (Address Verification Service Response). 
• 
Issuers will receive CVC 2 requests in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 92 
(CVC 2 Value) and respond with the appropriate value in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private 
Use), subelement 87 (Card Validation Code Result). 
• 
Issuers send the acquirer a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message where DE 
39 (Response Code) can contain either the value 05 or 85. 
• 
Issuers will receive Name Validation requests in DE 108 (Additional Transaction Reference 
Data), subelement 07 (Name Validation Request Data), subfield 01 (Name Validation 
Request) and respond with the appropriate value in DE 108 (Additional Transaction 
Reference Data), subelement 08 (Name Validation Response Data), subfield 01 (Receiver 
Name Validation Response) or subfield 02 (Sender Name Validation Response).

Issuers can provide a response to an inquiry, indicating whether they will accept a subsequent 
Payment Transaction for a particular amount, for a particular account and can identify the 
difference between a purchase ASI transaction and a payment ASI transaction 


No funds are credited to a receiver’s account based on a payment ASI transaction. 


The issuer, at its discretion, send the acquirer an Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message where DE 39 (Response Code) contains either value 00 (Approved or completed 
successfully), 05 (Do not honor), 85 (Not declined), or other valid business decline responses. 
Acquirers should treat any other response as a decline. 


Automated fuel dispenser transactions and Mastercard contactless transit 
transactions 


A Financial Transaction Request/0200 message for an automated fuel dispenser (AFD) 
transaction that includes DE 18 (Merchant Type), value of 5542 (Fuel Dispenser Automated) 
will continue to submit USD 1 (or local currency equivalent) authorization requests. 


Aggregated Mastercard contactless transit transactions generated by the transit authority and 
held for a period before being cleared can continue to submit USD 1 (or local currency 
equivalent) authorization requests. 


Technical description 


The Account Status Inquiry service requires DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] Data), subfield 7 
(POS Transaction Status) to contain value 8 (Account Status Inquiry Service). 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026

System functionality and services 
Payment account status inquiry 


DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) is the amount of funds the cardholder requested in the local 
currency of the acquirer or source location of the transaction. 


For Account Status Inquiry Service transactions: 


• 
When DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] Data), subfield 7 (POS Transaction Status) contains 
value 8 (Account Status Inquiry Service) and DE 3 (Processing Code) contains a value other 
than 28 (Payment) or 00 (Purchase), the Single Message System will decline the transaction 
with DE 39 (Response Code), value 30 (Message format error) and DE 44 (Additional 
Response Data), value 003. 
• 
When DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] Data), subfield 7 contains value 8 and DE 4 (Amount, 
Transaction) contains a value greater than zero and DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1 
(Cardholder Transaction Type Code) contains a value of 00 (Purchase), the Single Message 
System will decline the transaction where DE 39 (Response Code) contains value 30 
(Message format error) and DE 44 (Additional Response Data), value 004 (data element in 
error). 
• 
If the acquirer sends a Reversal Request/0420 message where DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] 
Data), subfield 7 (POS Transaction Status), value 8 (Account Status Inquiry Service), the 
Single Message System sends the acquirer an Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 
message where DE 39 (Response Code) contains value 30 (Message format error). 
The Single Message System supports alternate processing for ASI transactions.

Address Verification Service 


Address Verification Service (AVS) is a fraud deterrent service that provides greater security to 
merchants and cardholders. It helps to protect against fraudulent use of cards by verifying the 
cardholder's billing address. 


Customer impact 


Participation in the Address Verification Service (AVS) is optional for acquirers. Participation is 
required for all issuers in the U.S. and Canada regions. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1118 



System functionality and services 
Address Verification Service 


NOTE: For information about the available AVS indicators, refer to Data element definitions and details 
in this guide. 


Acquirers 


Acquirer participation in AVS is optional. To request AVS, the acquirer provides additional data 
elements in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message. The acquirer must be able to 
receive the AVS response data in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message. 


Issuers 


Participation in AVS is required for all U.S. region issuers. All U.S. region issuers must validate 
addresses when requested in a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message. Issuers will 
respond with a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message. 


Issuers that do not provide a valid AVS response in the Financial Transaction Request Response/ 
0210 message will cause the Single Message System to reject the transaction and send the 
issuer an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 message containingDE 60 (Advice Reason Code) with 
the value 4540000 (Network Advice: invalid data). 


Issuers in the Canada region: 


• 
Must participate in AVS at a processor level via an internal Single Message Transaction 
Manager parameter. For information, customers should contact Customer Implementation 
Services for assistance. 
• 
Will receive Address Verification Service (AVS) data in condensed format in DE 120 (Record 
Data). 
• 
Must support AVS matching: for Automated Fuel Dispenser (AFD) transactions (MCC 5542): 
that recognizes the three numeric digits from Canadian postal codes, plus two trailing zeros 
as a postal code match (for example, L7M 1W9 = 71900) in AVS request indicated by DE 48 
(Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 82 (Address Verification Service Request) = 52 
and address information in DE 120 (Record Data) of Financial Transaction Request/0200 
messages and provide a valid AVS request response in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), 
subelement 83 (Address Verification Service Response). 
Application notes 


Mastercard will require all issuing and acquiring processors to code for, support, and integrate 
into their systems the data elements, subelements, and values associated with AVS. 


NOTE: Mastercard does not require issuers or acquirers to enroll in these optional products and 
services, but they must code their systems to support these fields to leverage such product and 
services in a timely manner in the event of a security issue. 


Message layouts 


The acquirer requests the cardholder billing address verification as part of the Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 message or uses a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message 
only to request address verification. The issuer performs the verification and returns the 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Address Verification Service 


appropriate information to the acquirer in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message. 


If the issuer participates in AVS, Mastercard will provide identifying information in DE 48 
(Additional Data: Private Use), and DE 120 (Record Data) in the Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 message. 


Data element definitions 


DE 48 and DE 120 (Record Data) support AVS. 


DE 48, subelement 82 (Address Verification Service Request) 


Acquirers provide the AVS address verification request option code in DE 48 (Additional Data: 
Private Use), subelement 82 (Address Verification Service Request). 


DE 48, subelement 83 (Address Verification Service Response) 


Issuers respond with DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 83 (Address Verification 
Service Response) and provide it back to the acquirer in the Financial Transaction Request 
Response/0210 message by Mastercard when the acquirer uses the Address Verification 
Service. 


DE 120 


DE 120 (Record Data) is used in financial transaction requests to contain billing address data 
for the Mastercard Address Verification Service (AVS). 


When Mastercard receives a financial transaction request with this data present, Mastercard 
forwards DE 120 within a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the issuing processor 
and the issuer must respond with the same data in DE 120 that it received from Mastercard. 
Mastercard then returns DE 120 to the acquirer. 


During AVS participation setup, issuers can choose from several AVS Service indicators (1–3), 
which is used to verify the cardholder's billing address: 


• 
Service Indicator 1: Full cardholder address 
• 
Service Indicator 2: The first five numerical values of the cardholder address and the full 
cardholder postal or ZIP code 
• 
Service Indicator 3: Up to five numeric values before the first alphabetic character or space in 
the cardholder address, and the full cardholder postal or ZIP code 
In the example, a service indicator 3 has been selected. 


Example using AVS Service Indicator 3: The AVS condensed format begins with the left-most 
position and uses up to five numeric values that appear before the first alphabetic character or 
space. Once AVS finds a space or an alphabetic character, it stops interrogating the cardholder 
billing address and constructs the condensed AVS key. 


For example: 223 NW 31st Street, Apartment #3, in this case, the match is 223.

ATM-Based Programs 


Mastercard offers several optional ATM-based services to acquirers, issuers, and processors 
connected to the Mastercard Network. 


Shared deposit service 


Many financial institutions that accept deposits at their ATMs accept them only from their own 
cardholders. With the Mastercard Shared Deposit service, Cirrus® and Maestro® customers in 
the United States (U.S.) region can choose to accept and to process deposits submitted at 
another customer's ATM within the same state or across states to the extent permitted by 
banking regulations. 


Customer impact 


Shared deposit transactions are allowed if both the acquirer and issuer involved in the 
transaction are signed up with Mastercard™ 
. 


By allowing deposits to be made at a Cirrus® 
ATM, customers can offer a wider range of services 
to their customers. Customers must comply with the Shared Deposit Service rules contained in 
Transaction Processing Rules. 


Acquirers 


When an acquirer sends a shared deposit transaction, the issuer may or may not reject the 
transaction depending on its participation. If the issuer does not participate, the transaction is 
rejected and the acquirer must take corrective action. 


To assist acquirer in determining whether an issuer is participating in the Shared Deposit service, 
the 80-byte Financial Institution Table Data file contains a Deposit Participation flag (position 


72) with a Y (Yes) or N (No) to indicate issuer participation in the optional Shared Deposit 
service.

Shared deposit service 


Issuers 


If an issuer elects to participate in the Shared Deposit service offered by Mastercard™, the issuer 
must designate its Bank Identification Number (BIN) and terminals that participate in any other 
Shared Deposit service for participation in the Mastercard Shared Deposit service. Issuers can 
activate deposits on any or all of their BIN. 


Batch 


Customers participating in the Mastercard™ Shared Deposit service must support the 250-byte 
Batch Data File and the 80-byte Financial Institution Table file. 


The 80-byte Financial Institution Table file contains the associated state code in the State Code 
field. acquirer can use this field to determine whether the issuer is located in a state that allows 
deposits to be completed in the acquirer state. 


In addition, the Deposit Participation flag (position 72) of the Financial Institution Table file will 
contain a Y (Yes) or N (No) to indicate issuer participation in the optional Shared Deposit service. 


For more information about the 250-byte Batch Data File or the Financial Institution Table file, 
refer to Reports and files. 


Reconciliation 


Processors that implement the Shared Deposit service must be able to reconcile with the Daily 
Control report (SWCHD363), Daily Interchange report (SWCHD412), and Exception Audit 
report (SWCHD53).

Adjustment reason code processing 


Mastercard permits acquirers to process adjustments because of deposit errors or returned 
items. Adjustments for deposited items contain DE 60 (Advice Reason Code), subfield 1 (Advice 
Reason Code), value 490 (Adjustment). 


The following DE 60 (Advice Reason Code), subfield 2 (Advice Detail Code) values, support 
deposit errors for adjustment transactions: 


• 
0010: Adjustment 


• 
0024: Empty deposit envelope (deposits only) 
• 
0025: Error in addition (deposits only) 
• 
0026: Error in settlement (deposits only) 
• 
0027: Customer keyed wrong amount (deposits only) 
• 
0028: Non-cash item deposited (deposits only) 
• 
0029: Foreign/Counterfeit currency deposited (deposits only) 
To support returned items, use DE 60 (Advice Reason Code), subfield 2, value 0020 (Returned 
Item), Returned item (documentation via MasterCom is required). 


Mastercard does not permit chargebacks on original transactions. Issuers can process a 
chargeback on the acquirer adjustment if applicable. For these chargebacks, issuers should use a 
DE 60 (Advice Reason Code), subfield 1, value 489 (Chargeback) and DE 60, subfield 2, value 
0030 (Cardholder Disputed Amount). 


Acquirers are allowed to process credit adjustments up to USD 10,000 above the original 
transaction amount for ATM deposit sharing transactions using the Single Message Transaction 
Manager. 


The Single Message Transaction Manager adjustment window contains an additional data field 
for comments to allow acquirers to provide additional information pertaining to the adjustment 
or chargeback. The Exception Audit Report (SWCHD53) also provides additional data.

information for exception items on deposits.

ATM access fee alliance service 


With this service, processors and financial institutions with multiple routing and transit numbers 
have the ability to form ATM access fee alliance groups based on routing and transit numbers 
between acquirers and issuers. 


This enables acquirers and issuers within an alliance group to identify ATM transactions and to 
assess ATM fees appropriately. Issuers will also avoid charging their cardholders surcharge and 
foreign fees for ATM transactions that they should be receiving free-of-charge. 


Single Message Transaction Manager 


To support the ATM access fee alliance service, the Access Fee Group Member field displays on 
the Transaction Processing and Exception Item Processing windows in the Single Message 
Transaction Manager. This field indicates that a transaction participated in the ATM access fee 
alliance service. 


250–byte Batch Data File 


To support the ATM access fee alliance service, acquirers, issuers, and their processors need to 
allow for the field description, Fee Alliance Indicator in the Financial/Non-financial Additional 
Data Addendum Record (ADDR) in the 250–byte Batch Data File. 


The valid values for this indicator are Y for yes, indicating that the transaction participated in 
the ATM access fee alliance service, or Blank if the transaction did not participate in this service. 


Customer impact 


Acquirers and issuers that choose to participate in the ATM access fee alliance service must 
register and follow regular testing procedures.

Balance inquiry 


Mastercard supports several types of balance inquiry requests cardholders can perform. 


Point-of-Sale Balance Inquiry 


This section provides details of how a cardholder can initiate a balance inquiry from a POS 
terminal or using mobile devices. 


• 
DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1, (Cardholder Transaction Type Code) = 30 (Balance 
Inquiry) 
• 
DE 18 (Merchant Type) does not = 6010 or 6011 
Once a customer has identified qualifying transactions, the following editing rules will apply: 
• 
DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) must equal zero 
• 
DE 22 (Point of Service Entry Mode) 
• 
If DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1 = 30 then DE 35 (Track 2 Data) or DE 45 (Track 1 Data) 
must be present must equal 02, 05, 07, 80, 90 or 91 
• 
If DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1 = 30 then DE 41 (Acceptor Terminal ID) and DE 43 
(Acceptor Name and Location) must be present 
If the transaction fails any of the above edits, the Single Message System will return DE 39 
(Response Code) = 30 (Message Format Error). 


NOTE: If an acquirer-generated Reversal Advice/0420 message is sent to obtain a POS Balance Inquiry, 
the transaction will be rejected. 


Acquirers 


Acquirers in the U.S. region must support POS balance inquiry transaction type and 
functionality for all prepaid Mastercard credit, Debit Mastercard, and Maestro card account 
ranges. 


To participate in POS balance inquiries, acquirers must provide DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 
1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code), value 30 (Balance Inquiry) in a Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 message. 


Acquirers in the U.S. region must be able to receive a Financial Transaction Request Response/ 
0210 message containing the balance information in DE 54 (Additional Amounts) and then 
forward that balance information to the merchant. 


Support for POS balance inquiries is optional for acquirers outside the U.S. region.

Balance Inquiry 


When making a purchase at the point of sale, a Debit Mastercard, Maestro, or Mastercard 
prepaid cardholder can initiate a balance inquiry at the point of sale. The issuer responds with 
the amount of funds remaining on the card. 


The POS balance inquiry feature helps the cardholder completely redeem the funds on the 
prepaid card and reduce the potential of a declined authorization request when the purchase 
amount exceeds the funds available on the card. 


Mastercard requires acquirers and prepaid card issuers in the U.S. region to support POS 
balance inquiries for all prepaid Mastercard credit, Debit Mastercard, and Maestro and account 
ranges. 


A merchant in the U.S. region is not required to offer POS balance inquiry, but an acquirer must 
be able to process POS balance inquiry requests for any merchant that wants to offer the 
service. 


Support for POS balance inquiries is optional for both acquirers and issuers outside the U.S. 
region. 


Customer Impact 


Customers can identify POS Balance Inquiry transactions by checking data elements DE 3 
(Processing Code) and DE 18 (Merchant Type) for certain values.

Short-Message-Service Balance Inquiry Service 


Short-Message-Service Balance Inquiry Service 


Mastercard offers a short message service (SMS) balance inquiry service for Debit Mastercard 
issuers and processors in the U.S. region. This service allows cardholders with SMS-enabled 
mobile devices to request and receive balance information on registered cards. 


The SMS balance inquiry service enables Debit Mastercard issuers in the U.S. region to be more 
competitive by providing cardholders with convenient real-time access to balance information 
using mobile devices. 


Customer impact 


Debit Mastercard issuers that participate in the SMS balance inquiry service will receive balance 
inquiries in Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages. SMS Balance Inquiries will be 
identified by the data elements DE 3 (Processing Code), DE 18 (Merchant Type), and DE 22 
(Point of Service Entry Mode). 


• 
DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1, (Cardholder Transaction Type Code) = 30 (Balance 
Inquiry) 
• 
DE 18 (Merchant Type) = 5969 (Mail Order/Telephone Order Providers) 
• 
DE 22 (Point of Service Entry Mode), subfield 1 (POS Terminal Pan Entry Mode) = 81 PAN/ 
Token entry via e-commerce with optional Identity Check-AAV in DE 48 (Additional Data: 
Private Use)), subelement 43 (Universal Cardholder Authentication Field [UCAF]) or DSRP 
cryptogram in DE 104 (Digital Payment Data), subelement 001 (Digital Payment 
Cryptogram). 
NOTE: DE 14 (Date, Expiration) and DE 41 (Acceptor Terminal ID) will be present on SMS Balance 
Inquiries. DE 35 (Track 2 Data) and DE 45 (Track 1 Data) will not be present. 


Debit Mastercard issuers in the United States that want to participate in the SMS Balance 
Inquiry service must: 


• 
Support balance inquiries. 
• 
Register their mobile phone number and bankcard number with Mastercard. Debit 
Mastercard cardholders will initiate balance inquiries via a text message using a SMSenabled 
mobile device. In addition, Debit Mastercard cardholders will receive balance 
information via text messages. 
• 
Sign a contract with Mastercard and complete the Issuer SMS Balance Inquiry Service 
information form 
• 
Support receipt of an e-commerce balance inquiry that includes DE 22 (Point of Service 
Entry Mode), subfield 1, value of 81

Cash back processing 


Cash back processing 


Mastercard supports two types of cash back processing: 


All issuers are required to support the receipt of financial transaction and reversal requests for 
purchase of goods or services with cash back. Issuers can approve or decline purchase of goods 
or services with cash back transactions at their discretion. 


Purchase with cash back 


A purchase with cash back transaction allows consumers to request additional cash at the 
point-of-sale (POS) location when purchasing goods or services. The purchase amount and the 
cash back amount are debited from the consumer’s Maestro or Debit Mastercard account. 


Mastercard offers the option to countries or regions for applying interchange to Purchase with 
Cash Back transactions for Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages that include DE 3 
(Processing Code), subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code), value of 09 (Purchase with 
Cash Back). This option allows different interchange amounts to be applied to the purchase 
amount and to the cash back amount of the transaction. 


NOTE: To see specific interchange information for each country or region, please refer to the 
appropriate regional Interchange Manual. 


Single Message Transaction Manager includes fields to gather information on the purchase and 
cash back amounts. The Single Message Transaction Manager: Transaction Processing, 
Transaction History, Transaction History Lookup, and Adjustment History windows display 
transaction history for Purchase with cash back transactions. 


The replacement cash back value is displayed on the 250-byte Batch Data File. 


In addition, DE 54 (Additional Amounts) is required in Reversal Advice/042x messages that 
include DE 60 (Advice Reason Code) that indicates an exception item, and DE 3 (Processing 
Code), subfield 1, value of 09. DE 54 (Additional Amounts) will represent the replacement 
amount of the cash back portion of the transaction. 


Purchase amount only: no cash back allowed 


Issuers also can approve the purchase amount of a transaction but not the cash back amount 
on the goods or services with cash back transactions. 


Applies to 


This table indicates the products that can be affected by cash back processing, both purchase 
with cash back and purchase amount only, no cash back allowed. 


All issuers are required to accept, but not necessarily approve, the receipt of financial 
transactions and reversal requests for Purchase of Goods or Services with Cash Back 
transactions.

Issuers can approve or decline Purchase of Goods or Services with Cash Back transactions at 
their discretion. 


To participate in Purchase with Cash Back processing: 


• 
Issuers are required to accept DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1, value 09, in Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 and Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages. Issuers also will be 
required to support the value in any exception transactions. 
• 
The issuer should not return balance information in DE 54 (Additional Amounts) in the 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 response message on a purchase with cash 
back transaction. 
• 
Issuers that support online exception item processing must be prepared to generate Issuer 
Reversal Advice/0422 messages for Purchase of Goods or Services with Cash Back 
transactions. 
• 
Issuers initiating a chargeback for the purchase amount, or for a portion of the purchase 
amount, must submit the First Chargeback/1442 message with a Function Code of 453 
(Partial Amount). 
In Purchase Amount Only (no Cash Back Allowed) processing: 


• 
Issuers are required to support the receipt of Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages, 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages, and Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: systemgenerated 
messages containing DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1, value 09. 
• 
Issuers must be able to receive Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages and Financial 
Transaction Advice/0220 messages containing DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), 
subelement 61. 
• 
When an issuer provides a purchase-only approval response to a purchase with cash back 
financial transaction request message, and currency conversion assessment was applied to 
the original request message, the Single Message System will recalculate the settlement 
amount and the currency conversion assessment amounts based on the purchase-only 
amount. Mastercard will send the revised information to the issuer in a Financial Transaction 
Advice (System-generated)/0220 message. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1131 



System functionality and services 
Cash back processing 


• 
If an issuer receives a Financial Transaction Request/0200 message containing DE 48 
(Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 61, subfield 2, value 1, the issuer has the 
following options: 
– 
Approve the entire transaction amount. 
– 
Decline the entire transaction amount. 
– 
Approve the purchase amount only. The issuer must approve the entire purchase amount. 
Partial approval (DE 39 (Response Code), value 10) of the purchase amount is not 
allowed. 
• 
An issuer must provide the following information in a Financial Transaction Request/0210 
message: 
– 
The approved amount (purchase amount) in DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) in the 
issuer’s cardholder billing currency. This amount must be the purchase amount as 
calculated by subtracting the cash back amount in DE 54 (Additional Amounts) from the 
amount present in DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) in the Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 message in the amount data element that corresponds to the issuer’s 
cardholder billing currency. 
– 
DE 39 (Response Code), value 87 (Purchase only, no cash back allowed) 
– 
DE 51 (Currency Code, Cardholder Billing) with the issuer’s cardholder billing currency 
code 
• 
Issuers must be prepared to receive Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages containing DE 
39 (Response Code), value 87 and the purchase only amount in DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) 
and DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing) (additionally, DE 5 (Amount, Settlement) if 
applicable). 
• 
Issuers that approve purchase only transactions must approve the entire purchase amount. 
Partial approval of the purchase amount DE 39 (Response Code), value 10 is not allowed on 
Purchase of Goods or Services with Cash Back transactions.

Alternate processing 


Mastercard allows issuers to define whether the Stand-In Authorization will process cash-back 
transactions based on the card verification method. If the issuer chooses No Stand-In

Accumulation Limit tests apply. When the cash back amount in DE 54, subfield 5 exceeds the 
total amount of cash disbursement allowed, the Authorization System will reject the 
transaction and forward a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 to the acquirer where 
DE 39 contains the value 61 (Exceeds withdrawal amount limit).

Reports 


Support of purchase of goods and services with cash back and purchase amount only, no cash

Chargebacks 


Issuers choosing to process chargebacks on Maestro and Debit Mastercard purchase with cash 
back or purchase amount only, no cash back transactions should follow existing procedures using 
the Single Message Transaction Manager system. 


The amount charged back for both types of cash back transactions should be entered as 
follows: 


• 
Chargebacks on purchase amount only, no cash back: For a chargeback of a net purchase 
only transaction (no cash back) the issuer will put the amount to be charged back in DE 4 
(Amount, Transaction). 
• 
Chargebacks on purchase with cash back (total amounts): For a chargeback on the entire 
transaction amount of a purchase with cash back transaction, the issuer will put the total 
amount of the transaction (purchase plus cash) in DE 4 (Amount, Transaction). The cash 
back portion of the transaction must be identified in DE 54, subfield 5 (Additional Amounts, 
Amount) in the same currency as the transaction amount contained in DE 4. 
Single Message Transaction Manager 


For Purchase with Cash Back exception item processing, the Replacement Amount—Local field 
on the Exception Item Processing pop-up window for Purchase with Cash Back will be a display 
field presenting the total amount of the transaction. 


For Purchase with Cash Back exception item processing, Single Message Transaction Manager 
users will be required to enter on the Exception Item Processing pop-up window for Purchase 
with Cash Back: 


• 
The replacement purchase amount in the New Purchase Amount field 
• 
If the purchase amount is not changing, Single Message Transaction Manager users will enter 
the original purchase amount into the New Purchase Amount field. 
• 
The replacement cash back amount into the New Cash back Amount field 
• 
If the cash back amount is not changing, Single Message Transaction Manager users will 
enter the original cash back amount into the New Cash back Amount field. 
For Purchase with Cash Back transactions, Single Message Transaction Manager users will be 
able to view the cash back amount and purchase amount of the transaction in new fields in the 
Original Amounts box on the Transaction History Lookup window. 


For Purchase with Cash Back adjustments, Single Message Transaction Manager users will be 
able to view the adjustment in the fields in the Adjusted Completion Amount box on the 
Transaction Adjustment History window. 


The optional Financial/Non-financial Fee Addendum Record (FEER) in the 250–byte Batch Data 
File will contain the following fields to support Purchase with Cash Back transactions: Separate 
Interchange Fee Paid and Separate Interchange Fee Paid DR/CR Indicator.

Cross-border transactions 


A cross-border transaction refers to any transaction on a Mastercard credit or debit card 
processed through the Mastercard Network in which the cardholder country code differs from 
the country code of the merchant. 


Identification as cross-border may impact transaction processing and application of certain 
transaction fees. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1143 



System functionality and services 
Currency conversion 


To qualify as a cross-border transaction, the country of the merchant listed in DE 43 (Acceptor 
Name and Location), subfield 5 (Acceptor Country Code) or DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] 
Data), subfield 13 (POS Country Code) will be different from the BIN country. 


If a transaction is identified as cross-border, the transaction currency in DE 49 (Currency Code, 
Transaction) will be compared with the currency (or currencies) of cardholder billing to 
determine whether currency conversion took place. If these values are equal, the Single Message 
System assumes currency conversion did not take place; if the currencies are not the same, 
currency conversion took place. 


Only the following transaction types identified in DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1 qualify for 
cross-border transaction fees: 


• 
00: Purchase 
• 
01: Withdrawal 


• 
09: Purchase with cash back 
• 
17: Cash Disbursement 
• 
21: Deposit 
• 
28: Payment Transaction 
Other transaction types not listed above are still valid Single Message System transaction 
types; however, they will not be subject to cross-border transaction fees. 


In online messages, cross-border transactions will contain values required for cross-border 
acquiring in DE 126 (Switch Private Data), subfield 3 (Cross-Border Transaction Indicator) and 
subfield 4 (Currency Indicator). 


Refer to Data element definitions and details for further details regarding DE 126 (Switch 
Private Data). 


The 250-byte Batch Data File contains the Cross Border Indicator and Currency Indicator in the 
Financial (FREC/Non-Financial (NREC) record and in the Financial/Non-Financial (EREC) record. 


Once the Mastercard Network identifies both the cross-border and the currency indicator flags 
in an online request message, it will send the cross-border transaction indicator, in DE 126 
(Switch Private Data), subfield 3, to the issuer in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 and 
the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages. Mastercard will send the cross-border 
transaction indicator, in DE 126 (Switch Private Data), subfield 3, to the acquirer in the 
Financial Transaction Request Response/0210. Mastercard will also send the cross-border 
indicator in the 250-byte Batch Data File to both issuers and acquirers in the FREC/NREC 
records. Mastercard will assess the cross-border fees based on these values. 


Currency conversion 


Currency conversion is a service that Mastercard performs to convert transaction amounts to 
cardholder billing amounts and reconciliation amounts whenever the transaction currency 
differs from the currency of the cardholder or the settlement currency. 


This process enables customers to: 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1144 



System functionality and services 
Currency conversion 


• 
acquire transactions in multiple currencies and issue cards that are billed in currencies 
preferred by cardholders. For each transaction, Mastercard converts the acquired transaction 
amounts from the transaction currency to the issuer-designated cardholder billing currency. 
• 
settle in currencies that best align with local business practices of acquirers and issuers. 
Mastercard buys and sells currencies to support settlement in multiple currencies for 
customers. Mastercard uses currency conversion rates for calculating acquirer and issuer 
settlement amounts. 
Mastercard guarantees the Mastercard-issued currency conversion rates (refer to definitions 
that follow) for each supported currency for each processing day. 


The following are terms used in this guide.

Amount and currency definitions 


Definitions of cardholder billing amount and transaction amount are as follows: 


• 
Cardholder Billing Amount: The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) name 
for DE 6 (Amount, Cardholder Billing). Although Mastercard adheres to the ISO name for this 
data element, the cardholder billing amount is actually the transaction amount in the 
currency that has been designated as the cardholder billing currency by the issuer. Issuers 
have the relationship with the cardholder and determine the eventual billing to the 
cardholder. 
• 
Transaction Amount: The ISO name for DE 4 (Amount, Transaction), in which Mastercard 
transmits the transaction amount. The transaction amount is in the currency appearing in 
the financial transaction request. 
Rates used for currency conversion 


Except as otherwise provided in the Mastercard Standards, Mastercard will convert all 


transaction amounts processed through the Single Message System into the equivalent 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1145 



System functionality and services 
Currency conversion 


settlement currency amount for settlement. When necessary, Mastercard will convert the 
transaction using the appropriate rates to calculate acquirer settlement, cardholder billing, and 
issuer settlement amounts. 


Mastercard-issued USD rates 


The Mastercard-Issued USD Rates support currency conversion involving currencies that are 
managed against the U.S. dollar. In this case, the U.S. dollar is considered as the reference 
currency. Within this guide and the T057 file, the Rate Class M (value M) description will indicate 
that a Mastercard-Issued USD Rate was used in the currency conversion process (for example, 
to convert from the transaction currency to the cardholder billing and/or reconciliation 
currency). For all Mastercard-Issued USD Rates, the U.S. dollar is the Reference Currency 
whereby the rates are quoted in units of foreign currency per U.S. dollar. 


Mastercard-issued cross rates 


The Mastercard-Issued Cross Rates support currency conversion involving currencies that are 
managed against currencies other than the U.S. dollar. For each cross rate, there is a non-U.S. 
dollar Reference Currency (for example, EUR or GBP) whereby the cross rates are quoted in 
units of foreign currency per Reference Currency. Within this guide and the T057 file, the Rate 
Class F (value F) will indicate that a Mastercard-Issued Cross Rate was used in the currency 
conversion process. 


In addition to enhancing the global capabilities of the Mastercard Network, this rate class aids 
Mastercard in complying with the: 


• 
European Monetary Union (EMU) regulations requiring conversion of currencies transitioning 
to the euro at the fixed rate to the euro that is established by the EMU for the transition 
period and 
• 
other policies as defined from time to time by the monetary authorities in the countries 
where Mastercard does business and Mastercard has been informed of said policies. 


The T057 (production) and T058 (test) bulk files contain the Currency Conversion Rate Detail 
Records; Mastercard-Issued Cross Rates (Rate Class F) and Mastercard-Issued USD Rates (Rate 
Class M). For each Mastercard-Issued Rate, the Reference Currency is indicated in field 3 of the 
T057 and T058 files. 


Mastercard will communicate availability of any new Mastercard-Issued Cross Rates through an 
Operations Bulletin. 


The Single Message System uses the Mastercard-Issued Cross Rates, class record (Rate Class F) 
only, when the source and target currencies for a transaction match the source and Reference 
Currency pair identified in the rate record or T057 Rate File. 


All other currency conversions occur using the Mastercard-Issued USD Rates, class records (Rate 
Class M), for the source currency to the target currency. In cases where the target currency is 
not USD, the source currency is converted to USD and then to the target currency which results 
in a computed cross rate.

Single Message System rounding of calculated amounts 


When the Single Message System performs currency conversion calculations, the interim 
calculations are carried out as far as six positions to the right of the decimal before rounding the 
computed amount. 


When amounts are calculated, the Single Message System uses the currency exponent to 
determine the decimal position. 


• 
If the transaction is in U.S. dollars, the Single Message System rounds the result to have two 
significant digits to the right of the decimal point. 
Example: 17.559048 results in 17.56 


• 
If the transaction is in Tunisian Dinar, the Single Message System rounds the result to have 
three significant digits to the right of the decimal point. 
Example: 17.5330011 results in 17.533 


NOTE: Rounding can occur at multiple times during the lifecycle of the transaction.

Data elements calculated during currency conversion process 


Data elements calculated during currency conversion process 


The Single Message System calculates values for some of data elements for each transaction 
during the currency conversion process to calculate acquirer and issuer settlement amounts and 
cardholder billing amounts. 


Currency conversion for transactions qualifying for regional 


settlement service 


This section provides details and examples related to the currency conversion approach used for 
transactions processed under a regional settlement service. To see a full list of the currencies 
that Mastercard offers for regional settlement, refer to the Settlement Manual. 


Acquirer side data elements 


To calculate the acquirer settlement amount, the Single Message System calculates and uses 
the following data elements: 


• 
Transaction Amount: Each transaction is submitted in a currency agreed upon by a merchant 
and a cardholder. The value of the transaction in the transaction currency is referred to as 
the Transaction Amount. 
• 
Total Acquirer Reconciliation Amount: The Transaction Amount is converted to acquirer 
reconciliation currency using the applicable rate associated with the transaction currency and 
the acquirer reconciliation currency. The Transaction Amount in acquirer reconciliation 
currency is referred to as the Total Acquirer Reconciliation Amount. 
• 
Fixed Interchange Amount: Fixed component of interchange fee applicable for a transaction 
is referred to as Fixed Interchange Amount in fixed interchange amount currency. This portion 
of the interchange fee does not change with the Transaction Amount. The Fixed Interchange 
Amount is converted from fixed interchange currency to acquirer reconciliation currency. 
• 
Variable Interchange Amount: Variable component of interchange fee applicable for a 
transaction is referred to as Variable Interchange Amount. This amount is calculated in 
transaction currency by multiplying the percentage Interchange Rate and the Transaction 
Amount. The calculated Variable Interchange Amount is then converted from transaction 
currency to acquirer reconciliation currency. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1151 



System functionality and services 
Acquirer side data elements 



• 
Total Interchange Amount: Fixed Interchange Amount and Variable Interchange Amount in 
acquirer reconciliation currency are added to calculate Total Interchange Amount in acquirer 
reconciliation currency. 
• 
Acquirer Net Reconciliation Amount: Total Interchange Amount is subtracted/added from 
Total Acquirer Reconciliation Amount to calculate Acquirer Net Reconciliation Amount in 
acquirer reconciliation currency. 
All above mentioned data elements are shown in the Online Messages and the 250-byte Batch

Other acquirer calculation considerations: Computed cross rates and 
fixed interchange 


The examples above illustrated currency conversion when a Mastercard-Issued Rate (USD or 
Cross Rate) is applicable. For transactions where a Mastercard-Issued Rate is not applicable 
(that is, none of the currencies are U.S. dollar or the currency pair is not a Mastercard-Issued 
Cross Rate), the Single Message System will perform currency conversion by going through the 


U.S. dollar and using two Mastercard-Issued Rates to calculate a cross rate (computed cross 
rate). 
First, for transactions where Mastercard offers a regional settlement currency, the cross rate is 
calculated by dividing the currency conversion rate for the transaction currency as published in 
field 9 of the T057 file by the currency conversion rate for the settlement currency as published 
in field 7. For transactions where Mastercard does not offer a regional settlement currency, the 
cross rate is calculated by dividing the currency conversion rate for the transaction currency as 
published in field 8 of the T057 file by the currency conversion rate for the settlement currency 
as published in field 7. 


Regarding fixed interchange, when the fixed interchange currency is different from the acquirer 
settlement currency, the currency conversion process will follow the same process as described 
in the examples above where the fixed interchange amount will be converted as any other 
transaction amount. 


Issuer side data elements 


To calculate the issuer settlement and cardholder billing amounts, the Single Message System 
calculates the following data elements: 


• 
Transaction Amount: Each transaction is conducted in a currency agreed upon by a merchant 
and a cardholder. The value of the transaction in the transaction currency is referred to as 
the Transaction Amount. 
• 
Initial Cardholder Billing Amount: This amount is calculated by converting Transaction 
Amount from transaction currency to cardholder billing currency. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1158 



System functionality and services 
Issuer side data elements 



• 
Currency Conversion Assessment: The Currency Conversion Assessment Rate (CCA Rate) is 
applied to the currency conversion rate to determine the Adjusted Conversion Rate with CCA 
Rate. 
• 
Issuer Currency Conversion Amount: The Cross Border Fee Manager (CBFM) Currency 
Conversion Method (CCM) is applied to the currency conversion rate to determine the 
Adjusted Conversion Rate with CCM. 
• 
Total Cardholder Billing Amount: This is amount is the Cardholder Billing Amount inclusive of 
Cross Border Fee Manager (CBFM) Currency Conversion Method (CCM). 
• 
Initial Issuer Settlement Amount: This amount is calculated by converting Initial Cardholder 
Billing Amount from cardholder billing currency to issuer settlement currency. 
• 
Total Issuer Settlement Amount: This amount is the Initial Issuer Settlement Amount 
inclusive of the Currency Conversion Assessment. 
• 
Fixed Interchange Amount: Fixed component of interchange fee applicable for a transaction 
is referred to as Fixed Interchange Amount in fixed interchange amount currency. This portion 
of the interchange fee does not change with the Transaction Amount. The Fixed Interchange 
Amount is converted from fixed interchange currency to issuer settlement currency. 
• 
Variable Interchange Amount: Variable component of interchange fee applicable for a 
transaction is referred to as Variable Interchange Amount. This amount is calculated in 
transaction currency by multiplying the percentage Interchange Rate and the Transaction 
Amount. The calculated Variable Interchange Amount is then converted from transaction 
currency to issuer settlement currency. 
• 
Total Interchange Amount: Fixed Interchange Amount and Variable Interchange Amount in 
issuer settlement currency are added to calculate Total Interchange Amount in issuer 
settlement currency. 
• 
Issuer Net Settlement Amount: Total Interchange Amount in issuer settlement currency is 
subtracted/added from Total Issuer Settlement Amount to calculate Issuer Net Settlement 
Amount in issuer settlement currency. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Currency conversion for transactions qualifying for intracurrency settlement 


Currency conversion for transactions qualifying for intracurrency 
settlement 


Generally, given the nature of the service, the transactions that are qualified for Intracurrency 
Settlement Service are not subject to currency conversion. In these rare cases where currency 
conversion can be required, the same approach of currency conversion is used as for regional 
settlement service except that under the Intracurrency Settlement Service transaction 
processing, Mastercard-Issued Cross Rates are not applicable. Therefore, for currency 
conversion, purposes only, Mastercard-Issued USD Rates (as published in field 8 of the T057 file) 
are used. 


A transaction qualifies for intracurrency settlement if 


• 
the transaction amount is moved to the settlement amount for both the acquirer and issuer, 
and the currency conversion rate is forced to a value of one 
• 
the transaction amount is multiplied by the variable interchange rate to determine the 
variable interchange amount, and 
• 
the fixed interchange amount is added to the variable amount to determine the total 
interchange amount 
NOTE: 


If the fixed interchange rate is not maintained in a local currency, the fixed interchange rate is 
converted to the fixed interchange rate in settlement currency. 


If the cardholder billing and transaction currency codes are the same, the transaction amount in 
transaction currency equals the Cardholder Billing Amount. 


Refer to Services or products leveraging the system for the regional versus intracurrency selection 
process. 


Single Message System currency conversion for chargebacks 


The Single Message System always uses the current rate when calculating chargebacks 
involving currency conversion. 


For example, if the transaction date used a rate of 2.5, but the current rate is 2.4, the Single 
Message System uses 2.4 when calculating the currency conversion for a chargeback. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1167 



System functionality and services 
Currency conversion for chargebacks submitted on behalf of customers in the U.S. region 


Currency conversion for chargebacks submitted on behalf of 
customers in the U.S. region 


The Single Message System uses the local amount then recalculates settlement amounts using 
current day rates. This happens regardless of the source of the adjustment. 


Currency conversion for chargebacks submitted on behalf of 
customers in regions outside the U.S. region 


When chargebacks are submitted for a customer outside the U.S. region, the chargeback 
amount submitted is in the transaction currency. 


The Single Message System converts the amount to the settlement currency by using the 
current rate. 


Example: 


1. 
U.S. region cardholder makes a purchase in Venezuela 
Currency Code, Transaction: Venezuelan Bolívar 
Currency Code, Cardholder Billing: USD 
Currency Code, Settlement: USD 
2. 
Chargeback submitted by the issuer 
Currency: bolivar fuertes 
Currency conversion for reversals 


This topic describes currency conversion for reversals. 


Same day reversals: The Single Message System uses the same currency conversion rate as the 
original transaction. 


Non-same day reversals (also known as adjustments, chargebacks, and representments): The 
Single Message System uses the current rate for the day that the reversal is processed. 


Enhanced Issuer Identification 


The enhanced issuer identification (EII) service enables acquirers to receive data elements that 
identify the issuer processor on a message-by-message basis. This data will be provided for 
select financial transaction and exception item messages. 


Applies to 


This service is optional for Debit Mastercard, Maestro or Cirrus brands.

System functionality and services 
Enhanced Issuer Identification 


Customer impact 


Participation in enhanced issuer identification is optional for acquirers. Issuers do not need the 
service but should be aware of the process because it will affect financial transaction messages. 


Acquirers 


To participate in Enhanced Issuer Identification processing, acquirers must: 


• 
Contact the Customer Implementation Services (CIS) team. 
• 
Be prepared to receive the following data elements in the Financial Transaction Request 
Response/0210 and the Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 messages to identify issuer 
information: 
– 
DE 20 (Primary Account Number [PAN] Country Code), which will contain the country 
code of where the card issuer is located. 
– 
DE 58 (Authorizing Agent Institution ID), which will contain the issuing processor’s 
financial institution routing and transit number. 
NOTE: DE 58 (Authorizing Agent Institution ID) will be received only in the Financial Transaction 
Request Response/0210 


– 
DE 100 (Receiving Institution Identification Code), which will contain the issuer processor 
ID to identify the receiver of the message. 
Issuers 


Issuers should be aware that if an acquirer participates in enhanced issuer identification (EII), 
the data elements identifying issuer information will be included in Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 and Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages. Issuers must return the data 
elements in Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 and the Acquirer Reversal Advice 
Response/0430 messages.

transaction processing required to support the enhanced issuer identification service.

Data element definitions 


DE 20 (Primary Account Number [PAN] Country Code),DE 58 (Authorizing Agent Institution ID), 
and DE 100 (Receiving Institution Identification Code) support EII. 


DE 20 (Primary Account Number [PAN] Country Code) 


DE 20 (Primary Account Number [PAN] Country Code) contains the country code of where the 
card issuer is located. 


Mastercard retrieves this data from configured data of the issuer and provides it back to the 
acquirer in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message by the Single Message 
System when the acquirer uses the Mastercard Enhanced Issuer Identification (EII) service. 


DE 58 (Authorizing Agent Institution ID) 


DE 58 (Authorizing Agent Institution ID) is the institution identifier of the card issuer. It contains 
the issuing processor’s financial institution routing and transit number. The Single Message 
System retrieves this data from configured data of the issuer and supplies it to the issuer in the 
Financial Transaction Request/0200 message 


DE 100 (Receiving Institution Identification Code) 


DE 100 (Receiving Institution Identification Code) identifies the receiver of the message. 


The Single Message System retrieves the issuer processor ID from configured data and sends it 
in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message to the issuer. The issuer must return the 
issuer processor ID in the 0210 response, which Mastercard will include in the Financial 
Transaction Request Response/0210 message to the acquirer. 


The processor ID is a 10-digit number in the form of 9000xxxxxx where the processor ID 
assigned by Mastercard will be up to the last six digits xxxxxx. 


250-byte Batch Data File 


EII data will appear in the 250-byte Batch Data File. 


Additional information 


Contact a Global Customer Care team representative or your regional representative for 
additional information about EII.
