Healthcare FSA and Real-Time Substantiation 


Healthcare FSA and Real-Time Substantiation 


The Single Message System supports processing of healthcare-related transactions made using 
prepaid flexible spending account (FSA) debit cards and Real-time Substantiation transactions. 


The real-time substantiation service supports substantiation at the point-of-sale (POS) for 
qualified healthcare expenses incurred on a Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Healthcare 
Reimbursement Arrangement (HRA), and Health Savings Account (HSA) cards when used at a 
merchant with a qualifying Inventory Information Approval System (IIAS). 


Applies to 


This service is optional for Maestro and Debit Mastercard brands. 


The following table lists possible impacts that the customers should consider; however, it can 
not be a complete list of the changes necessary for the individual processor environment to 
participate in a Healthcare FSA service. 


Customer impact 


The impact on customers that support healthcare FSA and real-time substantiation is described 
in this topic. 


Healthcare FSA 


Participation in the Healthcare FSA is optional for acquirers. Issuers do not need the service but 
should be aware of the process since it will affect financial transaction messages. 


Acquirers 


To participate, acquirers must provide Mastercard with a list of merchants certified as 
compliant with the Inventory Information Approval System (IIAS)—a POS technology used by 
retailers that accept flexible spending account (FSA) debit cards. Mastercard will generate and 
assign an ID number to uniquely identify each merchant as a IIAS program participant. The 
acquirer will provide the ID number assigned by Mastercard in Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 messages with DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 32 (Mastercard 
Assigned ID). 


To obtain or allow a Mastercard Assigned ID to be used for IIAS merchant validation, acquirers 
need to submit a request which specifies whether this is an addition or update of the 
Mastercard Assigned ID, and at a minimum include: 


• 
the acquirer name 
• 
telephone number 
• 
email address 
• 
acquirer ID 
• 
processor ID 
• 
merchant parent/owner name (if applicable) 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1171 



System functionality and services 
Healthcare FSA and Real-Time Substantiation 


• 
Mastercard Assigned ID (if the request is to update an existing MAID) 
• 
merchant contact information 
Acquirers will provide in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 61 (POS Data, 
Extended Condition Codes) if the merchant has validated the transaction with IIAS by adding 
the appropriate value in subfield 3 (Healthcare IIAS Substantiation). Valid values are: 


• 
0 = (default) Merchant terminal did not verify purchased items against Inventory Information 
Approval System (IIAS). Acquirer to provide value. 
• 
1 = Merchant terminal did verify purchased items against Inventory Information Approval 
System (IIAS). Acquirer to provide value. 
• 
2 = Merchant exempt from Inventory Information Approval System (IIAS) based on IRS 90 
percent rule. Acquirer to provide value. 
• 
4 = Transaction submitted as Inventory Information Approval System (IIAS) but from a nonIIAS-
certified merchant. Mastercard to provide value. 
Cash back is not allowed on health care signature-based transactions. Purchase with cash back 
health care related transactions will be declined except for BINs where an issuer has signed up 
for the optional service when the issuer maintains an unrestricted purse (optional service 
described below). 


Issuers 


Issuers should be aware that if an acquirer participates in Healthcare FSA, the data elements 
identifying issuer information will be included in Financial Transaction Request/0200 and 
Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 messages. Issuers must return the data elements in Financial 
Transaction Request Response/0210 and Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430 messages. 


Issuers must notify Mastercard to support real-time substantiation processing by completing 
the Real-time Substantiation Participation Request Form and providing the form to their Global 
Customer Service representative. Participation authorizes Mastercard to provide the issuer with 
real-time substantiation information in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 or the 
Authorization Advice/0120 message. The Single Message System will remove healthcare related 
amounts from the Financial Transaction Request/0200 or the Authorization Advice/0120 
message for non–participating issuers. 


Issuers can choose to sign up for a service that will allow health care related purchase with cash 
back transactions to be passed to them. For BINs that have an unrestricted purse, contact 
Global Customer Care for more information. 


PIN acceptance for healthcare cards 


Mastercard is providing issuers with the ability to approve or decline purchases with cash back 
on unrestricted purses on healthcare cards with a PIN. Mastercard will continue to deny 
purchases with cash back for signature-based healthcare transactions. Mastercard will also 
deny purchase with cash back on healthcare transactions with a PIN, unless the issuer instructs 
Mastercard to send transactions for specific account ranges to them in order to leverage the 
Mastercard purchase with cash back functionality. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1172 



System functionality and services 
Healthcare FSA and Real-Time Substantiation 


Mastercard will allow purchase with cash back on PIN-based activity if the issuer pre-registers 
the BIN. Purchase with cash back activity should be identified as using DE 3 (Processing Code), 
subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code), value 09 (Purchase with Cash back) and allowing 
healthcare-related transactions, indicated in DE 54 (Additional Amounts), subfield 2 (Amount 
Type), value 10 (Healthcare Eligibility Amount) and, if appropriate, subfield 2, value 11 
(Prescription Eligibility Amount), with subfield 2, value 40 (Cash Back). 


Acquirers will send healthcare-related purchase with cash back transactions to Mastercard, and 
Mastercard will decline the transaction or send it to the issuer for the approval decision, 
depending on whether the issuer has registered for the capability to allow Mastercard to pass 
purchases with cash back on unrestricted purses of healthcare cards with a PIN. 


Acquirers must be prepared to receive DE 39 (Response Code), value 30 (Message format error) 
on purchase with cash back requests on a healthcare-related transaction with a PIN when the 
issuer has not registered for the purchase with cash back capability. 


Real-time substantiation amounts 


• 
Mastercard defines DE 54 (Additional Amounts), subfield 2 (Amount Type) with a redefined 
value of 10 (Healthcare Eligibility Amount). When the acquirer is providing the real-time 
substantiation indicator in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), sub element 61, subfield 3, 
this redefined amount type allows the acquirer to indicate the portion of DE 4 (Amount, 
Transaction) that is eligible for real-time substantiation. 
• 
In addition to the Healthcare Eligibility Amount, Mastercard supports amount type, DE 54 
(Additional Amounts), subfield 2, value 11 (Prescription Eligibility Amount), which allows the 
acquirer to indicate the portion of the healthcare eligibility amount that includes the amount 
spent for prescriptions. 
• 
Mastercard Network supports amount type value 12 (Vision Rx Eligibility Amount) for the 
vision Rx total transaction amount. 
Technical description 


The following sections describe technical impacts to acquirers and Single Message System 
transaction processing required to support Healthcare FSA and real-time substantiation. 


Message layouts 


The message types within Single Message System are 


• 
Financial Transaction Request/0200 and 
• 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages. 
Data element definitions 


DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use) and DE 54 (Additional Amounts) support Healthcare FSA. 


DE 48 (Additional Data) 


These conditions apply to DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use) to support the Healthcare FSA 
service 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1173 



System functionality and services 
Healthcare FSA and Real-Time Substantiation 


• 
If the original Financial Transaction Request/0200 message contains DE 48 (Additional Data: 
Private Use), subelement 61, subfield 3 value 0, the merchant terminal did not verify against 
Inventory Information Approval System (IIAS). 
• 
If the original Financial Transaction Request/0200 message contains DE 48 (Additional Data: 
Private Use), subelement 61, subfield 3 value 1, the Single Message System also will confirm 
the Mastercard Assigned ID against the Mastercard IIAS database repository. 
• 
If the merchant has generated 90 percent of its total sales from FSA/HSA/HRA-certified 
healthcare products in the previous fiscal year, that merchant is exempt from IIAS rules. The 
acquirer indicates this exemption by providing DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), 
subelement 61, subfield 3, value 2. 
NOTE: To support the Inventory Information Approval System (IIAS) for auto-substantiation of 
healthcare-related transactions (such as FSA, HRA or HSA), merchants exempt from the IIAS rules 
identified as 90 percent merchants must include their Acquirer ID and Merchant ID in DE 124 
(Member-Defined Data) when DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 61, subfield 3 
(Real-time Substantiation Indicator) is = 2 (Merchant exempt from IIAS based on IRS 90 percent 
rule). 


• 
If the acquirer does not provide a Mastercard assigned ID, or, if the Single Message System is 
unable to confirm the number provided, Mastercard will override the current value of DE 48, 
subelement 61, subfield 3 in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message forwarded to 
the issuer and insert a value of 4 to indicate the transaction was submitted as IIAS-certified, 
but was received from a non IIAS-certified merchant. 
Merchants and acquirers can indicate both the full transaction amount as well as the amount of 
the transaction that is a healthcare-related expense only, in the Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 message. 


DE 54 (Additional Amounts) 


The Financial Transaction Request messages contain DE 54 (Additional Amounts), subfield 2, 
value 10 (Healthcare Eligibility Amount), 11 (Prescription eligibility amount), or 12 (Vision Rx 
Eligibility Amount) to indicate the healthcare, prescription, or vision Rx amounts and sent only to 
the issuers that participate in Real-time Substantiation. 


DE 54 (Additional Amounts), subfield 2, value 11 must only be present when the acquirer 
provides DE 54 (Additional Amounts), subfield 2, value 10 in the Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 or the Authorization Advice/0120 message. In addition, the amount in DE 54 (Additional 
Amounts), subfield 2, value 11 must be less than or equal to the amount of DE 54 (Additional 
Amounts), subfield 2, value 10. 


The prepaid healthcare account issuer will determine whether to approve the entire amount in 
DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) or only the FSA Eligible Expenditure in DE 54 (Additional Amounts). 
If the issuer approves only the amount in DE 54 (Additional Amounts), the issuer is required to 
respond with DE 39 (Response Code)), value 10 (Transaction request approved for the partial 
approval amount) of the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message. This 
determination also will be based on the ability of the merchant or acquirer to support partial 
approval transactions. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1174 



System functionality and services 
Healthcare FSA and Real-Time Substantiation 


DE 54 (Additional Amounts), subfield 2, value 12 can be provided by itself in the Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 or Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages or in combination 
with value 10 or values 10 and 11. 


Values 10, 11, or 12 will not be returned to the acquirer in the Financial Transaction Request 
Response/0210 or the Financial Transaction Advice Response/0230 message. 


DE 124 (Member Defined) 


For PIN Acceptance for Healthcare Cards, DE 124 (Member-Defined Data) must be provided as 
follows. 


To properly identify those 90 percent merchants that are registered and certified with Special 
Interest Group for IIAS Standards (SIGIS) for PIN transactions, acquirers must be prepared to: 


• 
Send the Acquirer ID in DE 124 (Member-Defined Data), positions 1–6, numeric only, right 
justified, zero-fill to the left. Mastercard will assign and provide the Acquirer ID to the 
acquirer. 
• 
Send the Merchant ID in DE 124 (Member-Defined Data), positions 7–21, numeric only, right 
justified, zero-fill to the left 
• 
Provide the six-digit Acquirer ID to merchants to provide SIGIS during registration. 
• 
Provide the 15–digit Merchant ID to merchants to provide SIGIS during registration. 
NOTE: 


Mastercard strongly encourages acquirers to notify their SIGIS-certified merchants that they should 
review the SIGIS recommended testing that is available from the SIGIS Web site: www.sig-is.org. 


To properly identify those 90 Percent merchants that are registered and certified with SIGIS for 
PIN transactions, issuers must be prepared to: 


• 
Receive DE 124 (Member-Defined Data) 
• 
Receive the Acquirer ID in DE 124 (Member-Defined Data), positions 1–6, numeric only 
• 
Receive the Merchant ID in DE 124 (Member-Defined Data), positions 7–21, numeric only 
250-byte Batch Data File 


Healthcare FSA data will appear in the 250-byte Batch Data File.

additional information about Healthcare FSA processing.

System functionality and services 
Mastercard One Credential 


Mastercard One Credential 


Mastercard One Credential is a single, digitally connected credential that offers cardholders a 
choice of multiple payment methods. It allows customers to choose the payment option (debit, 
credit, or prepaid, including installments) that best suits their needs through a seamless digital 
experience in their banking app or website. Mastercard One Credential connects multiple 
existing funding accounts and lets consumers set their payment preferences. 


Overall benefits of the Mastercard One Credential are: 


• 
Consumer benefits: Mastercard One Credential addresses the consumer's need for flexibility 
and control, enabling consumers to personalize their spending preferences and access various 
payment methods. This results in greater choice and convenience. 
• 
Issuer benefits: Issuers can provide a differentiated offering, enhancing customer loyalty, 
stickiness and engagement, solidifying their status as the consumer’s primary financial 
provider. Mastercard One Credential allows issuers to offer new ways to access credit 
(subject to consumer being credit qualified) to existing customers and reach new customers. 
• 
Acquirer benefits: Acquirers may benefit from increased transaction volumes and 
incremental revenue with minimal development required as Mastercard One Credential 
adoption grows. 
• 
Merchant benefits: Availability of multiple funding methods may allow merchants to 
experience higher average transaction amounts and volumes, better conversion rates, and 
improved consumer retention through personalized mechanisms. 
For more information on Mastercard One Credential, refer to the Mastercard One Credential 
Technical Implementation Guide.

Multiple Completions 


Multiple completion allows customers up to seven days to submit completions from the 
settlement date, providing more time to settle transactions. 


Financial Transaction Request/0200: Maestro multiple completion 


Acquirers using multiple completions should submit DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] data), 
subfield 7 (POS Transaction Status) value 4 (Preauthorization request). 


• 
DE 61, subfield 12 (POS Authorization Life Cycle) contains value 07 (Preauthorization stays 
in effect for seven days). 
• 
When DE 61, subfield 7 (POS Transaction Status) contains value 4 (Preauthorization 
request) and DE 61, subfield 12 contains a value 07, Mastercard will allow one or more 
delayed completions in support of multiple completions. 
Issuers will receive DE 61, subfield 7 (POS Transaction Status) value 4. 


• 
DE 61, subfield 12 contains value 07. 
• 
When DE 61, subfield 7 contains value 4 and DE 61, subfield 12 contains a value 07, 
Mastercard will allow one or more delayed completions in support of multiple completions.

Online Exception Item Processing 


Online Exception Item Processing 


This section documents information about 04xx Online Exception Item messages for customers 
and processor host systems. 


Technical description 


Online exceptions are available to processors the day following the settlement day. To have the 
04xx message processed as an online exception item, the message must be submitted following 
Mastercard settlement of the original transaction. 


Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 and Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 messages that occur within the 
same settlement day as the original request message are processed as same day reversals. All 
reversal advice messages contain settlement amount and transaction fee data that are 
included with Mastercard reconciliation and settlement. 


Acquirer-generated exception items 


An acquirer can initiate an exception request by sending an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: 
acquirer-generated exception message to the Single Message System after end-of-day 
processing. 


The Single Message System will match the request to the original logged transaction. If the 
requested exception passes the appropriate editing, Mastercard will forward a positive response 
to the acquirer with an Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430: system-generated message 
where DE 39 (Response Code) is 00 (approved or completed successfully). If the acquirer 
receives a positive response, the Single Message System will format the appropriate Acquirer 
Reversal Advice/0420 message and then forward it to the issuer of the transaction. 


If the requested exception fails to pass the appropriate editing, the Single Message System will 
deny the acquirer exception with an Acquirer Reversal Advice Response/0430: system-generated 
message. The Single Message System will return DE 39, value 30 and DE 44 with the reason 
code for the denial. Where possible, the data element in error also is present in DE 44. No advice 
will be sent to the issuer. 


Issuer-generated exception items 


An issuer can initiate an exception request by sending an Issuer Reversal Advice/0422: exception, 
issuer-generated message to the Single Message System after end-of-day processing. 


The Single Message System will match the request to the original logged transaction. If the 
requested exception passes the appropriate editing, the Single Message System will forward a 
positive response to the issuer with an Issuer Reversal Advice Response/0432: exception, 
Acquirer-generated message, where the DE 39, (Response Code) is 00 (approved or completed 
successfully). If the issuer receives a positive response, the Single Message System also will 
format the appropriate Issuer Reversal Advice/0422: exception, issuer-generated message and 
forward it to the acquirer. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1195 



System functionality and services 
Reversing previously entered chargebacks 


If the requested exception fails to pass the appropriate editing, the Single Message System will 
deny the issuer exception with an Issuer Reversal Advice Response/0432: exception, acquiregenerated 
message. The Single Message System will return DE 39, value 30 (Message format 
error) and DE 44 with the reason code for the denial, and DE 44 (Additional Response Data) will 
contain the reason code for the denial. Where possible, the data element in error is also present 
in DE 44. No advice will be sent to the acquirer. 


Reversing previously entered chargebacks 


Debit Mastercard issuers can reverse chargebacks through Single Message Transaction Manager 
or online exception item processing for first chargebacks or arbitration chargebacks only. 


Debit Mastercard issuers that use Single Message Transaction Manager can reverse chargeback 
transactions entered in error when they select chargeback reason detail code 82 (Chargeback 
Reversal). 


Debit Mastercard issuers that use online exception item processing can reverse chargeback 
transactions when they send an Issuer Reversal Advice/0422 transaction to the Single Message 
System with DE 60 (Advice Reason Code), subfield 1 (Advice Reason Code) with a value of 489 
(Chargeback) and subfield 2 (Advice Reason Detail Code) with a value of 82. 


For additional details on DE 60, refer to Data element definitions. .

Transaction Processing Rules 
Partial Approval Processing 


This section describes procedures for acquirers and issuers to implement, support, and process a 
partial approval transaction. 


A partial approval enables the issuer to indicate approval of all or a portion of the requested 
transaction amount submitted by the acquirer in the financial transaction request. 


Debit Mastercard and Maestro cardholders may not know the exact balance on their accounts 
when making a retail purchase. The issuer may decline the transaction, which could result in a 
lost sale; or the response message can require the merchant to call the issuer for approval, 
which could increase checkout time and processing expenses for the acquirer and the issuer. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1197 



System functionality and services 
Partial Approval Processing 


To assist in these situations, Mastercard offers support for partial approvals in financial 
messages in the Single Message System. A partial approval enables the issuer to indicate 
approval of all or a portion of the requested transaction amount submitted by the acquirer in 
the financial transaction request. When the transaction amount is equal to or more than the 
remaining balance on an account, this service enables the issuer to respond with the full account 
balance amount, or a lower approved amount in the Financial Transaction Request Response/ 
0210 message. 


NOTE: Debit Mastercard issuers in the U.S. region that support the partial approval amount service 
must support, and non-U.S. region Debit Mastercard issuers can optionally support, the ability to 
provide a partial approval amount in DE 6 of the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message that is less than, equal to, or greater than the original transaction amount requested in DE 6 
of the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message when DE 18 contains a value of 5542 indicating 
the transaction was initiated at an Automated Fuel Dispenser (AFD). 


Automated fuel dispenser (AFD) transactions will be declined when the difference between the preauthorization 
amount of a transaction and the completed amount of a transaction exceeds USD 1000. 


Partial approvals will be allowed when processing virtual card number (VCN) transactions. This applies 
to Mastercard In Control VCNs only. 


Applies to 


NOTE: Support for partial approvals is optional for both acquirers and issuers. 


An acquirer can indicate that the merchant terminal supports partial approvals in the Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 message. The issuer can approve all or a portion of the requested 
transaction amount by responding with the approved amount and a partial approval response 
code in the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message. 


Upon receipt of the partial approval response, an attended terminal will prompt the 
participating merchant to initiate a split-tender payment to obtain the remainder of the 
transaction amount in another form of payment from the cardholder. A terminal using MCC 
5542 will stop the dispensing of fuel at the partial approval amount. 


Partial approvals are not allowed for purchase with cash back, ATM, or electronic certificate 
request transactions. Stand-In Authorization does not support partial approvals. 


Acquirers 


Acquirers and merchants that acquire Debit Mastercard and Maestro transactions must 
support the partial approval of authorization transactions and real-time transaction reversals 
(full or partial) and account balance responses from the point of sale. 


NOTE: Support is required in the U.S., and is optional elsewhere. 


For merchant terminals that support the receipt of partial approval responses and split-tender 
processing, acquirers must provide the following in DE 48 (Additional Data), subelement 61 
(POS Data Extended Condition Codes) in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message: 


• 
Subfield 1 (Partial Approval Terminal Support Indicator), value of 1 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1198 



System functionality and services 
Partial Approval Processing 


• 
Subfield 2 (Purchase Amount Only Terminal Support Indicator), value of 0. 
• 
Subfield 3 (Real-time Substantiation Indicator), values 0, 1, 2, or 4. 
• 
Subfields 4-5 (Reserved for Future use - Final Authorization Indicator) value of 0 
Acquirers that support the receipt of partial approval responses must be prepared to receive the 
following in Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 messages: 


• 
DE 39 (Response Code), 10 (Transaction request approved for the partial approval amount) 
• 
DE 4 (Amount, Transaction), which will contain the partial approval amount (also DE 5 
[Amount, Settlement], and DE 6 [Amount Cardholder Billing], if applicable to the 
transaction) 
• 
DE 54 (Additional Amounts), which will contain the original amount. 
NOTE: 


If the issuer responds with a partial approval amount equal to the original requested amount, the 
acquirer must request alternate payment for any additional amount, such as for a tip. 


Issuers 


All debit and prepaid issuers in the U.S. region must support the ability to process and respond 
appropriately to merchants that support partial approvals and real-time reversals (full or 
partial). 


Issuers can respond to a request with a partial approval equal to the original requested amount. 
Instead of a regular approval, in the case where funds are limited to that which will allow them 
chargeback rights for any amount over the approved amount (i.e.; equal to the requested 
amount on a prepaid account). 


Issuers that support partial approvals are affected as follows: 


• 
Issuers that support partial approvals must provide DE 39, value 10, the partial approval 
amount in DE 6 in the issuer’s cardholder billing currency, and the issuer’s cardholder billing 
currency code in DE 51 of the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message. 
• 
Issuers must respond with a partial approval only when they receive a Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 message containing DE 48, subelement 61, subfield 1, value 1 (merchant 
terminal can accept partial approvals). 
• 
Debit Mastercard issuers in the U.S. region that support the partial approval amount service 
must support, and non-U.S. region Debit Mastercard issuers can optionally support, the 
ability to provide a partial approval amount in DE 6 of the Financial Transaction Request 
Response/0210 message that is less than, equal to or greater than the original transaction 
amount requested in DE 6 of the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message when DE 18 
contains a value of 5542 indicating the transaction was initiated at an Automated Fuel 
Dispenser (AFD).

Transaction Processing Rules 
Payment Transactions 


A Payment Transaction transfers funds to a Mastercard, Maestro, or Cirrus account. 


A Payment Transaction is not a credit that reverses a previous purchase. Payment Transactions 
include Mastercard Send Payment Transactions, Gaming Payment Transactions, and China 
Funds Transfer Payment Transactions. 


The requirements for initiating and processing Payment Transactions appear in the Mastercard 
Rules, the Mastercard Move - MoneySend and Funding Transactions Program Standards, and the 
Mastercard Gaming and Gambling Payments Program Standards. 


DE 3 (Processing Code) 


The following DE 3 subfields describe the effect of a transaction on the customer account and 
the type of accounts affected. 


Subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code) 


DE 3, subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code) describes the specific transaction being 
performed. 


Subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code), Value 28 (Payment Transaction) 


Mastercard supports Maestro Payment Transactions identified in DE 3 (Processing Code), 
subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code), value 28 (Payment Transaction) that are 
acquired in Europe and routed to an issuer on the Single Message System.

PIN Management at the ATM 


PIN Management at the ATM 


The PIN management at ATM service allows cardholders to perform PIN changes and PIN 
unblock activities at the ATM terminal. 


Personal identification number (PIN) management is an optional service for acquirers and 
issuers. 


The PIN management at the ATM service allows cardholders using chip cards and non-chip cards 
(magnetic stripe) to perform the following transactions at an automated teller machine (ATM): 


• 
PIN unblock (for chip cards only): Cardholders can reset the counter on their chip card to 
unblock it, such as, when they have exceeded the maximum number of allowable 
unsuccessful PIN entries. 
• 
PIN change (for chip or magnetic stripe cards): Cardholders can change the PIN on their chip 
card or magnetic stripe card. 
PIN management is administered at the bank identification number (BIN) level and is available 
for both chip and non-chip (magnetic stripe) cards used at an ATM. 


NOTE: PIN unblock and PIN change transactions cannot be processed at a point-of-sale (POS) device. 


Acquirers 


Participation in the PIN management at the ATM service is optional for acquirers. 


Acquirers can determine whether an issuer participates in the PIN management at the ATM 
service by checking position 73 (PIN Management Flag) in the 80-byte FIT data file. If the issuer 
participates and the acquirer's record is correctly formatted, PIN Management transactions will 
be processed. 


The following table provides a list of the response codes for the Financial Transaction Request/ 
0200 message format used by the Single Message System. The table also lists definitions, 
expected acquirer actions, and examples of recommended English language window messages.

Issuers 


Issuers that choose to participate in one or both of the PIN management services, PIN change 
and PIN unblock, can request the services by contacting their Customer Implementation 
Services representative. 


Participation is administered at the BIN level. If an issuer’s BIN participates in the chip-tomagnetic 
stripe conversion service or chip pre-validation on-behalf service, the issuer’s BIN 
cannot participate in the PIN management at the ATM service. 


Issuers must pay the acquirer the interchange on all PIN management transactions. Interchange 
will apply to both approvals and denials. Issuers will pay switch fees to Mastercard. The fees will 
be billed at the same rate as ATM balance inquiry transactions. 


Issuers must be prepared to receive an acquirer reversal canceling the PIN change. If the PIN 
cannot be changed for the chip or magnetic stripe, Mastercard processes an Acquirer Reversal 
Advice/0420 message to the issuer. 


Issuers are responsible for any PIN validation necessary in DE 125 (New PIN Data). Mastercard 


does not perform PIN validation on DE 125. 


Technical description 


Mastercard supports PIN Management in Financial Transaction Request/0200 and Financial 


Transaction Request Response/0210 messages processed via an ATM. 


A PIN Management transaction message is identified using DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1 
(Cardholder Transaction Type Code) for Mastercard ATM brands Mastercard, Maestro, and 
Cirrus, as follows: 


• 
PIN unblock (valid for chip cards only): value 91 
• 
PIN change (valid for chip and magnetic stripe cards): value 92 
DE 3, subfield 1 values 91 and 92 are valid only when DE 3, subfield 2 (Cardholder Account Type 
[From]) and subfield 3 (Cardholder Account Type [To]) equal value 00, indicating No Account 
Specified transactions.

ATM PIN change transactions for all regions 


Valid codes for DE 3 (Processing Code) are 


• 
PIN unblock, no account specified: 910000 and 
• 
PIN change, no account specified: 920000. 
ATM PIN change transactions for all regions 


PIN management at the ATM service, specifically PIN change transactions for non-chip 
(magnetic stripe) cards, is available to all regions. 


Issuers with BINs that currently participate in PIN management for chip cards must be prepared 
to receive and support PIN change transactions for magnetic stripe cards. 


PIN change processing requirements 


These conditions apply to the processing of PIN change transactions. 


• 
If the card is a magnetic stripe card or a chip card not supporting offline PIN, the issuer can 
– 
approve the PIN change transaction with a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 
message containing DE 39 (Response Code), value 00 (Approved or Completed 
Successfully) or value 85 (Not Declined) or 
– 
decline with DE 39, value 70 (Contact Card Issuer), 71 (PIN Not Changed), or 89 
(Unacceptable PIN–Transaction Declined–Retry). 
• 
If the card is a chip card supporting offline PIN, the issuer must not approve the transaction 
when DE 22, subfield 1 contains a value of 80 or 90. The issuer must decline the transaction 
with a Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message containing DE 39, value 57 
(Transaction not permitted to issuer or cardholder). 
NOTE: PIN management transactions initiated with a chip card must include DE 22, subfield 1 (POS 
Terminal PAN Entry Mode), value of 05 (PAN auto-entry via integrated circuit card) and DE 55 
(Integrated Circuit Card [ICC] System-Related Data). 


NOTE: If these transactions are approved, the offline PIN will be out of sync with the online PIN, 


and subsequent offline transactions can be declined because of invalid PIN. 


PIN change participation requirements 


These conditions apply to participation in the PIN management service for PIN change 
transactions. 


• 
If an issuer’s BIN participates in chip to magnetic stripe conversion or M/Chip cryptogram 
pre-validation on-behalf services, the issuer’s BIN cannot participate in PIN change 
transactions, even if the BIN also contains magnetic stripe cards. 
• 
If the Single Message System performs PIN verification on behalf of the issuer, the issuer’s 
BIN cannot participate in PIN Change transactions.

PIN translation 


Issuers that choose to participate in the PIN management at the ATM service for PIN change 
transactions must contact a Customer Implementation Services representative and complete a 
PIN Management Service Request (form 888). 


PIN translation 


When Mastercard receives a PIN management transaction, the PIN in DE 52 (Personal 
Identification Number [PIN] Data) must be translated (encrypted/decrypted) in the validation 
process. For a PIN change transaction, the new PIN data will be passed in DE 125 (New PIN 
Data). PIN translation will be performed on DE 125 using the same keys used for translating DE 
52. 


The following sections describe technical impacts to acquirers and issuers supporting the PIN 
management at the ATM service. 


Message layouts 


The use of DE 125 in the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message is described in this 
section. 


Acquirers will provide new PIN data in DE 125 (New PIN Date) for PIN Change transactions in 
the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message. 


Issuers will receive new PIN data in DE 125 in whichever format has been agreed to with 
Mastercard. Mastercard performs the necessary format conversion where appropriate.

DE 125 (New PIN Data) 


DE 125 (New PIN Data) for the PIN change function will be passed in DE 125 (New PIN Data), a 
binary data block containing a derived encrypted value calculated from the new PIN introduced 
by the cardholder at an ATM offering PIN change. The Single Message System permits PINs 
from 4 to 12 characters in length. The encrypted PIN block is always 64 bits (8 bytes) in length, 
regardless of the original PIN length.

Single Message Transaction Manager 


The participation indicators for the Institution Routing Table (IRT) window to support PIN

• 
A PIN Management label has been added. 
•

80-byte Financial Institution Table File 


The PIN Management Flag is in position 73 of the 80-byte Financial Institution Table (FIT) File 
and has values Y (Yes) and N (No). 


Supporting documentation 


Go to Mastercard Connect to access the Single Message Transaction Manager User Guide. 


PIN Verification Value on File Service 


Mastercard supports the PIN verification value (PVV) on file service during Stand-In 
Authorization for point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Issuers that request to participate in this 
service will send a file to Mastercard that contains the PVV/PIN offsets required by the PIN 
validation process. 


NOTE: Mastercard supports optional PIN validation for issuers whose PVV/PIN offset are encoded on 
Track 1 or Track 2. 


The PVV on file service during Stand-In Authorization provides the following benefits to issuers. 


• 
Issuers that do not encode a PVV/PIN offset on Track 1 or Track 2 of the cards can have 
access to PIN validation services. 
• 
Issuers can migrate card portfolios from service providers that perform PIN validation 
services on the issuer's behalf. 
Issuers can have Mastercard verify the PIN in a POS transaction during Stand-In Authorization. 
This service is restricted to transactions that are sent to Mastercard. 


Issuers that choose to register for this service must send a PVV/PIN Offset File to Mastercard to 
update cardholder PINs and must use the security keys managed by Mastercard. This file must 
be sent using the secure Global File Transfer (GFT) approved by Mastercard. Issuers must also 
be sure to exchange the PIN verification keys (PVKs) with Mastercard before using this service. 


Issuers sending their files to the Single Message System can use Bulk ID RM29 (Production), 
RM31 (MTF), or CONNECT:Direct to send the PVV/PIN Offset file to Mastercard.

Recurring Payment Services 


This section describes procedures for acquirers and issuers to indicate a recurring Payment 
Transaction through the Single Message System and how to participate in the payment 
cancellation service. 


Recurring payments are arrangements in which cardholders give merchants approval to bill their 
accounts at either predetermined (such as monthly or quarterly) intervals or as agreed to by 
cardholders and merchants. The amounts can differ for each transaction (such as phone service 
or utility bills). 


Recurring payments 


Acquirers indicate a recurring Payment Transaction by including DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] 
Data), subfield 4 (POS Cardholder Presence), value 4 (Standing order/recurring transactions) in 
Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages to the issuer. 


Some merchants currently obtain pre-authorization and submit completion messages for 
recurring Payment Transactions after receiving notifications from cardholders to terminate 
billing. 


Cardholders who notify merchants to stop recurring payment billing and continue to be billed 
can dispute those recurring Payment Transactions with their issuers. Issuers can initiate 
chargebacks for disputed recurring Payment Transactions using Message Reason code 41 
(Cancelled Recurring Transaction [Debit Mastercard only]). 


An ASI transaction is an optional message type that enables the merchant to determine the 
status of the cardholder account before requesting an online authorization for the full amount 
of the transaction. The transaction amount of an ASI transaction is zero. No liability shift or 
chargeback protection is associated with ASI transactions. Refer to Reports and files for more 
information. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

message. Recurring payment ASI transactions are not applicable for Maestro issuers. 


Issuers

transactions, as identified by the presence of the following data elements in Financial

Stand-In Authorization Account Validation Services 


The Stand-In Authorization account validation services are mandated for all issuers to adopt the 
validation services that are appropriate for their Mastercard® card programs. 


Issuers must share security keys with Mastercard for Mastercard to perform validation in Stand-
In Authorization. 


NOTE: Mastercard mandates to use account validation services to lock in account protection with 
market-appropriate cardholder authentication and validation methods. PIN validation is an optional 
validation service. 


Magnetic stripe validation 


Tests the magnetic stripe, or CVC1 data, to validate the legitimacy of the account and the 
authenticity of the POS or ATM transaction. 


M/Chip validation 


Evaluates the chip cryptogram data in the authorization request to validate payment 
authenticity for POS, ATM, and contactless transactions. The M/Chip validation supports issuers 
that process chip transactions on an ongoing basis, including the validation of the Authorization 
Request Cryptogram and generation of the Authorization Response Cryptogram on their hosts 
when the issuer is signed out, the transaction cannot be delivered to the issuer, or the issuer 
timed out. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1222 



System functionality and services 
Stand-In Authorization 


PIN validation 


Verifies the cardholder's personal identification number (PIN), instead of the sales receipt 
signature, during authorization to ensure legitimate transactions. 


Contactless validation 


Tests magnetic stripe, or CVC3 data, to authenticate accounts used for contactless 
transactions. 


Stand-In Authorization 


Stand-In Authorization is a Mastercard service that responds on behalf of the issuer to 
authorization requests that have been routed to the Mastercard Network when the issuer does 
not respond, cannot be reached, provides an invalid response, or declines the transaction with 
91, 92, or 96. 


DE 39 (Response Code), values 


Stand-In Authorization can help issuers protect their revenue and minimizes their risk, 
strengthening their cardholder relationships and safeguarding their brand reputation. Stand-In 
Authorization supports various brands, for example: 


• 
Mastercard, Maestro, Cirrus, and non-Mastercard brands 
• 
Segments: consumer and commercial 
• 
Products: credit and debit 
• 
Channels: POS, CNP, and Quasi-Cash for transactions switched through the Mastercard 
Network. 
As transactions occur and are switched through the Mastercard Network, the network 
attempts to pass transactions to the issuer. If the issuer is unavailable or unresponsive, Stand-In 
Authorization steps in and decisions the transaction on their behalf. 


Stand-In Authorization is enabled, by default, for all authorization account ranges for 
Mastercard, Maestro and Cirrus card programs. Information on required use of Stand-In 
Authorization is available in the Transaction Processing Rules. 


Issuers may list accounts in the Stand-In Authorization Account File as Negative (lost/stolen/ 
fraud) or Premium Listings for valued/preferred cardholders. 


Issuers may list individual card numbers to identify exception accounts that are processed 
differently than regular accounts. They can list these accounts either with higher limits to ensure 
approval, such as the limits for Premium Listings or as Negative for lost/stolen/fraud or unpaid/ 
over limit accounts that must be declined. If Stand-In Authorization determines that an account 
is listed on an exception file, Stand-In Authorization is modified. For a description of how to list 
accounts, refer to the Account Management System User Manual. 


Issuers must support SAF interleaving for online Stand-In Authorization advice messages. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Time-Based Payments Services 


Mastercard time-based payment services are available to acquirers and issuers of Mastercard® 
, 
Maestro®, and Cirrus® cards 


Global time-based installment payment services 


ATM credit card cash advance installments service is available globally. 


ATM credit card cash advance installments service 


This service allows a cardholder at an ATM the ability to request a credit card cash advance and 
to choose the schedule of installments over which payments will be extended. 


The issuer will respond and accept the cardholder’s proposed installment schedule, present an 
alternate installment schedule, or decline the transaction. 


The cardholder can choose to accept the issuer’s alternate terms or cancel the transaction. If 
the cardholder accepts the terms, the acquirer will submit a withdrawal transaction to the 
issuer. 


The issuer will respond authorizing the withdrawal transaction and the cash will be dispensed by 
the ATM along with the details of the installment payment schedule printed on the ATM receipt. 


The issuer will debit the cardholder on the monthly credit card statement with payments 
extending over the agreed upon installment schedule. 


Acquirers and issuers 


Participation in the ATM credit card cash advance installments service is determined at the 
country level. Within a participating country, customers that choose to participate in this service 
must contact Customer Implementation Services. 


Customers that participate in the ATM credit card cash advance installments service must 
prepare their systems to send and to receive values in DE 112 (Additional Data [National Use]), 
subelement 027 (ATM Credit Card Cash Advance Installments). 


Technical description 


The ATM credit card cash advance installment service affects data element definitions, system 
edits and Single Message Transaction Manager. 


Data element definitions 


This service affects DE 112 (Additional Data [National Use]).

ATM credit card cash advance installments service 


DE 112 (Additional Data [National Use]) 


DE 112 (Additional Data [National Use]) is reserved for national organizations to define data 
unique to specific networks or specific programs and services. 


For the ATM Credit Card Cash Advance Installments service, a cardholder at an ATM can make 
an inquiry requesting a credit card cash advance with payments extending over a scheduled 
number of installments. The issuer responds and accepts the cardholder’s installment schedule, 
offers an alternate installment schedule, or declines the transaction. The cardholder can accept 
or reject the issuer’s terms. If rejected, the acquirer submits a reversal. 


NOTE: An ATM Cash Advance Installments Withdrawal transaction, in which DE 61 (Point of Service 
[POS] Data) position 7 equals 0 (Normal request [original presentment]), cannot occur without a 
preceding ATM Cash Advance Installments Inquiry transaction in which DE 61, position 7 equals 3 
(Time Based Payment Authorization Request or CDC inquiry request). 


The use of each subelement in DE 112 is summarized in Data element definitions and details. DE 
112, subelement 027 (ATM Credit Card Cash Advance Installments) is used by inquiry/ 
withdrawal messages for ATM credit card cash advance installment Payment Transactions.. 


DE 112, subelement 001, positions 7-8 contains Transaction Type information on the type of 
ATM Cash Advance transaction. 


Valid values for ATM Cash Advance transactions are:

Region-Specific Installment Payment Services 


Region-Specific Installment Payment Services 


The following time-based payment services provide Maestro cardholders several options to 
delay full payment of purchase, post-dated, and installment payments. 


Consumer direct credit (CDC) 


Consumers at the point of interaction can make an inquiry requesting time pay options for a 
major purchase. The issuer can respond, providing up to four financing plans for the consumer to 
choose. The consumer can then select one of the options and the merchant submits the 
“purchase” request in another transaction. The consumer is then billed monthly for the 
installment payment. 


NOTE: CDC Inquiry transactions must include DE 61 (Point of Service [POS] Data), subfield 7 (POS 
Transaction Status), value 3 (Time based payment authorization request or CDC inquiry request) 
equals 3. If the acquirer sends a transaction type other than 50 in DE 112, subelement 1 and the issuer 
returns a transaction type 50, the Single Message System will send a 0420 reversal message to the 
issuer with DE 60 value 4540000 to indicate a format error in the 0210 message. The Single Message 
System will return the Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 message to the acquirer with a 
DE 39 value of 91. 


Parcelas with interest 


Under this option, the length of repayment installments ranges from two to six months. The 
transaction is billed monthly to the cardholder. The authorization returned to the acquirer 
includes the amount of interest over the total installment value and taxes on interest. 


Post-dated 


A transaction is authorized in real time with the associated payment due to the issuer up to 60 
days from the original transaction date. No settlement occurs at the time of the original 
transaction. A merchant can pay a “warranty fee” to guarantee funds availability once the 
issuer authorizes the transaction. Warranty fees are collected at the time of settlement. 


Installment payments 


A transaction is authorized in real time with payments to the merchant spread over a 
predetermined number of months with monthly installments on the balance. A merchant can 
pay a warranty fee to guarantee funds availability for each installment. 


Merchant-generated installment 


Time-based payments enable merchants and customers to negotiate the timing of cardholder 
debits for a purchase. The merchant is paid on day one, while the cardholder can be debited by 
the issuer at a later date. Payments can be split into several installments. These transactions 
display under the Maestro POS brand. 


NOTE: For customers in Brazil that participate in Merchant Generated Installment Payments, if the 
acquirer sends a transaction type of 70 in subelement 001, the Single Message System will include DE 
112, subelement 001 in Reversal Advice/0420 messages.

Reports and files 
Batch file overview 


Presentation of Reports 


Each Single Message System report starts with an overview that contains the following information. 


• 
Title: name of the report 
• 
Generated by: system generating the report 
• 
Purpose: reason for providing the report 
• 
Description: type of information included in the report 
• 
Frequency: how often the report is generated 
• 
Distribution methods: distribution options and associated bulk file or Mastercard File Express 
application identification numbers 
A sample of the report follows each overview description. Field descriptions for the report follow the 
report sample. 


Batch file overview 


The Single Message System provides different types of batch files to customers participating in 
one or more electronic funds transfer programs offered by the Single Message System. 


Single Message System batch files 


The Single Message System provides batch files to assist acquirer and issuer with their internal 


customer service, settlement, and reconciliation operations. 


The types of batch files provided by the Single Message System are: 


• 
Mastercard Debit Switch (MDS) Report Transmission File 
• 
250-byte Batch Data File 
• 
80-byte Financial Institution Table File 
• 
Contactless Chargeback Protection Amounts File 
MDS Report Transmission File 


The MDS Report Transmission File contains daily and month-to-date Single Message System 


generated reports for customers processing through the Mastercard Network. 


Customers will receive: 


• 
Production Bulk ID T461 
• 
MDS Member Test Bulk ID T467 
Customers in South Africa will receive: 
• 
Production Bulk ID TS61 
• 
MDS Member Test Bulk ID TJ61

250-byte Batch Data File 


The 250-byte Batch Data File is available for each customer participating in an EFT program. 
Customers that process through the Mastercard Network receive the batch data files as: 


• 
Production Bulk ID T464 
• 
Member Test Bulk ID T470 
Customers that process through the Mastercard Network in South Africa receive the batch data 
files as: 


• 
Production Bulk ID TS65 
• 
Member Test Bulk ID TJ65 
80-byte Financial Institution Table File 


The Single Message System creates a batch Financial Institution Table (FIT) data file from the 
online database. These FIT data files can be sent to customers for full FIT file loads and 
additional product information. 


Customers will receive the FIT data files as: 


• 
Production Bulk ID (T458) 
• 
Member Test Bulk ID (T459) 
Contactless Chargeback Protection Amounts File 


The Single Message System produces a daily file of all Contactless Chargeback Protection 
Amounts for each customer that has requested to receive these files. 


Customers will receive: 


• 
Production Bulk ID (TAN4) 
• 
Member Test Bulk ID (TAN6)

Customer testing 


Customer testing 


For customer testing, the Single Message System settles on average five times a day. 


• 
Maestro®/Cirrus® (domestic): 02:00 Eastern time 
• 
Debit Mastercard®: 15:00 Eastern time 
• 
Maestro®/Cirrus® (international): 15:00 Eastern time 
• 
24:00 Brazil time (intracurrency)/17:00 to 18:00 Eastern time (depending on daylight saving 
time) 
• 
Canada: 10:00 Toronto time 
• 
24:00 New South Wales (NSW) Australia/08:00 to 10:00 Eastern time (depending on 
daylight saving time) 
Data delivery options 


Most customers are set up to receive their Report Transmission File, 250-byte Batch Data File, 
and FIT Data File at the Single Message System end of day (EOD). 


However, some customers prefer to receive the 250-byte Batch Data File and Report 
Transmission files early in alignment with when they settle. Acquirers and issuers that choose to 
receive the 250-byte Batch Data File in the T464 bulk file early must be prepared to handle 
multiple transmissions within a 24-hour timeframe. Actual transmission will coincide with and 
occur as soon as possible after the above-stated settlement times. 


If an early delivery option is selected for reports, Report Transmission Files or T461 Bulk Files will 
be delivered during every settlement cutoff in which transaction activity occurs after the 
designated delivery settlement time. Acquirers and issuers that choose to receive the T461 
reports early must be able to accept multiple deliveries of the T461 throughout the day and end 
of day if the need arises. If no transaction activity occurs within an entire settlement day, some 
administrative and month-to-date statistical reports may end up being delivered during the 
normal end-of-day window. 


The following reports distinguish activity for each new settlement service transaction cutoff 
totals: 


• 
Daily Control Report (SWCHD363) 
• 
Monthly Control Report (SWCHM363) 
• 
Daily Interchange Report (SWCHD412) 
• 
Monthly Interchange Report (SWCHM412) 
Acquirers and issuers that choose to receive their T464 and T461 file transmissions earlier to 
align with the settlement service cutoffs should contact Customer Technical Services for setup 
options.

Single Message System batch file transmission 


Single Message System batch file transmission 


The Single Message System provides optional electronic transmission of transaction detail and 
report data files. 


Data transmissions 


The Single Message System supports external complex-to-complex batch file data transmission 
with various Mastercard supported protocols. 


Mastercard has developed its own proprietary file transfer products that can be used for data 
transmission. Mastercard also utilizes non-proprietary data transmission products that were 
developed by outside organizations. 


Mastercard file transfer products 


Mastercard has developed proprietary file transfer products to assist with data transmissions. 
Mastercard File Express is a software product developed by Mastercard. Mastercard File Express 
enables processors to download and upload production and test files from the Single Message 
System to the customer, retrieve archived files, generate a file transmission report, and print the 
file transmission report to the customer's printer or preview it from Mastercard File Express. 
Another tool that can be used is the Mastercard File Express Scheduler which can be used in 
batch mode for file data transmissions. 


Other file transfer products 


Mastercard has various non-proprietary file transfer products that are available to assist with 
data transmissions. 


The following is a list of non-proprietary products: 


• 
File transfer products developed by Sterling Commerce: Connect:Direct (also known as NDM) 
– 
Connect:Enterprise (also known as SuperTRACs) 
– 
Connect:Gateway (Connect:Gateway add-on product for ASCII file transfers) 
• 
File transfer products developed by Computer Associates 
• 
CA-XCOM (also known as XCOM 6.2) 
Configuration options 


Available configurations are: 


• 
Connect:Direct-to-Connect:Direct 
• 
Mainframe-to-mainframe VPN over TCP/IP (preferred option) 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1236 



Reports and files 
Mastercard Network MIP batch file transmission 


• 
Mastercard File Express-to-PC Workstations 
• 
Dial Line, Internet, or VPN using Mastercard OnLine® Enterprise Edition (data exchanged 
using TCP protocol, data encrypted at 128-bit key encryption, data compressed using Run 
Length Encoding algorithm, users authenticated through SecurID™ token) 
Mastercard Network MIP batch file transmission 


Customer processing systems that use the Mastercard Network MIP Bulk Data Facility (T461 
file) for batch data file transmission must refer to the File Transfer Manual Version 1.1 for all 
technical specifications. 


Batch file retransmission 


To assist in data recovery, the Single Message System maintains cycles (for example, business 
days) of transaction detail and report data for each customer in production. If a customer 
encounters problems, it can request a retransmission of data files (report and detail) as needed 
by contacting Customer Technical Services. 


250-byte Batch File format 


The 250-byte format supports financial, non-financial and addendum records. Each record 
layout is displayed with the appropriate fields and corresponding attributes from the online 
transaction processing log file used to create the records. The values in the Comments and 
Values column are generated from the online messages, unless otherwise indicated, except 
interchange fees which are calculated in batch. Customers can choose to receive the 250-byte 
Batch Data File at an earlier time to align with their settlement service. Unless the schedule 
option is requested to receive the earlier 250-byte Batch Data File, the Single Message System 
will continue to provide processors with the file during the standard end-of-day delivery 
processing, 24:00 (Eastern time). Customers must be able to handle multiple 250-byte Batch 
Data File transmissions within a 24-hour window. 


250-byte Transaction records 


Transaction records are sorted by settlement service, settlement currency, and acquirer or issuer 
position. The 250-byte Batch Data File Transaction records indicate to processors the credit or 
debit position of the transactions as they are settled to the customers. Debits to issuers are 
presented as credits to acquirers, and credits to issuers are presented as debits to acquirers. The 
250-byte Batch Data File also provides a net settlement record in addition to the acquirer and 
issuer settlement records in the file. When the file contains both acquirer and issuer activity, the 
net settlement record represents the net of both these positions. This net settlement record 
provides information useful for reconciling and validating to Single Message System reports.

Settlement Header Record (SHDR) 


The Settlement Header Record (SHDR) represents the settlement currency code and other 
information about the transactions that follow. There can be multiple settlement header 
records per file if the customer has different settlement currencies or if a customer has 
transactions from both an acquirer and issuer perspective. 


The settlement header record contains processor ID, settlement currency, and service 
information. It specifies the settlement position at a customer level by settlement currency of 
the transactions, so it is possible to have multiple Settlement Header Records on the file. Each 
Settlement Header Record defines one of the settlement currencies. The Settlement Header 
Record is required when there is activity on the file.

Field description details 


For original switch serial number (SSN) positions 5-13 when following an: 


• 
EREC for financial reversal message, positions 5-13 will contain the SSN from the original 
financial transaction. 
• 
EREC chargeback, representment, or adjustment, positions 5-13 will contain the SSN from 
the original financial 0200 message. 
• 
EREC chargeback, representment, or adjustment for an AFD completion, positions 5-13 will 
contain the SSN from the 0220 completion message. 
• 
EREC chargeback, representment, or adjustment for a multi-completion, positions 5-13 will 
contain the unique SSN from each 0220 completion message. 
• 
EREC chargeback, representment, or adjustment for an incremental preauthorization 
completion, positions 5-13 will contain the SSN from the 0220 completion message. 
For original trace number positions 58-63 when following an: 


• 
EREC for financial reversal message, positions 58-63 will contain the trace id from the 
original financial transaction. 
• 
EREC chargeback, representment, or adjustment, positions 58-63 will contain the trace id 
from the original financial 0200 message. 
• 
EREC chargeback, representment or adjustment for an AFD completion, positions 58-63 will 
contain the trace id from the original 0220 completion message. 
• 
EREC chargeback, representment, or adjustment for a multi-completion, positions 58-63 will 
contain the unique trace id from each 0220 completion message. 
• 
EREC chargeback, representment, or adjustment for an incremental preauthorization 
completion, positions 58-63 will contain the trace id from the 0220 completion message. 
For additional trace number positions 244-249 when following an: 


• 
EREC for a reversal of a financial 0200 message, positions 244-249 will contain zeros.

Switch serial number (SSN) position 5-13:

Original SSN position 228-236: 


•

contain the SSN from that financial 0200 message. (matching the value in position 5-13). 
• 
When following an EREC associated to an AFD completion, position 228-236 will contain the 
SSN from that AFD completion. (matching the value in position 5-13). 
• 
When following an EREC associated to an Incremental preauthorization completion, position 
228-236 will contain the SSN from the most recently approved incremental 
preauthorization. 
• 
When following an EREC associated to a Multi-completion, position 228-236 will contain the 
SSN from the preauthorization.

Financial (FREC)/Non-financial (NREC) Records 


The Financial (FREC)/Non-financial (NREC) Records layout reflects the core format of a Single 
Message System financial or non-financial transaction that contains data elements of both the 
online International Organization for Standardization (ISO) message and batch calculated 
settlement. These records are required. 


Financial (FREC)/Non-financial (NREC) Records 


These data elements provide information that can be used by Single Message System customers 
for reconciliation and reporting purposes.

Field description details 


For switch serial number (SSN) positions 5-13 when following a: 


• 
FREC for financial 0200 message, positions 5-13 will contain the SSN from DE 63 (Network 
Data), Subfield 3 (Network Reference Number). 
• 
FREC for AFD completion, positions 5-13 will contain the SSN from the preauthorization. 
• 
FREC for Incremental preauthorization completion, positions 5-13 will contain a new unique 
SSN in DE 63 (Network Data), Subfield 3 (Network Reference Number). 
• 
FREC for each multi completion, positions 5-13 will contain its own new unique SSN in DE 63 
(Network Data), Subfield 3 (Network Reference Number). 
• 
NREC for each incremental preauthorization, positions 5-13 will contain its own unique SSN 
from DE 63 (Network Data), Subfield 3 (Network Reference Number). 
• 
NREC for AFD preauthorization (no completion is received), positions 5-13 will contain the 
SSN from the preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for a non-AFD preauthorization, positions 5-13 will contain the SSN from the 
preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for incremental preauthorization hold cancellation, positions 5-13 will contain a new 
unique SSN in DE 63 (Network Data), Subfield 3 (Network Reference Number). 
• 
NREC for a non-AFD single preauthorization/hold cancellation, positions 5-13 will contain a 
new unique SSN in DE 63 (Network Data), Subfield 3 (Network Reference Number). 
For trace number positions 58-63 when following a: 


• 
FREC and NREC for financial 0200 message, positions 58-63 will contain the trace id from 
DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number). 
• 
FREC for AFD completion, positions 58-63 will contain the trace id DE 11 (Systems Trace 
Audit Number) from the preauthorization. 
• 
FREC for incremental preauthorization completion, positions 58-63 will contain the trace ID 
DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) from the most recently approved incremental 
preauthorization. 
• 
FREC for a single preauthorization and multi completion, positions 58-63 will contain DE 11 
(Systems Trace Audit Number) from the single preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for each incremental preauthorization, positions 58-63 will contain DE 11 (Systems 
Trace Audit Number) from each individual preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for AFD preauthorization (no completion is received), positions 58-63 will contain the 
DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) from the AFD preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for a non-AFD preauthorization, positions 58-13 will contain the DE 11 (Systems Trace 
Audit Number) for the non-AFD preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for incremental preauthorization hold cancellation, positions 58-63 will contain DE 11 
(Systems Trace Audit Number) from the most recently approved incremental 
preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for a non-AFD single preauthorization/hold cancellation, positions 58-63 will contain 
the DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) from the preauthorization.

Reports and files

For additional trace number positions 244-249 when following: 


• 
FREC for financial 0200 message, positions 244-249 will contain zeros. 
• 
FREC for AFD completion, positions 244-249 will contain a new system-generated trace ID. 
• 
FREC for incremental preauthorization completion, positions 244-249 will contain DE 11 
(Systems Trace Audit Number) provided by the acquirer when it is different from the DE11 in 
the most recently approved incremental preauthorization. 
• 
FREC for incremental preauthorization completion, positions 244-249 will contain a new 
system generated value when DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) provided by the acquirer 
is the same value as the most recently approved incremental preauthorization. 
• 
FREC for multi completions, positions 244-249 will contain DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit 
Number) provided by the acquirer when it is different from the DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit 
Number) in the preauthorization. 
• 
FREC for multi completions, positions 244-249 will contain a new system generated value 
when DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) provided by the acquirer is the same DE 11 
(Systems Trace Audit Number) value from the preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for each incremental preauthorization, positions 244-249 will contain zeros. 
• 
NREC for AFD preauthorization when no completion is received, positions 244-249 will 
contain zeros. 
• 
NREC for a non-AFD preauthorization, positions 244-249 will contain zeros. 
• 
NREC for incremental preauthorization and hold cancellation, positions 244-249 will contain 
DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) provided by the acquirer in the hold cancellation 
message when it is different from the DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) value from the 
most recently approved incremental preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for incremental preauthorization and hold cancellation, positions 244-249 will contain 
a new system generated value when DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) provided by the 
acquirer in the hold cancellation message and is the same DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit 
Number) value from the most recently approved incremental preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for single preauthorization and hold cancellation, positions 244-249 will contain DE 11 
(Systems Trace Audit Number) provided by the acquirer in the hold cancellation message 
when it is different from the DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) value from the 
preauthorization. 
• 
NREC for single preauthorization and hold cancellation, positions 244-249 will contain a new 
system generated value when DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit Number) is provided by the 
acquirer in the hold cancellation message and is the same DE 11 (Systems Trace Audit 
Number) value from the preauthorization.

Financial/Non-financial Posting Addendum Record (FPS2) 


The Financial/Non-financial Posting Addendum Record (FPS2) will follow the corresponding 
Financial/Nonfinancial Posting Addendum Record (FPST). Customers who elect to receive the 
FPST message will also receive the FPS2 message. 


The FPS2 record is created when either the: 


• 
FPST Processor Data File (PDF) flag is turned on 
• 
STND PDF flag is turned on and the Response Code is STND 
• 
MMBH PDF flag is turned on and the Response Code is MMBH

Financial/Non-financial Debit Mastercard Addendum Record 
(DBMC) 


The Financial/Non-financial Debit Mastercard Addendum Record (DBMC) follows the FREC core 
record and any corresponding FPST, EPST, and FEER records. This record is optional. 


Financial/Non-financial Debit Mastercard Addendum Record (DBMC) 


The product type must be MD for this addendum record to be created. The DBMC record does 
not include preauthorization transactions. Preauthorization transactions will continue to be 
included with NREC records. Issuers need to be able to accept DE 48, subelement 63 in the 
DBMC record. The DE 48, subelement 63 data will be added in the current filler section of the 
DBMC record.

Financial/Non-financial Additional Data Addendum Record (ADD2) 


The Financial/Non-financial Additional Data Addendum Record (ADD2) follows the 
corresponding FREC, NREC, or EREC core records and any corresponding FPST, EPST, or ADDR 
addendum records, or both. This record is optional. 


If a Mastercard® Merchant Presented QR transaction does not meet the criteria for properly 
formatted Merchant Presented QR data, the transaction will be rejected to the OI, the Sender 
Account Number field is not populated, and the ADD2 record will not be created. 


This addendum will only be created and supplied to the customer if the customer opts in for it 
and the transaction is a Merchant Presented QR transaction, a Mastercard One Credential 
transaction, or a tokenized transaction.

Financial/Non-financial Additional Data Addendum Record (QRD1) 


The Financial/Non-financial Additional Data Addendum Record (QRD1) follows the 
corresponding FREC or NREC core records and any corresponding FPST or ADDR/ADD2 
addendum records, or both. This record is optional. 


If a Mastercard® Merchant Presented QR transaction does not meet the criteria for properly 
formatted Merchant Presented QR data, the transaction will be rejected to the OI, the Sender 
Account Number field is not populated, and the QRD1 record will not be created. The QRD1 
record will not be sent, even when requested, if the QR data field is not populated.

Miscellaneous Fee Records (1740) 


The Miscellaneous Fee Records (1740) provides detailed information about miscellaneous fee 
records the Single Message System receives from the Global Clearing Management System 
(GCMS). These records are optional. 


Miscellaneous Fee Records (1740) 


These records are typically customer-to-customer fees not associated with a particular 
cardholder transaction. They may be customer or clearing system generated, used to reflect the 
settlement position at a processor level by settlement currency.

Corporate card addendum data: optional 


Corporate card addendum data: optional 


The Single Message System provides addendum data submitted by acquirers on Corporate 
Mastercard Cards to the Debit Mastercard® issuers that request to receive corporate card 
transaction data. 


This service is optional for all Debit Mastercard® issuers that issue Mastercard Corporate Cards. 
The corporate card data information is contained on the following addendum records: 


• 
Passenger Transport Detail (General Ticket Information) 
• 
Passenger Transport Detail (Trip Leg Data) 
• 
Passenger Transport Detail (Rail Data) 
• 
Vehicle Rental Detail 
• 
Lodging Summary 
• 
Temporary Services 
• 
Shipping/Courier Services 
• 
Corporate Card Common Data 
• 
Corporate Line Item Detail 
Issuer benefits 


The corporate card addenda allows issuers to assess spending and make better decisions by 
providing rich, accurate, and timely data. The Corporate Card addendum data also allows 
issuers to streamline spending and control costs for greater efficiency. Refer to corporate card 
addendum data Corporate card addendum data: optional in this manual for additional 
information, record layouts, and attributes.

required.

FIT Optional Addendum Record (FIT1) 


Acquirers can use the FIT Optional Addendum Record (FIT1) to determine if the regulatory rate 
is applicable. 


The regulated rates will apply when the Regulated Status Indicator value is a B (Base) or a 1 
(Base Plus Fraud Adjustment). 


Regulatory status updates will be distributed with the next day’s distribution of the 80-byte FIT 
Data File with Addendum Record. Frequent issuer status updates are not anticipated currently.

The Acknowledgment file is ASCII-fixed block. The record length is 125. The block size is 1,000. 


Customers must send the Acknowledgment file from the same endpoint on which they received 
it. If they receive multiple Acknowledgment files on multiple endpoints, an individual 
Acknowledgment file must be sent for each endpoint. 


Mandate to update BIN tables 


Acquirers and merchants are mandated to update BIN tables within the timeframe set in the 
rules. These rules fall under Category A (Payment System Integrity) of the Mastercard 
Noncompliance Framework. Mastercard is notifying acquirers that noncompliance assessments 
may be applied without further notice for noncompliance by themselves or with merchants 
regarding this mandate. 


Transaction processing rules for the FIT 


Section 7 POI Terminal Requirements of the Transaction Processing Rules states, “Acquirers who 
do not default route must update their FIT within six (6) calendar days of being informed of a 
change by the Interchange System. Acquirers who do not default route to the Interchange 
System must use the FIT for routing before default routing to any competing network.” 


Test sending option for the Acknowledgment file 


Acquirers have the option to test sending the Acknowledgment file to Mastercard. For more 
information, contact Customer Implementation Services.

Mastercard does not enforce a specific order for attributes within the file. Users may send 
attributes in any sequence, provided that each field name exactly matches those defined in the 
table below. Every file must include a single set of header, detailed records, and trailer sections. 
The file may contain up to 1 million data records, excluding the header and trailer. 


Mastercard does not support files containing multiple header, detail, and trailer blocks. If a file 
includes more than one such combination, it will be rejected entirely. 


Users may include comments in the top section of the UUFS file by using the pound symbol. 
These comments are intended for informational purposes only and will be excluded from 
processing.
