Reports: specifications 


This section provides descriptions of the reports included in the MDS Report Transmission File. 


Reports overview 


The Single Message System produces transaction processing summary and detail reports for all 
products the Single Message System supports. These reports assist customers in daily 
settlement, reconciliation, system management, customer support functions, and provides 
customer performance statistics. 


All report data in this section is fictitious and does not reflect actual customer activity. Reports 
that provide BIN Number fields will continue to support BINs and BIN extensions from six digits 
to eleven digits. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1373 



Reports and files 
Report transmission 


Report transmission 


Customers can access Single Message System reports through two methods: Global File 
Transfer or Mastercard Operational Reports. Customers request reports in the form that best 
suits their business. 


Table 1344: Report transmission timeframes 


Transmission type 
Timeframe 
Communication line 
Monday through Sunday 
Mastercard Network in the T461 bulk files 
Monday through Sunday 
MDS Report Transmission File—Single Message 
System Member Test Bulk ID (T467) 
Monday through Sunday 


Report transmission availability 


All reports are available through Global File Transfer. The Single Message System transmits 
reports through Global File Transfer to processors, to be delivered per the customer’s request of 
early or at the end of day. 


Additionally, all reports are available through the Mastercard Connect® Operational Reports 
product, accessible through Mastercard Connect®. Customers with access to Mastercard 
Connect® can view the online Single Message System reports using their billing ICA. The online 
reports are available for viewing in Operational Reports for a period of 13 months from the 
original date of publication. 


NOTE: The Single Message System provides customers all of the reports described in this section. 
Customers can contact a Customer Implementation Services (CIS) Specialist or their regional 
representative for information about specific report options.

processor. It is produced by transaction type within a 
brand and includes: 


• 
Financial counts for approved and denied 
• 
Financial amount of the transaction 
• 
Financial and non-financial counts and amounts 
for interchange fee categories 
• 
Counts and total amounts for exception items by 
product 
The SWCHD363 report will display extended decimal 
precision and will allow as many as six digits following 
the decimal point within each specific field to help 
ensure that the net summary total equals the daily 
settlement amount. 


NOTE: Due to multiple settlement distributions and 
extending precision interchange rounding, 
differences between the Settlement Advisements 
and the Settlement Control Report are occasionally 
expected. The advisement amount indicates the 
actual fund movement. 


The following fields on the Acquirer Processor 
Summary and Issuer Processor Summary pages of the 
reports will allow as many as six digits following the 
decimal point: 


• 
Total fees settlement (debit and credit amounts) 
• 
Interchange settlement (debit or credit amount, as 
appropriate) 
Debit Mastercard preauthorization reversals received 
after the settlement cutoff will display as a new line 
under Exception Items in the Summary, there will be a 
count but no dollar amounts. The SWCHD363 reports 
the surcharge amount (DE 28) for an acquirer 
generated, full reversal transaction for both ATM and 
POS in a separate line. This is beneath the existing 
lines for ATM and POS surcharge on financial 
transactions. 


The Single Message System provides the surcharge 
amount in DE 28 in: 


• 
Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: acquirer-generated

The following fields on the Net Settlement Summary 
page of the report will allow as many as six digits 
following the decimal point: 


• 
Interchange fees (debit, credit, and net amounts) 
• 
Total acquirer (debit, credit, and net amounts) 
• 
Total issuer (debit, credit, and net amounts) 
The Net Settlement Summary page lists the net 
settlement of transactions, exception items, and 
interchange fees separated by debit, credit, and net 
for both the acquirer and issuer. For all lines on the 
Net Settlement Summary page, the Credit Indicator 
"CR" will appear to support the changes to the 
reported amounts. It also provides a final combined 
net settlement disposition for the Automated 
Clearing House System (ACH) and the Global Clearing 
Management System (GCMS). 


Intracurrency (ISIS) transactions are detailed on this 
report. The ISIS Agreement Number and Settlement 
Service information are included in the header to 
identify intracurrency transaction information. Pages 
break by currency type within processor, and then by 
Routing and Transit number (Institution ID). This is 
within a processor if the processor participates in 
member level settlement. 


Frequency 
Daily 
Availability 
Available through Global File Transfer and Mastercard 
Operational Reports on Mastercard Connect. 


NOTE: This report is activity driven. If a fee does not have activity, it is not shown. There is also a 
month end version of this report (Monthly Control Report [SWCHM363]).

Table 1353: Daily Direct Settlement Balancing Summary Report (SWCHD364) 


Report Description 
This report provides summary detail in the designated 
settlement currency of the acquirer or issuer. It is 
produced by settlement ICA and currency type and 
summed on all financial total fields. 


The report includes: 


• 
Approved, pending, and resolved inbound 
presentment records for S.A.M. and Single 
Message System. 
• 
Approved, pending, and resolved inbound 
representment records for S.A.M. and Single 
Message System. 
• 
Approved, pending, and resolved accepted 
chargeback records for S.A.M. and Single Message 
System. 
• 
Approved, pending, and resolved inbound and 
outbound miscellaneous records for S.A.M. and 
Single Message System. 
Pending items are items that have been settled in 
GCMS but have not been processed in the Single 
Message System such as first and second 
presentments. They are also items processed in the 
Single Message System but not cleared through 
GCMS such as outbound chargebacks and 
outbound miscellaneous fees. The detail for these 
items will be included on the SWCHD537–1 
report. The summary lines on the SWCHD364 
report should balance to the detail lines on the 
SWCHD537–1 report to enable customers to 
track items that are still in transit between GCMS 
and the Single Message System. 
The miscellaneous records totals will reconcile to the 
Debit Mastercard Inbound/Outbound Fee Report 
(SWCHD586-A) and to the Miscellaneous Fee Records 
(1740) record in the 250-byte Batch Data File. 


Frequency 
Daily 
Availability 
Available through Global File Transfer and Mastercard 
Operational Reports on Mastercard Connect. 


NOTE: To aid in daily reconciliation, the summary lines on the enhanced SWCHD364 report are 
intended to balance to the detail lines on the SWCHD537–1 report to enable customers to track items 
in transit between GCMS and the Single Message System.

Daily Interchange Report (SWCHD412) 


The Daily Interchange Report (SWCHD412) assists customers with the reconciliation process by 
providing enhanced fee reporting. 


Table 1355: Daily Interchange Report (SWCHD412) 


Report Description 
This report provides each fee record description 
alphabetically by product and the interchange fee 
record within the product category. Amounts are 
presented in the designated settlement currency of 
the processor. 


The Single Message System divides the Daily 
Interchange Report into three sections: 


• 
Fee description by category 
• 
Transaction volume by category 
• 
Interchange fees for each category 
The report shows all fee counts, separated by 
Financial, Percentage-based, Non-financial, and Nonbillable 
categories. 


The Single Message System segregates this report 
according to acquiring and issuing processor. The 
report page breaks on currency types within 
processors. 


The Net Interchange Summary page lists the 
acquirer’s and issuer’s net interchange fees. The 
information is also listed by acquirer and issuer on the 
Net Settlement Summary page of the Daily Control 
Report (SWCHD363). 


NOTE: This report is activity driven. If a fee does not 
have activity, it is not shown. 


ISIS appearing in the FEE DESCRIPTION field 
identifies the intracurrency transactions. 


Refer to the following table for a description of the 
SWCHD412 report fields. 


Frequency 
Daily 
Availability 
Available through Global File Transfer and Mastercard 
Operational Reports on Mastercard Connect.

Current Day Open Transaction Report (SWCHD537-1) 


The Current Day Open Transaction Report (SWCHD537-1) assists Debit Mastercard direct 
settlement customers with the reconciliation process by providing the detail of current day open 
transactions between the Single Message System and GCMS/S.A.M. 


Table 1358: Current Day Open Transaction Report (SWCHD537-1) 


Report description 
This report provides the detail of all current day 
transactions that have not been settled by GCMS/ 
S.A.M. The Grand Total amount for the current day is 
expected to balance to the Suspense/Open Total on 
the Direct Settlement Balancing Summary 
(SWCHD364) report. The sequence of this report is 
Settlement ICA and then Currency Code, Activity 
Date, Transaction Type, and PAN. 
Frequency 
Daily 
Availability 
Available through Global File Transfer and Operational 
Reports on Mastercard Connect.

Debit Mastercard Inbound/Outbound Fee Report (SWCHD586-A) 


Debit Mastercard Inbound/Outbound Fee Report (SWCHD586-A) 


Debit Mastercard processors can use the Debit Mastercard Inbound/Outbound Fee Report 
(SWCHD586-A) to track and monitor miscellaneous inbound and outbound fees incurred 
through the submission of various fee collection messages. 


Table 1362: Debit Mastercard Inbound/Outbound Fee Report (SWCHD586-A) 


Report description 
Customers must settle all miscellaneous fees and 
charges by use of the IPM Retrieval and Fee 
Collection/1740 message. The fee collection message 
contains the information required for customers to 
process the miscellaneous fees and charges identified 
and is used for several diverse applications. 


The Single Message System generates this report to 
provide a summary detail of Retrieval and Fee 
Collection messages received on the GCMS Debit 
Mastercard inbound and outbound IPM format file. 


This report includes various fee collection types with 
the following message type identifiers and function 
codes: 


• 
Retrieval request fees (1644 MTI-603 FNC) 
• 
Record clearing fees: member and systemgenerated 
(1740 MTI-700/783 FNC) 
• 
Handling Fees: member-generated (1740 
MTI-700, 780-782 FNC) 
• 
Interchange compliance fees: system-generated 
(1740 MTI -783 FNC) 
The Single Message System also will provide a Net 
Fees Report Summary page per processor, which lists 
the combined fee amounts incurred inbound and 
outbound with a Net total of the inbound and 
outbound fee amounts. 


This report is by ICA number within processor number 
order. This report is based upon activity. Therefore, if a 
fee collection type has zero activity, it will not be 
reported. 


Frequency 
Daily 
Availability 
Available through Global File Transfer and Operational 
Reports on Mastercard Connect. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1422

Monthly Control Report (SWCHM363) 


The Single Message System generates the Monthly Control Report (SWCHM363) to validate 
the processor’s monthly net settlement position to the processor’s settlement account. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1427 



Reports and files 
Monthly Control Report (SWCHM363) 


Report Description 
This report is a month-end version of the Daily Control 
Report (SWCHD363). 


This report provides summary detail by transaction 
type within product type and includes: 


• 
Financial quantity for approved and denied 
• 
Financial amount of transaction and fees 
• 
Reversal quantity and net amount of transactions 
and fees 
NOTE: Debit Mastercard preauthorization reversals 
received after the settlement cutoff will display as a 
new line called Non-Same Day, Non-Financial under 
Exception Items in the Summary. There will be a 
count but no dollar amounts. 


The SWCHM363 report was updated to report 
surcharge amount (DE 28) for an acquirer-generated, 
full reversal transaction for both ATM and POS in a 
separate line, beneath the existing lines for ATM and 
POS surcharge on financial transactions. 


The Single Message System currently provides the 
surcharge amount in DE 28 in the following message 
types: 


• 
Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: acquirer-generated 
• 
Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: time-out induced, 
acquirer-generated 
The SWCHM363 report presents the surcharge 
amount on an acquirer-generated, full-reversal 
transaction as: 


• 
ACCESS CHARGE (ATM SUR) REV 
• 
ACCESS CHARGE (POS SUR) REV 
This enhancement does not affect the net settlement 
or total financial settlement amounts. 


The Single Message System provides totals derived 
from the Batch Data File settlement messages for 
acquiring and issuing processors. 


The Net Settlement Summary page lists the net 
settlement of transactions, reversals, and fees 
separated by debit, credit, and net for both the 
acquirer and the issuer. It also provides a final 
combined net settlement disposition for the 
Automated Clearing House System (ACH) and the 
Global Clearing Management System (GCMS).

Table 1364: Monthly Interchange Report (SWCHM412) 


Description 
This report is a month end version of the Daily

Interchange Report into three sections: 


•

•

•

according to acquiring and issuing processor. The Daily

This report is activity driven. If a transaction type has 
“0” activity, it is not shown.

Debit Mastercard Miscellaneous Billing Report (SWCHM501-M) 


Debit Mastercard Miscellaneous Billing Report (SWCHM501-M) 


Debit Mastercard processors can use the Debit Mastercard Miscellaneous Billing Report 
(SWCHM501-M) to track and monitor miscellaneous inbound and outbound fees incurred 
through the submission of various fee collection messages. 


Report description 
This report is a month-end version of the Debit 
Mastercard Inbound/Outbound Fee Report 
(SWCHD586). 


The Single Message System divides this report by 
reason code and ICAs by Processor ID. It lists the 
message text separated by message text and 
associated fee amounts within a reporting month. 
Therefore, if a fee collection type has zero activity, it 
will not be reported. 


Customers must settle all miscellaneous fees and 
charges by use of the IPM Retrieval and Fee 
Collection/1740 message. The fee collection message 
contains the information required for customers to 
process the miscellaneous fees and charges identified 
and is used for several diverse applications. 


The Single Message System generates this report to 
provide a summary detail of Retrieval and Fee 
Collection messages received on the GCMS Debit 
Mastercard inbound and outbound IPM format file. 


This report includes various fee collection types with 
the following Message Type Identifiers and function 
codes: 


• 
Retrieval Request Fees (1644 MTI-603 FNC) 
• 
Record Clearing Fees–member and systemgenerated 
(1740 MTI-700/783 FNC) 
• 
Handling Fees–member-generated (1740 
MTI-700, 780-782 FNC) 
• 
Interchange Compliance Fees–system-generated 
(1740 MTI -783 FNC) 
The Single Message System also will provide a 
summary page per processor, which lists the combined 
fee amounts incurred inbound and outbound with a 
Net total of the inbound and outbound fee amounts 
by processor ID. 


Frequency 
Monthly

Exception Audit Report (SWCHD53) 


Report description 
This report details exception items including 
adjustments, chargebacks, and second presentments. 
The report contains summary totals by product, for all 
the exception items. 


Same day reversals can be found on the SWCHD353 
Reversals report. 


Exception items are included in the customer’s net 
daily settlement and in the Daily Control Report 
(SWCHD363). Exception items do not appear on the 
Transaction Audit Report. 


The Single Message System sequences the 
transactions in reversal code order and segregates the 
report by acquiring and issuing processor. 


Interchange type 2 appearing in the BRAND field 
identifies intracurrency transactions. 


STND appearing in the RESP CODE field identifies 
Stand-In transactions.

The Single Message System generates the Reversals Report (SWCHD353) to provide advice 
reason codes and response codes for same-day Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420 transactions. The 
report contains the original switch serial number for same day reversals. It also includes all 
reversals, including reversals for preauthorizations received after the settlement cut off.

card numbers residing on the Stand-In Account File. 


Table 1369: Account File Updates Report (SWCHD141-1) 


Report description 
This report provides an audit trail of Online File 
Update messages sent to the Mastercard Network by 
the Single Message Transaction Manager or online 
message sending methods. Card number records 
added, changed, or deleted by the Single Message

multiple processors are owned, and then by PAN and 
Switch Date/Time values in ascending order.

Month-to-Date Processing Summary Report (SWCHM06) 


Processors should use the Month-to-Date Processing Summary Report (SWCHM06) to monitor 
their performance rates to help ensure that they comply with network standards and to 
highlight the differences in debit and credit performance. Processors can use this report to 
identify problems such as PIN failures, invalid account selection, format errors, and the need for 
increased cardholder education.

by total debit/credit).

Reports: intracurrency 


Reports: intracurrency 


Intracurrency (ISIS) supports the settlement of local transactions submitted in currencies other 
than U.S. dollars. 


Intracurrency reports overview 


Intracurrency enables participating customers to establish unique interchange fees for their 
intracurrency arrangement transactions and operate on their own holiday schedule. 


Intracurrency transactions are displayed on the reports in the designated currency of the 
intracurrency agreement. The Daily Control Report (SWCHD363) will detail each intracurrency 
settlement currency supported within a processor. Intracurrency agreement detail, settlement 
service information, settlement currency, and country information are reported to further define 
intracurrency financial and interchange totals. 


The Daily Interchange Report (SWCHD412) will also detail interchange information for each 
intracurrency processor by the designated settlement currency. Detail transaction interchange 
counts and amounts will be reported on the SWCHD412 report. 


Related intracurrency reports are detailed in the following table. These reports enable 
customers to research, identify and reconcile transactions, fees, and their net settlement as 
reported in their 1740 IPM settlement record. 


Intracurrency transactions are identified by the BRAND field on the report. The third position of 
this field will contain a 2 to uniquely identify the intracurrency transactions. 


In the Asia/Pacific and Latin America and the Caribbean regions, Mastercard will not generate 
Fee Collection/1740-783 messages within the T112 or T140 bulk files for Single Message 
intracurrency activity. Refer to the intracurrency settlement advisement, which lists an input 
source of SMS for said activity. 


Table 1375: Intracurrency-related reports

Purpose

has processed all exception items.

Reports: Stand-In 


Stand-In reports assist processors in monitoring their system’s percentage of availability, 
withdrawal limits, usage counts, and card statuses for all transactions the Single Message 
System routed to Stand-In during periods the processor was unavailable. 


Stand-In reports overview 


There are two types of Stand-In reports. 


• 
Single Message Transaction Manager database file reports: These reports provide the status 
information of the Premium Card file and the Hot Card file records: 
– 
PREMIUM is any Mastercard® card selected by the customers to receive higher withdrawal 
limits and usage counts for the individual Premium accounts during Stand-In activity. They 
are listed in the Account File with an entry reason code value of "V". 
– 
A Hot Card is a card being used on an account on which excessive purchasing is taking 
place. This may indicate a lost or stolen card or other unauthorized purchasing. 
• 
Stand-In Transaction report (SWCHD149): This report provides the details of financial 
transaction activity during Stand-In Authorization. It is documented on the following pages. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Daily Processor Up Time Report (MS1100BB) 


Daily Processor Up Time Report (MS1100BB) 


The Single Message System generates the Daily Processor Up Time Report (Settlement Date) 
(MS1100BB) daily for all issuing processors. The report displays processor activity by settlement 
cut-off time. This is broken down by hour and settlement date. 


Table 1377: Report details 


Report description 
This report provides summary availability data for 
each hour of that settlement period. If a processor 
settles at 15:00 (CT) daily, then the details are from 


15:00 (CT) of the first day until 14:00 (CT) of the next 
day. The report displays the date that the Single 
Message System job processed (Process Date) and 
the date of the data/work that was processed (Work 
of). This is displayed in the MM/DD/YYYY format. 
Since the data covers a 24-hour period, the report is 
broken down to cover the starting and ending dates 
for the data. 
The top section of the report describes: 


• 
Who the processor is 
• 
The processor ID (processor number) 
• 
The processor country 
• 
The processor region 
• 
The business entity the processor is associated 
with 
The next section identifies: 


• 
Number of approved transactions 
• 
Denied transactions 
• 
Comm-related time-outs (network communication 
errors) 
• 
Non-comm-related time-outs (RC 91, RC91(s) and 
RC96 errors) 
• 
Total transactions 
• 
Stand-In transactions 
• 
Up time percentage 
• 
Downtime percentage 
The last line is a total of all transactions for the 24hour 
period displayed and the calculated percentages 
for the up and down times. 


Frequency 
Daily

Reports: Asia/Pacific regional 


This section provides a description of the Asia/Pacific regional reports included in the MDS 
Report Transmission File. 


Region and country reports overview 


Regional reports are available through Global File Transfer. The Single Message System 
transmits reports through Global File Transfer to processors at the end of each settlement day. 


All reports are available through Operational Reports, accessible through Mastercard Connect® 
. 
Customers with access can view the online Single Message System reports using their billing 
ICA. The online reports are available for viewing in Operational Reports for a period of 13 
months from the original date of publication. 


NOTE: The Single Message System provides customers all reports described in this section. Customers 
can contact a Customer Implementation Services (CIS) Specialist or their regional representative for 
information about these reports. All report data in this section is fictitious and does not reflect the 
activity of actual processors.

Corporate card addendum data 


Corporate card addendum data 


This appendix describes the corporate card addendum data submitted by acquirers on 
Mastercard Corporate Cards for those Debit Mastercard issuers that request to receive 
corporate card transaction data. It is available in the 250-byte Batch Data File. 


Overview 


The Single Message System provides addendum data submitted by acquirers on Mastercard 
Corporate Card ® to Debit Mastercard® issuers that request to receive corporate card 
transaction data. This service is optional for all Debit Mastercard® issuers that issue 
Mastercard Corporate Card ® 
. 


Corporate card data 


The corporate card data information is available in the 250-byte Batch Data File. 
This data is included in: 


• 
Passenger Transport Detail (General Ticket Information) 
• 
Passenger Transport Detail (Trip Leg Data) 
• 
Passenger Transport Detail (Rail Data) 
• 
Vehicle Rental Detail 
• 
Lodging Summary 
• 
Temporary Services 
• 
Shipping/Courier Services 
• 
Corporate Card Common Data 
• 
Corporate Line Item Detail addendum records 
Corporate card addendum records 


The Corporate Card Addendum records are contained in the 250-byte Batch Data File in 40 
record segments. The corporate card addenda allows issuers to assess spending and make 
better decisions by providing rich, accurate, and timely data. The corporate card addendum data 
also allows issuers to streamline spending and control costs for greater efficiency. The 
addendum records listed below are followed by the number of associated segments. 


These segments are: 


• 
Passenger Transport Detail: General Ticket Information (3) 
• 
Passenger Transport Detail: Trip Leg Data (2) 
• 
Passenger Transport Detail: Rail Data (2) 
• 
Vehicle Rental Detail (4) 
• 
Lodging Summary (5) 
• 
Temporary Services (5) 
• 
Shipping/Courier Services (12)

Reports and files 
Corporate card addendum data tables 


• 
Corporate Card Common Data (4) 
• 
Corporate Line Item Detail (3) 
Corporate card addendum data tables 


The addendum data tables represent the addendum data reflected in the addendum records 
listed above. This information is available in the 250-byte Batch Data File. 


In the following tables, PDS and subfield names are listed in the description column and in the 
IPM PDS No./Subfield column. The IPM PDS number is listed before the “/” with the associated 
subfield number listed after the “/.” 


Subfield names are indented and listed below the associated PDS description. Their 
corresponding “Position” and “Attribute” values are enclosed in parenthesis. If adding Attribute 
values, add only the PDS attribute. The sum of the PDS subfield attributes will equal the PDS 
attribute value. 


Passenger Transport Detail General Ticket Information (GTxx) 


This message supports ticketing transactions for airline, railway, and travel agency transactions 
to provide passenger ticket information for the cardholder. Acquirers may submit one occurrence 
of this message for each airline, railway, or travel agency transaction to provide general ticket 
information. This message is optional.

Passenger Transport Detail Trip Leg Data (TLxx) 


This message supports ticketing transactions for airline, railway, and travel agency transactions 
to provide detailed itinerary information for the cardholder. This message is optional. 


Acquirers may submit 1–998 occurrences of this message. Each occurrence provides detailed 
itinerary data for one trip leg associated with an airline, railway, or travel agency transaction. If 
this addendum detail describes an airline itinerary, the City of Origin/Airport Code, and City of 
Destination/Airport Code then each trip leg should contain an Airport Code from the Official 
Airline Guide (OAG). This document contains a list of standard airport and airline service 
abbreviations.

Vehicle Rental Detail (VRxx) Record 


This message provides detailed vehicle rental information for the cardholder. This message is 


optional. 


One occurrence of this message provides rental agreement reporting for a single vehicle rental 
transaction. This message may be provided in a single occurrence such as one transaction for a 
single vehicle rental, or in multiple occurrences such as one transaction for the rental of multiple 
vehicles.

Lodging Summary (LSxx) Record 


This message provides detailed information about lodging accommodations and related 
expenses for the cardholder. This message is optional. 


One occurrence of this message provides lodging accommodation reporting for a single lodging 
folio, such as a single stay at a lodging facility with one check-in and one check-out. 


The following five segments are listed in this record: LS01, LS02, LS03, LS04, and LS05.

Temporary Services (TSxx) Record 


The Temporary Services detail addendum provides detailed information regarding the billing for 
services rendered on a temporary or contract basis. This record is optional. 


The message layout provides information such as the employee job performed, timekeeping, and 
billing rates. 


Temporary Services (TS01) Record segment 1 


The following five segments are listed in this record: TS01, TS02, TS03, TS04, and TS05.

Shipping/Courier Services (SSxx) Record 


The Shipping/Courier Service detail addendum provides detailed information regarding delivery 
or courier services. This record is optional. 


The message layout supports the shipping and delivery tracking information.

SS07, SS08, SS09, SS10, SS11, and SS12.

Corporate Card Common Data Requirements (CDxx) Record 


The Financial Detail Addendum (Corporate Card Common Data Requirements) message may 
be provided with any transaction in which one of the corporate card products is used. This record 
is optional. 


If a Mastercard Corporate Purchasing Card or other corporate program or service is used for 
airline, railway, lodging, or vehicle rental, those industry-specific addendum messages may be 
submitted in addition to the Corporate Card Common Data Requirements message. If the 
transaction is a business-to-business purchase, customers may provide up to 998 occurrences of 
the Financial Detail Addendum (Corporate Line Item Detail) message in addition to the 
Financial Detail Addendum (Corporate Card Common Data Requirements). 


Corporate Card Common Data Requirements (CD01) Record segment 1 


The following four segments are listed in this record: CD01, CD02, CD03, and CD04.

Corporate Line Item Detail (LIxx) Record 


When a corporate card (such as Mastercard Corporate Purchasing Card® or Mastercard 
Corporate Fleet Card®) is used in a business-to-business purchase, any line item detail related to 
the purchase is presented via 1–998 occurrences of the Financial Detail Addendum (Corporate 
Line Item Detail) message (Usage Code 98, Industry Record Number 950). This record is 
optional. 


One of these messages is submitted for each occurrence of line item data in the transaction. 


Corporate Line Item Detail (LI01) Record segment 1 


The following three segments are listed in this record: LI01, LI02, and LI03.

Processors connected to the Single Message System through the Mastercard Network 


Settlement 


Settlement is the process by which Mastercard® facilitates the exchange of funds on behalf of its 
customers that have sent or received financial transactions through a clearing system. 


Some of the important financial transactions are included in this process, including: 


• 
Collaboration (merchant refund) 
NOTE: This is the same refund process when the acquirer issues a refund. No new process is being utilized 
for merchant refunds. 


• 
Presentments from acquirer to issuer 
• 
Chargebacks from issuer to acquirer 
• 
Fee collections (sender and receiver fees depend on the message reason code and include 
transactions sent from Mastercard to the customer) 
• 
Bill payments, such as RPPS 
• 
Others, such as reversals. 
The exchange of successfully processed detailed financial transaction data through a clearing system 
represents an obligation to exchange funds. To facilitate the settlement of funds, Mastercard uses 
the Global Clearing Management System (GCMS) system—a Windows®–based, Client–server 
software application designed to streamline the process of moving funds. 


• 
Transaction amounts and all other transaction and interchange charges processed through the 
clearing systems 
• 
Cash disbursement and ATM cash disbursement accommodation fees, and 
• 
Billing items submitted by the Mastercard Consolidated Billing System (MCBS) to the clearing 
systems, the Settlement Account Management (S.A.M.) system, or both. 
The process by which Mastercard facilitates the exchange of funds on behalf of its customers and the 
distinct components of the process are referred to herein as Mastercard Settlement. 


The GCMS creates the Financial Position Detail/1644 reconciliation message that confirms each 
sending customer’s accepted retrieval fulfillment fees. 


The issuer may collect a USD 25 (EUR 25) handling fee if the retrieval request fulfillment or TID 
provided with the second presentment verifies an incorrect merchant name, location, or transaction 
date. When collecting a handling fee, the issuer must submit a Fee Collection/1740 message with 
message reason code 7612. 


Processors connected to the Single Message System through 
the Mastercard Network 


Each customer processing system that is connected to the Single Message System through an 
online Customer Interface Specification (CIS) interface to the Mastercard Network receives 
Integrated Product Messages (IPM) clearing data reflecting settlement data in accordance with 
standard Mastercard procedures.

Processors connected directly to the Single Message System 


Processors connected directly to the Single Message System 


Each customer that is connected directly to the Single Message System must perform clearing 
and settlement determination processing in accordance with the procedures established by the 
Single Message System. 


Reconciliation 


The Single Message System provides reconciliation data for customers through batch detail 
transmission files (raw data files) and various Single Message System transaction detail reports 
(pre-formatted bulk file reports). 


Mastercard encourages customers to develop an automated process to compare batch detail 
files (generated and transmitted by the Single Message System) to internal batch records 
(maintained by the processor). 


The automated compare process will highlight any balancing differences, which the customer 
can research using Single Message System reports. Each customer is responsible for a daily 
reconciliation of its internal batch totals to the settlement totals provided by the Single 
Message System. 


Single Message System settlement service options 


These sections describe the settlement service options that are available in the Single Message 
System settlement process. 


Direct settlement is the mandated, standard settlement process for Debit Mastercard issuers. 


For specific information about settlement service types, refer to the Settlement Manual on 
Mastercard Connect™ 
. 


Regional settlement 


The regional settlement option is available to Maestro® Cirrus® and Debit Mastercard® 
processors, acquirers, and issuers. Every processor, acquirer, and issuer must participate in a 
regional settlement service. In the defined regional service, settlement can be either in U.S. 
dollars or a local currency supported by Mastercard. 


Automated clearing house (ACH): 


ACH is a nationwide electronic funds transfer system. 
ACH is: 


• 
Available to Maestro and Cirrus processors, acquirers, and issuers. 
• 
Only available for settlement in U.S. dollars at a U.S. bank.

Intracurrency settlement 


Intracurrency settlement 


The Single Message System settles intracurrency (ISIS) through the Global Clearing 
Management System (GCMS) allowing settlement in the currency of the intracurrency 
arrangement instead of USD for both credit and debit card programs. The Single Message 
System also has the ability to use the Mastercard Settlement Account Management (S.A.M.) 
system for intracurrency settlement. All countries with ISIS agreements in Single Message settle 
through GCMS except for Brazil which uses the direct S.A.M. service. 


Overview 


The Single Message System settles intracurrency (ISIS) through the Global Clearing 
Management System (GCMS) allowing settlement in the currency of the intracurrency 
arrangement instead of USD for both credit and debit card programs. The Single Message 
System also has the ability to use the Mastercard Settlement Account Management (S.A.M.) 
system for intracurrency settlement. All countries with ISIS agreements in Single Message settle 
through GCMS except for Brazil which uses the direct S.A.M. service. 


This requirement is applicable for all intracountry activity for the Cirrus® Maestro® and Debit 
Mastercard® brands. 


The Mastercard intracurrency functionality supports the settlement of local transactions 
submitted in currencies other than U.S. dollars and allows its customers to choose their own 
settlement currency and interchange rates. Debit intracurrency supports multiple intracurrency 
settlement currencies within a country. Debit intracurrency is applicable only to products, 
qualified by Mastercard. 


At least one acquirer and one issuer must participate in the intracurrency settlement 
arrangement. Each intracurrency settlement service will net to zero (that is, debits equal 
credits) in the payment currency for each settlement date.

Customer impact 


Customer impact 


The Mastercard Global Settlement Operations department will arrange a local banking 
relationship to effect payments for intracurrency settlement processing. Mastercard will 
designate a local settlement bank for this purpose. 


Mastercard can require customers (issuers and acquirers) to open settlement accounts at the 
designated settlement bank, though whenever possible, the local interbank payment process 
will be used. Refer to the Settlement manual for specific requirements for each settlement 
service. Acquirers and issuers must agree on a settlement currency. The interchange rate can be 
selected in U.S. dollars, and the Mastercard Network will perform the conversion to the local 
currency of the intracurrency agreement. 


Mastercard will include the interchange rates in the system once all participation requirements 
are fulfilled. All participating customers must have a valid ICA established in GCMS for 
settlement to occur. 


Customers/processors participating in debit intracurrency must verify their host is capable of 
handling a value of 2 in subfield 2 (Interchange Rate Indicator), of DE 63 (Network Data). In 
addition, customers must verify they can accept the same values in DE 49 (Currency Code, 
Transaction), and DE 50 (Currency Code Settlement), for all identified intracurrency 
transactions. 


Customers must enhance their reconciliation systems to balance to the Daily Control report, 
(SWCHD363). This report balances to the net settlement amount in the GCMS Fee Collection/ 
1740 miscellaneous records in the T112 file. 


All intracurrency exception item processing can be done via Single Message Transaction 
Manager.

Debit Intracurrency Recommendations and Requirements 


• 
Mastercard recommends implementing credit intracurrency first if a debit intracurrency 
project includes Authorization Request/0100 messages for credit card issuers. 
• 
At least one issuer and one acquirer must participate in an intracurrency arrangement. 
• 
Mastercard has an assigned ICA number for each intracurrency arrangement. This ICA 
number is the sending ICA number for settlement records. 
• 
Customers must agree on the in-country interchange fees (either Single Message System 
default interchange fee in their local currency or a different amount in local currency,

Cirrus, Maestro, or Debit Mastercard transactions eligible for 
intracurrency settlement 


For a Cirrus, Maestro, or Debit Mastercard transaction to be eligible for intracurrency 
settlement: 


• 
both the issuer and acquirer must participate in the same intracurrency arrangement, and 
• 
the settlement currency of the issuer and acquirer must be the same as the settlement 
currency of the intracurrency arrangement. 
Transactions performed at ATMs that dispense multiple currencies are deemed intracurrency 
transactions when: 


• 
the currency code assigned to the card issuer is equal to the dispensed currency code 
provided by the acquirer in the online message, 
• 
both currency codes are reflective of the currency of the intracurrency arrangement, and 
• 
If the local currency is not supported in a regional settlement service, participation in the 
intracurrency service, if available, is required. 
Intracurrency features 


These items are features of the debit intracurrency settlement program. Customers will: 


• 
Designate a single settlement currency for the intracurrency arrangement. Mastercard 
settles all intracurrency transactions in the specified currency of the intracurrency 
arrangement. 
• 
Participate in ISO 8583-1987 CIS Authorization/01xx and Single Message System Financial 
Transaction/02xx message formats. 
• 
With a debit-only ICA number, receive separate settlement advisements in the currency of 
the intracurrency arrangement for intracurrency transactions. Customers that do not have a 
debit-only ICA, will receive settlement advisements with combined debit and credit activity. 
• 
Define an interchange rate structure. 
• 
Receive separate summary-level reporting of intracurrency settlement positions, by issuer 
and acquirer. 
• 
Need to open settlement accounts at a designated settlement bank if an issuer or acquirer. 
• 
Receive settlement advisements in the currency of the intracurrency arrangement. 
NOTE: Mastercard must approve the local settlement bank selected by the customer. The customer 
must use the same settlement bank for both debit and credit intracurrency settlement if they are 
processing credit at the ATM or Debit Mastercard transactions.

Intracurrency benefits 


Intracurrency benefits 


Participating in the debit intracurrency program offers these benefits for customers. 


• 
May reduce customer costs associated with foreign exchange risk, because of the floating of 
local currency against the dollar. The local settlement bank facilitates payment between the 
issuer and acquirer in the local settlement currency 
• 
Supports flexible interchange rates that are determined by participants 
• 
Supported by the ISO 8583 message format 
• 
Supports the display of all Cirrus, Debit Mastercard, and Maestro intracurrency transactions 
in Single Message Transaction Manager 
Debit intracurrency online processing 


Mastercard provides debit card processing support for several Mastercard programs and 
identifies the transactions eligible for intracurrency settlement. 


Intracurrency transactions are determined by comparing the currency code of the card issuer on 
the Mastercard database with that of the dispensed currency code provided by the acquirer in 
the online authorization request message. The bank identification number (BIN) identifies the 
issuer as an intracurrency participant, and the Institution Definition File (IDF) identifies the 
acquirer as an intracurrency participant. 


Mastercard provides debit card processing support for several Mastercard programs including 
Mastercard® Cirrus® ATM Network, Debit Mastercard® and the Maestro® point-of-sale debit 
program and identifies the transactions eligible for intracurrency settlement. 


Mastercard applies an interchange rate, in the local currency, with the intracurrency transaction, 
and the amount is included in the intracurrency settlement for that customer. 


Clearing/settlement flow for Debit Mastercard 


The Single Message System will create a force post message (Financial Transaction Advice/ 
0220) for each individual presentment message submitted by the acquirer. 


The Single Message System will then brand the Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message as 
intracurrency settlement by including the value 2 in the third position of DE 63. Also DE 49 and 
DE 50 will have the same currency code. 


The Financial Transaction Advice/0220 message from the Single Message System should be 
treated as a clearing message, indicating that the issuer can clear the preauthorization and 
settle to the cardholder. 


Issuers can get Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages for all six clearing cycles depending 
on whether a presentment is presented from the acquirer for each cycle.

Data element definitions 


Intracurrency Settlement affects DE 49 (Currency Code, Transaction), DE 50 (Currency Code, 
Settlement), DE 63 (Network Data), and DE 126 (Switch Private Data). 


Debit intracurrency offline processing 


The offline process calculates the interchange fees for intracurrency transactions and reports 
them through a batch file. 


Intracurrency interchange 


Mastercard calculates all interchange. Customers in an intracurrency arrangement can 
determine the interchange rate of the intracurrency arrangement. 


Mastercard calculates all interchange. Fee Collection/1740 records are created and sent to 
GCMS for the creation of settlement. These amounts are included in the customer’s daily Global 
Clearing Management System (GCMS) settlement records. The Intracurrency Daily Control 
Report (SWCHD363), and the Daily Interchange Report (SWCHD412) provide a summary of 
the intracurrency interchange. 


Customers in an intracurrency arrangement can determine the interchange rate of the 
intracurrency arrangement. Mastercard uses these interchange rates for Cirrus® Maestro® 
Debit Mastercard® and Mastercard ATM transactions that qualify for intracurrency settlement. 
When customers agree upon an interchange rate, Mastercard applies that rate to all 
intracurrency transactions. Zero interchange is a valid option for intracurrency transactions. 
International interchange will remain at the current standard rate. 


Local interchange 


To establish local interchange, customers must contact their regional office representative. 


If the customer selects the default option, Mastercard will apply the standard interchange rate 
for international transactions. Mastercard then converts the international rate to the currency 
of the intracurrency arrangement.

Settlement and Reconciliation 
Settlement service 


Settlement service 


Mastercard settlement service options permit customers to settle in multiple currencies within a 
single business day, allowing customers to customize their settlement based on their individual 
activity. 


This settlement functionality allows Mastercard to respond to regional transaction processing 
requirements at different times of day. 


Mastercard determines the settlement service according to information contained in the 
transaction. The Single Message System derives the settlement date from the settlement 
service and populates this information in DE 15 (Date Settlement). Mastercard then forwards 
the transaction on to the issuer for approval. 


Mastercard provides balancing reports for each settlement service, once a day at end of day. 
Mastercard continues to provide all other reporting and detail transactions once a day at end of 
day. 


NOTE: Customers can participate in more than one settlement service agreement. 


Settlement advisement 


Customers can request a settlement advisement to facilitate their settlement reconciliation. 
Advisements are not automatically generated and transmitted to a customer if they participate 
in an intracurrency service. 


Customers must designate the method of transmission and destination for receipt of a 
customer advisement. 


If requested, each customer participating in an intracurrency arrangement receives a separate 
advisement for intracurrency settlement. Mastercard sends the advisement to the participating 
customer after each settlement cutoff per currency. The advisement shows the net debit or 
credit in the currency of the intracurrency arrangement. Refer to the Settlement Manual for a 
sample advisement. 


If the customer uses the same ICA number for debit and credit intracurrency settlement, the 
advisement will contain a combined net position. 


Mastercard also sends a transfer funds order to the intracurrency Local Settlement Bank to 
initiate the settlement process. Customers in an net debit position can be required to push funds 
to the Local Settlement Bank if direct debit is not offered, see the Settlement Manual for direct 
debit options. The daily positions of all customers participating, when summed together, should 
net to zero.

Intracurrency settlement bank holidays 


Customers participating in an intracurrency arrangement settle their intracurrency transactions 
according to the holiday schedule of their intracurrency local settlement bank. 


These customers should work with the Regional Office and Mastercard Central Site to establish 
a list of settlement bank holidays. 


NOTE: U.S. dollar funds are settled Monday through Friday, except for U.S. Federal Reserve holidays. 
Participants in a credit and debit intracurrency arrangement must agree to the same Local Settlement 
Bank holidays.

MLS supports issuers and acquirers that process ATM and POS transactions.

Customer impact

Technical description 


This topic outlines the technical specifications for member level settlement. 


Processors that have multiple customers processing behind them have the option of having 
settlement occur at an ICA level rather than at a processor level. MLS is beneficial for processors 
that do not want to take the financial responsibility of settlement for their down-stream 
customers. 


Mastercard settlement reports and the raw data file are sent at a processor level, but the net 
settlement amount is sent at an individual ICA level. MLS is available only for customers that 
participate in the S.A.M. system. Each individual customer needs to be set up in S.A.M. for 
settlement with a valid ICA number. 


NOTE: For customers that settle in currencies other than 840 (USD), the settlement file will be sent 
directly to S.A.M., and no Miscellaneous Fee/1740 record will be provided. 


Each customer will be set up with a unique routing and transit number. 


The following topics describe technical impacts to acquirers and issuers, and Single Message 
System transaction processing requirements to support Member Level Settlement processing. 


For specific questions not covered in this document, please contact your Mastercard Regional 
Office representative. 


Message layouts 


In GCMS the format of the IPM Fee Collection/1740 message within the IPM T112 bulk file will 
not change. However, Mastercard will forward multiple IPM Fee Collection/1740 messages in 
the GCMS file (an IPM Fee Collection/1740 message for each corresponding customer identified 
by ICA) if participating in GCMS settlement. 


If the customer is participating in multiple currency settlement, the customer will not receive 
IPM Fee Collection/1740 messages.

Data element definitions 


MLS does not require the use of any new data elements. For settlement to occur correctly at a 
customer/ICA level, it is important for the correct routing and transit number to be present in 
DE 32 (Acquiring Institution Identification Code), in the online acquiring message from the 
processor. 


Routing and transit numbers: Institution Definition File (IDF) 


A unique routing and transit number identifies each corresponding customer participating in 
MLS. 


After flagging a transaction as an MLS transaction, based on an internal edit in the Single 
Message System. Mastercard refers to the routing and transit number (contained in DE 32) 
when obtaining the settlement data for that ICA. 


BIN modification: Institution Routing Table (IRT) 


Processors must know their individual customer’s routing and transit number to apply it 
correctly to the online message and to process the settlement reports. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1653 



Settlement and Reconciliation 
Reports 


Reports 


Member Level Settlement processors will receive a daily report that provides a transaction 
summary at an ICA level, and a bulk file that is created and sent to the processor containing the 
net settlement amount for that ICA. 


Member Level Settlement processors will receive a Daily Control Report, (SWCHD363), that 
provides a transaction summary at an ICA level, and an IPM T112 Bulk file that is created and 
sent to the processor. This file will contain the net settlement amount for that ICA. Customers 
settling multiple currency settlement through S.A.M. will see their settlement amount on their 
Net Settlement Advisement. 


Processors that implement Member Level Settlement must be able to reconcile with the Daily 
Control Report (SWCHD363). This report provides information at an institution level (routing 
and transit number). Processors can use the data from this report to settle with their downstream 
customers. Even though Mastercard provides the processor with the reports and bulk 
files, settlement occurs at an ICA level. The MLS product enables the processor to process 
transactions but financially settle at an individual customer level. Single Message System does 
not provide settlement reporting to the individual down-stream ICA for reconciliation purposes. 
It is the responsibility of the processor to provide the information to the downstream ICAs. 


Processors implementing MLS also can participate in intracurrency settlement agreements. 
Intracurrency settlement flags will be set up at the institution and routing number level. 


Settlement of intracurrency transactions will occur at the customer level (routing and transit), 
not at the processor level. Intracurrency settlement transactions will be reported at a summary 
level at the settlement ICA level rather than at a processor level. The Daily Control Report, 
(SWCHD363) contains intracurrency and non-intracurrency settlement transactions. 


Intracurrency settlement agreements are not currently supported in multiple currency 
settlement processing. 


Bulk files 


The processor will receive 


• 
the T461 report bulk file type received in the production environment (T467 in the test 
environment) and 
• 
the T464 data bulk file type received in the production environment (T470 in the test 
environment) 
when participating in member-level settlement. 
Member-level settlement has no effect on the format of these bulk files. 


Single Message Transaction Manager 


Customers can use the Institution Routing table to view system setup information for specific 
routing and transit numbers.

How to participate 


Customers are required to send a letter or e-mail message to the Customer Implementation

Contact a Customer Implementation Services Specialist or your regional representative for 
information about how to participate in member-level settlement processing. 


MLS implementation process 


These steps describe the process to implement MLS. 


1. 
Mastercard updates its database to enable MLS for all the processor’s participating 
customers. 
2. 
Mastercard validates the ICA. 
3. 
Mastercard will report all activity on the Daily Control report (SWCHD363). 
A Customer Implementation Services specialist will monitor the production performance for 30 
days after migration to production. 


Multiple currency settlement and reporting 


This section explains that customers can receive online transactions and reports in their local 
settlement currency. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1655 



Settlement and Reconciliation 
Overview 


Overview 


Multiple currency processing allows customers to settle their activity in any regional settlement 
currency supported by Mastercard, independent of the settlement currency of the other parts to 
the transaction. 


For example, customers that settle their activity in Australian dollars will see Australian dollars 
reflected in their settlement online messages, reports, and 250-byte Batch Data File, regardless 
of transaction currency. 


Applies to

With multiple currency processing, settlement positions calculated by Mastercard will no longer 


be submitted to GCMS via the Fee Collection/1740 message. Instead, the Single Message 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1656 



Settlement and Reconciliation 
Customer impact 


System will feed the settlement position directly to the Mastercard Settlement Account 
Management (S.A.M.) system, eliminating the need for the Fee Collection/1740 message. 


NOTE: Customers that participate in an intracurrency agreement will continue to receive a Fee 
Collection/ 1740 message for their intracurrency settlement activities. 


The Single Message System will send the settlement position directly to S.A.M. in the customer’s 
settlement currency, thereby possibly preventing an occurrence of currency conversion. The 
currency that issuers choose for settlement can be set up at the processor, institution, or BIN 
level. 


Mastercard converts non-U.S. dollar transaction amounts to base U.S. dollars and then to the 
issuer’s settlement currency and the acquirer’s settlement currency, if different than the 
transaction currency. 


Refer to Currency conversion in this manual for information about currency conversion 
calculations. 


For more information about multi-currency processing support, contact your regional 
representative. 


Customer impact 


Support of multiple currency processing is optional for both acquirers and issuers. Acquirers and 
issuers that support multiple currency processing will be affected as follows. 


Acquirer impact 


Acquirers can choose to receive their online transactions, applicable reports, and the 250-byte 
Batch Data File in their chosen settlement currency. 


Issuer impact 


Issuers can choose to receive their online transactions, the 250-byte Batch Data File, and 
applicable reports in their chosen settlement currency. Issuers also can receive their cardholder 
billing amounts in the cardholder’s currency in their online messages. The cardholder billing 
currency is the currency of the BIN as defined by Mastercard. 


Technical description 


These topics describe technical impacts to acquirers and issuers, as well as Single Message 
System transaction processing required to support multiple currency processing. 


Data element definitions 


This data element information applies to multiple currency transaction processing through the 
Single Message System. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1657 



Settlement and Reconciliation 
Reports 


• 
The value in DE 50 (Currency Code, Settlement) in an online message specifies the 
settlement currency chosen by the message recipient. DE 5 (Amount, Settlement) contains 
the amount in the currency designated by DE 50. 
• 
The value in DE 49 (Currency Code, Transaction) in an online message specifies the currency 
used for the transaction. DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) contains the amount of the currency 
designated by DE 49. 
– 
If the value in DE 49 is not U.S. dollars, the Single Message System converts the 
transaction amount in DE 4 to a base amount in U.S. dollars, and then using the base 
amount applies the appropriate conversion rate to calculate the settlement position in DE 
5. 
– 
If the value in DE 49 is U.S. dollars, the Single Message System uses the transaction 
amount as the base amount for calculating the settlement position in DE 5. 
• 
The value in DE 5 in an online message to the issuer includes the settlement amount plus any 
applicable fees 
• 
The value in DE 51 (Currency Code, Cardholder Billing) in an online message contains the 
currency code that specifies the currency that the issuer uses to bill the cardholder. DE6 
(Amount, Cardholder Billing) contains the amount in the currency designated by DE 51. 
– 
When the value in DE 51 is different from the transaction currency code value in DE 49, 
the Single Message System converts the transaction amount in DE 4 to a base amount in 
U.S. dollars and then to the cardholder’s billing amount in DE 6. 
– 
When the value in DE 51 is the same as the transaction currency code value in DE 49, the 
cardholder’s billing amount in DE 6 is the same as the transaction amount 
NOTE: Intracurrency transaction processing is not affected. 


Reports 


The Daily Control Report (SWCHD363) and Daily Interchange Report (SWCHD412) are 
affected by multiple currency processing. 


Settlement amounts 


For customers that participate in the Multiple Currency Settlement and Reporting service, all 
reports will reflect settlement amounts in the customer’s chosen settlement currency. 


The chosen settlement amount will be displayed wherever “Amount Settlement” or “Original 
Settlement Amount” occurs in a given report. 


The processor will receive the relevant settlement value. For example, as an acquirer, the 
processor will receive the “Acquirer Settlement Amount.” 


The following reports will reflect settlement in the customer’s chosen settlement currency for 
those customers participating in the Multiple Currency Processing service:

Settlement advisements 


Advisements are created and delivered to customers via S.A.M., and a Settlement report is 
available to facilitate customers balancing to S.A.M. advisements. 


Customers are provided with documentation that clearly describes the differences between 
current reporting and S.A.M. advisements. If the previous source of the advisements was not 
S.A.M., customers are notified six months in advance about the advisement layout and are 
provided a sample. 


Mastercard eService allows licensed users to access transfer agent and customer advisements 
online. Each user needs to be set up to receive settlement advisements via Mastercard eService 
using the settlement ICA number. This can be done by going to Mastercard Connect™ and 
submitting an eService Settlement Advisement product request form.

Participate in the multiple currency processing service 


To participate in the multiple currency processing service, customers must register. 


Multiple currency processing service registration process 


A Net Settlement Information Form (NSIF) (Form 339) must be completed to sign up for the 
Multiple Currency Settlement and Reporting service. Customers and processors must follow all 
applicable Mastercard rules and procedures to submit this form. 


NOTE: Only customers that participate in a Regional settlement service are eligible to participate in 
the Multiple Currency Settlement and Reporting service. 


Customers that want to change their current settlement currency from U.S. dollars to one of 
the settlement currencies supported by Mastercard must submit a Net Settlement Information 
Form (NSIF) (Form 339) to the Global Customer Care group in Mastercard. Refer to the 
Settlement Manual for a complete listing of regional settlement currencies and their 
corresponding currency codes supported by Mastercard. 


A new customer that wants to take advantage of this service must submit an NSIF to the 
Mastercard Customer Integration Team. 


Contact a Customer Implementation Services specialist or your regional representative for 
information about how to participate in multiple currency settlement and reporting.

acquirer and issuer must code their systems to support these fields to leverage such product and 
services in a timely manner in the event of a security issue. 


Allpoint ATM surcharge free program 


The Single Message System supports prepaid issuers who participate in the Allpoint® ATM 


surcharge free program. 


Customer impact 


Issuers with prepaid portfolios that choose to participate in the Allpoint® ATM surcharge-free 
program must be prepared to receive a value of A (Allpoint®) in DE 48 (Additional Data), 
subelement 95 (Mastercard Promotion Code), subfield 1 (Surcharge-Free Alliance) in issuer 
Financial Transaction Request/02xx and Reversal Advice/04xx messages. 


This does not apply to Financial Transaction Advice/0220 Force Post messages and Financial 


Transaction Advice/0220—Debit Mastercard Stand-In messages. 


In addition, issuers that participate must recognize the pricing structure for the eligible 


transactions. 


An eligible surcharge-free ATM transaction must: 


• 
Include DE 63 (Network Data), subfield 2 (Interchange Rate Indicator) with value 0 (U.S. 
Region). 
• 
Include DE 3 (Processing Code), subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type Code) with value of: 
– 
01 (Withdrawal) 
– 
30 (Balance Inquiry) 
• 
Have the acquiring terminal identified as an: Allpoint® participant 
• 
Have the issuer BIN identified in position 71 on the 80-byte Financial Institution Table File 
with a Surcharge-free Program ID value of A (Participates in Allpoint® ATM surcharge-free 
program). 
A transaction that does not meet these requirements will not include DE 48, subelement 95 in 
Financial Transaction Request/0200, Financial Transaction Advice/0220, Financial Transaction 
Request/02xx and Reversal Advice/04xx messages forwarded to the issuer. 


Issuers should contact their Customer Implementation Specialist for registration information for 
the Allpoint® ATM surcharge-free program.

ATM premium listing service 


The ATM premium listing service allows issuers to register cardholder accounts to help ensure 
ATM transactions are not blocked by the Fraud Rule Manager for ATM service, when an account 
is included on the listing service. 


The ATM premium listing service will automatically block any fraud-related chargeback request 
with message reason code 70 (Chargeback-Chip Liability Shift (POS and ATM)) if the PAN is 
listed on the ATM premium and the transaction was not blocked by the Fraud Rule manager for 
ATM. 


Mastercard allows participating issuers to submit PANs to be included in ATM premium listing 
using the File Update Request/0302 message. 


Issuers 


Participating issuers will submit cardholder accounts to the Account Management System using 
value G (ATM Premium List) in File Update Request/0302 messages. 


NOTE: Once a cardholder account number is submitted to the Account Management System to be 
added to the ATM premium listing, an issuer will have to request a deletion from the listing to have it 
removed.

ATM access fees for cross-border transactions 


Acquirers can assess fees on transactions that take place at an ATM located outside the country 
in which the card was issued (cross-border transactions). 


The permission for cross-border transactions applies only under the following conditions: 


• 
Where local laws and regulations do not prohibit the imposition of the fee. 
• 
Any ATM access fee charged on a Mastercard, Maestro, or Cirrus transaction must not be 
greater than any ATM access fee charged by the acquirer in connection with the transactions 
of any other network accepted at that terminal. 
• 
The acquirer applies the ATM access fee in a consistent and nondiscriminatory fashion. 
• 
The ATM access fee must be provided in DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) and DE 28 (Amount, 
Transaction Fee) of the Financial Transaction Request/0200 message. 
Notification of ATM access fee 


An acquirer that plans to add an ATM access fee must notify its sponsoring principal, in writing, 
of its intent to do so before the planned first imposition of such ATM access fee by the acquirer. 
The principal must update the Location Administration Tool (LAT) regarding its or its affiliates’ 
imposition of ATM access fees. 


Cancellation of transaction 


Any acquirer that plans to add an ATM access fee must notify the cardholder with a window 
display that states the ATM access fee policy and provides the cardholder with an option to 
cancel the requested transaction.

The network supports PINs from four to 12 characters long. The encrypted PIN block always is eight

hexadecimal number and working key be provided. DE 52 houses the 16-digit number in the 
customer’s PIN block format.

Direct charging ATM access fee for Australia 


Mastercard has granted acquirers in Australia a waiver from the Mastercard Rules and 


Transaction Processing Rules to support direct charging ATM access fee. 


The Single Message System supports an option for acquirers to charge a fee directly to 
cardholders when cardholders use a card at a foreign ATM other than the issuing institution for 
cash withdrawal, balance inquiry, PIN change, and PIN unblock transactions. 


This direct charging model will convert balance inquiry, PIN change, and PIN unblock 
transactions that were previously non-financial to financial transactions when a fee has been 
applied. The total requested amount of the transaction in DE 4 will include the fee charged 
directly to the cardholder in DE 28 (Amount, Transaction Fee). 


Cardholders will be advised of the fee they will incur while making the transaction at the 
terminal. The cardholder’s issuer will be able to decline a transaction in cases where an overdraft 
can occur. No fees will be imposed for failed or declined transactions. 


In the case of a communication failure, the Single Message System will reverse directly charged 


transactions with an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: system-generated message. 


When a directly charged transaction fails to complete, customers will be allowed to reverse the 
transaction with an Acquirer Reversal Advice/0420: acquirer-generated message. Partial 
reversals of balance inquiries, PIN change, and PIN unblock transactions will be declined. 


The Single Message System will not support chargebacks, representments, or adjustments for 
Balance Inquiry, PIN Change, and PIN Unblock transactions. Improper direct charging fees can 
be disputed via compliance resolution. Please refer to the Chargeback Guide for more 
information.

Customer impact 


Acquirers and issuers that choose to participate in the Direct Charging Access Fee for Australia 
will take the actions described below. 


Acquirers 


Acquirers no longer receive an ATM interchange fee for Australian intracountry transactions. 
Instead, an acquirer has the option to charge another institution’s cardholder a direct ATM 
access fee for Cash Withdrawal, Balance Inquiry, PIN Change, and PIN Unblock transactions 
conducted at its ATM. 


Acquirers that choose to levy an ATM access fee must be prepared to send both the transaction 
amount and direct charging fee in DE 4 (Amount, Transaction) and the direct charging fee 
amount in DE 28 (Amount, Transaction Fee). 


Acquirers that levy a fee must disclose the fee to the cardholder before the transaction occurs 
to ensure the cardholder has an opportunity to cancel the transaction without incurring a fee. 


Issuers 


Issuers no longer will pay an ATM interchange fee for Australian intracountry transactions. 
Instead, cardholders will be charged a fee directly for Cash Withdrawal, Balance Inquiry, PIN 
Change, and PIN Unblock transactions conducted at another institution’s ATM. 


Issuers must be prepared to receive the original transaction amount and the direct charging fee 
in DE 4 (Amount, Transaction), and the direct charging fee amount in DE 28 (Amount, 
Transaction Fee). 


Gambling transaction processing 


The Mastercard Network supports Gaming Payment Transaction processing for the Mastercard 
and Maestro card brands in Europe and Mastercard card brands in Middle East/ Africa region 
countries where the crediting of gambling winnings is permitted by law. The Dual Authorization 
Message System also supports Gaming Payment Transaction processing for the Mastercard and 
Maestro brands in the United States region to transfer lottery winnings to a card. 


U.S. region Mastercard and Maestro issuers must block online gambling transactions in 
accordance with the Standards and applicable U.S. law. Such potentially illegal online gambling 
transactions are declined during Stand-In Authorization processing.

Maestro PIN-less Single Message program 


Mastercard offers a Maestro PIN-less Single Message program. A PIN-less Single Message 
transaction is an option to route electronically read magnetic stripe, contact chip, and 
contactless transactions for less than or equal to USD 100 in the U.S. region. U.S. territories are 
excluded from the program and the issuing and merchant geographies must be in the U.S. 
region. This option is designed for non-Mastercard branded debit cards where Maestro is 
enabled. 


The 80-byte Financial Institution Table File distributed to acquirers will include the Maestro PINless 
Program Indicator in position 63 indicating the account range participates in the PIN-less 
Single Message program. 


Acquirers should only route Maestro PIN-less transactions when the final purchase amount is 
certain at the time of authorization. 


For a point-of-sale (POS) Maestro PIN-less transaction, U.S. region issuers of non-Mastercard 
branded debit cards where Maestro is enabled and their processors must be able to identify and 
approve Maestro PIN-less transactions. Issuers can choose to leverage the PIN-less indicator 
provided by Mastercard in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 81 (Maestro PINless 
Program Indicator) in Financial Request/0200 messages to facilitate identification of these 
transactions. 


To qualify for this program, a PIN-less transaction must meet the criteria defined. 


For the first set of qualifications, the Single Message System will evaluate Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 messages for the following conditions to determine if the transaction qualifies as 
a Maestro PIN-less transaction: 


• 
The BIN qualifies for and participates in the PIN-less Single Message Program. 
• 
The transaction is identified as a purchase transaction indicated by DE 3 (Processing Code), 
subfield 1 (Cardholder Transaction Type) which contains a value 00 (Purchase). 
• 
The transaction is acquired by a U.S. region merchant. 
• 
No PIN is used at the point-of-sale and no PIN data is present in the request DE 52 (Personal 
Identification Number [PIN] Data) or DE 110 (Encryption Data). 
When the above criteria have been met, the Single Message System will evaluate the request 
message further to confirm the following: 


• 
The transaction is face-to-face: DE 61 (Point-of-Service [POS] Data), Subfield 1 (POS 
Terminal Attendance) reflects it is an attended terminal, Subfield 4 (POS Cardholder 
Presence) shows the cardholder is present and Subfield 5 (POS Card Presence) indicates the 
card is present. Card not present transactions are not permitted.
