For transactions that meet all conditions from both sets of criteria, the Single Message System 
will: 


• 
Set DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), Subelement 81 (Maestro PIN-less Program 
Indicator) to value Y (The transaction does qualify as a PIN-less Maestro transaction) 
• 
Include DE 48, subelement 81 in the Financial Request/0200 message only if the issuer has 
configured the relevant account range to participate in the PIN-less Single Message program 
If the first set of criteria is met and any of the second set of conditions is not met, the Single 
Message System will assign to DE 48, subelement 81 the value N (The transaction does not 
qualify as a PIN-less Maestro transaction). 


If the first set of criteria is not met, or if the issuer has not configured the relevant account 
range to participate in the PIN-less Single Message program, the subelement will be excluded 
from the Financial Request/0200 message. 


Mastercard Digital Enablement Service overview 


Mastercard Digital Enablement Service (MDES) is a secure, globally scalable digitization service 
for generating and provisioning digital payment credentials into mobile devices, smart 
wearables, PCs, and other form factors. 


Tokenization replaces a PAN with a unique payment token (an alternative number) that is 
specific to the platform or entity that will use the token, such as a particular wallet application 
on a particular device. Digitization provisions the token to the target platform or device so it can 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1687 



Services or products leveraging the system 
MDES participants and interactions 


be used instead of the PAN to perform financial transactions, including contactless payments 
(using an NFC-enabled device), web, and in-app purchases. 


Figure 133: MDES digitization for different payment methods and devices 



The cardholder's PAN is not used in token transactions, reducing the possibility and impact of 
account data compromise. If a device is lost or stolen, only the tokens created for that device 
need to be replaced; the physical card can still be used. If a token is somehow intercepted, it 
cannot be used for payments because a token can only be used by the device to which it was 
provisioned. 


MDES is a single integrated platform for issuers, wallet providers, merchants, and other token 
requestors, and enables the digitization of supported Mastercard card types for many digital 
payment methods. The MDES end-to-end services are supported by the reliability and global 
reach of the Mastercard Network. 


MDES participants and interactions 


MDES connects wallet providers, other token requestors and Mastercard issuers, who can also 
be wallet providers. 


Token requestors integrate with MDES to request tokens for Mastercard payment cards, which 
can be used for digital payments (token transactions). 


Example token requestors: 


• 
Issuers and wallet providers, provide wallet applications for cardholders to digitize their cards 
and make digital payments through existing contactless technology and other point-of-sale 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1688 



Services or products leveraging the system 
MDES participants and interactions 


(POS) systems, and through new remote payment methods such as app-to-app payments. 
Wallet providers can provide wallets for their own devices, such as smart phones, smart 
watches, and fitness bands, or partner with device manufacturers (OEMs). 


• 
Merchants, who digitize the consumer PANs stored on their servers, so they can use tokens 
and cryptograms for browser-based e-commerce and in-app transactions. 
• 
Commerce Platforms, who provide pass-through digital wallet applications for cardholders 
to digitize their cards stored in a remote/cloud implementation and make e-commerce digital 
payments by transmitting tokens and cryptograms to integrated third-party merchants. 
These wallet providers can provide wallets in their own ecosystems, such as a social media 
marketplace or connected car, or within an integrated third-party merchant's checkout 
experience, such as a “pay-with” button. 
• 
On-behalf-of token requestors (OBOTRs), who initiate and request tokenization of 
consumers' PANs on-behalf of merchants and/or digital wallets, so that tokens and 
cryptograms are used for transactions. Payment facilitators may group submerchants based 
on shared characteristics, for example, business type, transaction volume, region, and so on, 
and tokens may be shared among submerchants of the same group, if adequate PAN checks 
are in-place. 
Figure 134: Issuers to token requestors 



© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Services or products leveraging the system 
MDES participants and interactions 


Issuers can benefit from connectivity to participating Wallet Providers and Token Requestors, so 
their Mastercard cards can be digitized for existing and emerging digital payment methods. 
Mastercard is the trusted partner, managing the integration between the parties. 


During issuer enablement (service setup), issuers choose the wallet programs they want to 
support and control how their Mastercard cards are digitized by providing Product 
Configurations and settings specific to each program. Mastercard works with issuers, Wallet 
Providers, and Token Requestors to help ensure that implementations work as expected. 


Issuers who support the: 


• 
Merchant Card on File Tokenization Program is automatically integrated with all merchants 
using that program. Mastercard requires all issuers in North America using MDES to process 
digitization requests and transactions for the Merchant Card on File Tokenization Program 
across all portfolios eligible for tokenization. 
• 
Commerce Platforms tokenization program are automatically integrated with all Commerce 
Platforms using that program. Mastercard automatically enables all U.S. issuers using MDES 
to process digitization requests and transactions for Commerce Platforms tokenization 
program across all portfolios eligible for tokenization, unless such Issuers choose to opt out 
from participating in the program as described in Card on file tokenization for Commerce 
Platforms. 
Provisioning models 


MDES tokens can be provisioned to a range of devices and platforms. As the following diagram 
shows, different types of tokens can be digitized to several targets, such as a device's Secure 
Element (SE), a Mastercard Cloud-Based Payments (MCBP) application, and a server. 
Depending on the deployment, the provisioned tokens can be used for contactless transactions 
(using NFC) or Digital Secure Remote Payment (DSRP) transactions. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Interactions and activities for device-based deployments 


Figure 135: Provisioning models 



NOTE: Samsung Pay also supports Dynamic Magnetic Stripe Data (DMSD), which allows payments at 
terminals that only have a magnetic stripe reader. 


MDES token transactions use the existing payments infrastructure. The transaction message 
sent to the acquirer includes the token and a cryptogram (for DSRP), instead of the PAN. 
Mastercard token transactions are routed through the Mastercard Network, where MDES 
validates them and maps the tokens back to the PANs for authorization by the issuer. 


For information on MCBP and DSRP, refer to chapters "Mastercard Cloud-Based Payments 
(MCBP)" and "Digital Secure Remote Payment (DSRP)" and respectively.

card, and the token and payment credentials are provisioned to the device.

Issuer/issuer processor 


• 
Specifies the account ranges within Bank Identification Numbers (BINs) that are available 
for digitization, and provides related Product Configuration data (such as card art and 
cardholder Terms and Conditions). 
• 
Configures rules and interacts with MDES during each digitization request, through 
predigitization messages, to determine whether the digitization can occur; issuers may 
decide that additional cardholder authentication is required before a token is activated. 
• 
Authorizes or declines the token transactions that have been validated by MDES. 
• 
Uses the MDES Customer Service Tools to address cardholder queries and manage the 
lifecycle of their cardholders' tokens, such as suspending and deactivating them.

Wallet provider (token requestor) 


• 
Provides a wallet application that enables cardholders to request card digitization, validate 
their identity (if required by the issuer), and use their digitized cards for payments. 
• 
Sends cardholder digitization requests to MDES. 
• 
(Depending on the implementation) Provisions the token and payment credentials to either: 
– 
The device's SE, through the Secure Element Issuer Trusted Service Manager (SEI TSM). 
– 
A Credentials Management System (CMS) that provides keys to a Mastercard Cloud-
Based Payments (MCBP) application in a device or on a server. 
MDES 


• 
Stores the issuer's Product Configurations and makes its card art and related textual data 
available to Wallet Providers, through the Mastercard card Image Repository. 
• 
Facilitates the digitization requests, passing the required data between the Wallet Provider 
and the issuer 
• 
Allocates a unique token to replace a cardholder PAN. 
• 
Prepares the provisioning package for sending the token (and associated credentials and 
data) to the target device 
• 
Validates each Mastercard token transaction and cryptogram (if used), applies token 
controls, and maps the token back to the PAN before forwarding the transaction to the 
issuer for authorization. 
• 
Notifies the wallet provider that cardholder transaction details are available, and delivers 
them directly to the device or solution. 
Cardholder: Activities depend on the type of device and the deployment, for example: 


1. 
Requests digitization of their payment card, agreeing to the issuer's Terms and Conditions. 
2. 
(If required by the issuer) Enters the authentication code sent to them, to validate their 
identity. This is just one of the authentication methods that the issuer may choose to 
provide. 
3. 
Makes payments, selecting the required digitized card. 
4. 
Views details of their MDES token transactions, such as the merchant name and 
transaction amount.

MDES features and benefits 


Mastercard issuers can use MDES to digitize their cardholder credentials without needing to 
build their own tokenization and digitization platforms. The MDES platform provides all the 
required digitization and transaction services, and connectivity to all participating wallet 
providers and token requestors. 


Features for issuers 


MDES features for issuers include: 
Flexible Product Configurations 
Issuers can define different digitization parameters and defaults for each wallet program they 


support, including: 


• 
The account ranges that are available for digitization 
• 
The card art and cardholder Terms and Conditions to be used 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1697 



Services or products leveraging the system 
MDES features and benefits 


• 
Eligibility rules and default digitization decisions 
• 
Default Activation Methods, if cardholder authentication is required before digitization 
Predigitization Messages 


Issuers can choose to receive either enhanced network messages, web service (API) messages or 
both from MDES for each digitization request. These messages provide data that an issuer can 
use to determine whether it wants to permit the digitization. 


Figure 142: Digitization message types 



For device-based wallets, issuers may decide that additional cardholder authentication is 
required before a token is activated, and they can supply different Activation Methods to MDES. 


Tokenization 


MDES allocates a unique token and generates a cryptographic key for each tokenization 
request. The token and key are specific to the platform or instance, such as a particular wallet 
application on a particular device. When PANs are tokenized for different applications, devices 
or programs, MDES issues different tokens and keys for each target. 


Figure 143: Tokenization 



The Mastercard Token Designation Service manages the availability and lifecycle of each token. 


Digitization 


MDES prepares the provisioning package, generating the cryptographic keys, personalization 
scripts and data for provisioning the token to the target, such as a device's SE, an MCBP 
application, or a secure server. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1698 



Services or products leveraging the system 
MDES features and benefits 


Card Image Repository 


Mastercard manages the repository of issuer card art and related textual data, which are to be 
used by wallet providers within their user interfaces (according to the issuer's Product 
Configurations). 


Transaction Processing Service 


This Mastercard service validates each token transaction, applies token controls, and maps the 
token to the PAN before forwarding the transaction to the issuer for authorization. The PAN is 
mapped back to the token when the authorization response is sent to the acquirer. 


Figure 144: Transaction processing service 



MDES uses cryptographic keys for EMV® and Card Validation Code 3 (CVC 3) verification. 
Mastercard generates and stores these keys for the token account ranges. 


Customer Service Tools 


The Mastercard Customer Service Application and Customer Service API are available for 
issuers to help their representatives or agents address cardholder queries and tokenization 
issues. Issuers can use the Mastercard application or integrate their own application with the 
API. For more information, refer to the "Customer Service Tools" section. 


The Customer Service Application is also available to wallet providers, with limited functionality, 
to assist visibility and investigations. 


Reporting Tools 


Several MDES reports are available for issuers, which provide data about different aspects of 
the issuer's MDES implementation, such as the wallet providers servicing their account ranges, 
tokenization counts, and transaction activity. 


Benefits to issuers 


MDES offers many benefits to issuers, including the following: 


• 
A range of business services for the complete end-to-end implementation of an issuer's 
tokenization and digitization requirements. 
• 
Tokenization and digitization are performed as services, so issuers are not burdened with 
significant upfront and ongoing investment (in costs and time). 
• 
A quick way to make an issuer's card account ranges available for digital payments through 
multiple wallet providers. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1699 



Services or products leveraging the system 
Supported card products 


• 
A single point of management where Mastercard handles integration and communication 
with the wallet providers and provisioning components. 
• 
A reduced time-to-market for issuers to roll out new digital device-based payment solutions 
to their cardholders. 
• 
Support of EMV/Chip requirements, delivering security and reduced fraud of chip-based 
payment processing for digitized cards. 
Supported card products 


MDES supports the digitization of existing card accounts and can tokenize Mastercard and 
Maestro-branded PANs. 


Supported card products: 


• 
Consumer debit and credit 
• 
Small Business cards 
• 
Prepaid cards (reloadable and nonreloadable) 
• 
Commercial cards 
Support for Mastercard Multicard, Mastercard Commercial Fleet (MCF) and Mastercard 
Government Fleet (MGF) product types: Tokens will not support merchant POS systems 
prompting for additional data required by Fleet cards. Therefore, issuers must inform 
cardholders they will still need to present their cards at merchant POS terminals that require 
prompting. 


Issuers and Digital Activity Customers (DACs) wanting to use either MDES, MCBP or both for 
non-Mastercard branded transactions (Co-Badge/ Private Label) are required to sign a 
separate commercial agreement with Mastercard for M/Chip technology licensing. 


MDES can only allocate the Card on File token type (used for server-based tokens) for 
Mastercard consumer product and acceptance brands, and Debit Mastercard. Contact your 
Mastercard representative for more information.

Several Mastercard APIs are useful to MDES issuers. These APIs are accessed through

ans-64 
When provided by the Wallet Provider, the issuer may use 
this hash value to match against known identifiers for the 
cardholder; for example, their email addresses on file. If the 
hash values match, this may aid an issuer’s digitization 
decision by providing additional factors to help verify that 
the Wallet Provider account holder is indeed their cardholder, 
or to differentiate between primary and secondary 
cardholders. The Wallet Provider computes the hash over an 
email address; MDES receives this and includes it in the data 
sent to the issuer. The issuer computes the hash of the email 
address on file for the cardholder; if it matches the hash of 
the one received from the Wallet Provider, the comparison 
with the hash value received from the Wallet Provider may 
be used by the issuer to assist determining the digitization 
decision. Hashing is used to help the issuer verify the 
cardholder email (or other relevant identifiers that the issuer 
may have for the cardholder) without the Wallet Provider 
providing the full email for privacy and security reasons. 
When the Wallet Provider is Apple Pay, the hash is generated 
using the PBKDF2 algorithm (PKCS #5). PBKDF2 is 
performed using 10 iterations, a salt, and the lowercase 
account ID as the password. The salt is calculated by taking 
the lower case UTF-8 bytes from the account ID and 
performing a SHA-256. Hash calculation example: 
Example: Input (Password): csharp@walletprovider.com 
Salt: 
41404d1bca85ddb59ab21466e277ac1ac5f61470be120c8 
2a21b1e45b5248123 
Count: 10 
Output: 
7098014b646d44c6f3b454c5d54f7a32b3b46e2b0c8e236 
7f3e5307e3036dfe6 
For all other Wallet Providers, the field contains the hash 
resulting from the following “accountIdHash” algorithm, 
rightpadded with spaces. “accountId” is the lower case 
UTF-8 bytes of the account ID: 
public String accountIdHash (String accountId) 
{String random8Bytes = 123CCB2F30BA420B return 
random8Bytes + lessSignificant24bytes(strongerHas 
h(accountId + random8Bytes))} public String 
strongerHash(String dataToHash) {String currentHash = 
dataToHash; for (int i = 0; i < 5000; i++) {currentHash = 
sha256(currentHash);} return sha256(sha256(dataToHash) 
+ currentHash);}

Wallet Service Provider 
Tokenization 
Recommendation Reason 
Codes 
ans-6 
Code indicating the specific reason the Wallet 
Provider is suggesting the tokenization 
recommendation. 
The data of this field is a hex-encoded bitmap, 
whereby each bit corresponds to a specific Reason 
Code. 
The bitmap is big-endian with the least significant bit 
corresponding to Reason Code 01, with the next least 
significant bit corresponding to Reason Code 02 and 
so on. For example, if Reason Codes 01, 05, and 16 
were encoded, the bitmap would be 
000000001000000000010001 and the hex value of 
this field would be 008011. 
If the Wallet Provider has no reason, this field will 
contain spaces.

Device Location 
ans-9 
Latitude and longitude where the device the consumer 
is attempting to tokenize a card onto is located. 


Device Location Latitude - an-4; hexadecimal encoded 
degrees with 2 decimal places. The first two 
characters represent the latitude value before the 
decimal place, and the last two characters represent 
the latitude after the decimal place. 


Device Location Longitude - an-4; hexadecimal 
encoded degrees with 2 decimal places. The first two 
characters represent the longitude value before the 
decimal place, and the last two characters represent 
the longitude after the decimal place. 


Device Location Lat/Long Sector - n-1; one of the 
following values: 


1 = Latitude = N, Longitude = W (positive latitude, 
negative longitude) 


2 = Latitude = N, Longitude = E (positive latitude, 
positive longitude) 


3 = Latitude = S, Longitude = W (negative latitude, 
negative longitude) 


4 = Latitude = S, Longitude = E (negative latitude, 
positive longitude) 


For example, a value of 264B5A4B1 would be 
interpreted as: 


• 
Latitude (first four characters) 264B 
– 
First hex digit (for value before decimal place) = 
0x26 = 38 (decimal) 
– 
Second hex digit (for value after decimal place) 
= 0x4B = 75 (decimal) 
• 
Longitude (next four characters) 5A4B 
– 
First hex digit (for value before decimal place) = 
0x5A = 90 (decimal) 
– 
Second hex digit (for value after decimal place) 
= 0x4B = 75 (decimal) 
• 
Device Location Sector (final digit) 1 = NW 
• 
Final location = 38.75N, 90.75W 
If the Wallet Provider has no information, this field 
contains spaces.

an-1

Token Data and Activation 
Method Value 
ans…283 
When the Token Data and Activation Method Type is 1, 2, 
3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 9 the issuer must provide values used to 
specify an activation method. Refer to Examples 1, 2, 3, 
and 4 for examples of Token Data and Activation 
Method(s) containing activation method values. 
Issuers have the option of providing an alternate account 
identifier in Tokenization Authorization Response messages 
(Token Data and Activation Method Type = a). 
An Alternate Account Identifier is a cardholder-friendly 
reference to a bank account, for example an IBAN 
(International Bank Account Number). It is typically useful 
for a Wallet Provider to display a suffix of this identifier to 
the cardholder to help them identify their tokenized card 
when they are not aware of their Account PAN. 
This will enable wallets to display alternate account 
identifier suffixes depending on the wallet functionality. 
Issuers must refer to each wallet’s documentation to 
determine if/how the alternate account identifier suffixes 
are displayed to cardholders. 
An alternate account identifier is in the format of a string 
with minimum 9 and maximum 64 characters, with no 
spaces allowed. An IBAN is an example of an alternate 
account identifier, as for example, 
GB82WEST12345698765432. 
When the Token Data and Activation Method Type is t, the 
issuer must provide one or multiple proprietary token 
personalization data items that MDES will include in the 
token profile. Refer to Example 8 for an example of Token 
Data and Activation Method(s) containing multiple token 
personalization data items. 
Each token personalization data item can have one to 
multiple instances of couples Token Personalization Data 
and Separator. 
Token Personalization Data: Base64 encoded data. 
Structure and content of data is defined separately per 
Mastercard Digital Enablement Service (MDES) Issuer 
Implementation Guide. Refer to Examples 6 and 7. 
Separator 
ans...1 
Each separate token personalization data (including after 
the last) will be delimited by a “~” character.

Reason Codes 
ans-6 
The reason for the cardholder authentication. The 
reason could impact the generation and validation 
of the authentication code in a number of ways 
including but not limited to the time period of 
validity of the code and the number of attempts 
allowed to validate the code. New reason codes can 
be added at any time and should not result in a 
failure. 


• 
01 = ADD_CARD – The account holder is being 
authenticated to verify account ownership at 
the time of adding a card in merchant system. 
• 
02 = VERIFY_ACCOUNT - The account holder is 
being authenticated to verify account 
ownership to use a service 
• 
03 = OTHER 
• 
04 = PAYMENT_TRANSACTION - The account 
holder is being authenticated to initiate 
payment transaction 
• 
05 = TOKEN_BINDING - The account holder is 
being authenticated to bind a token to bind id. 
• 
06 = ACCOUNT_BINDING - The account holder 
is being authenticated to bind associated 
account with bind id (device). 
The data of this field is a hex-encoded bitmap, 
whereby each bit corresponds to a specific Reason 
Code. 


The bitmap is big-endian with the least significant 
bit corresponding to Reason Code 01, with the next 
least significant bit corresponding to Reason Code 
02 and so on. For example, if Reason Codes 01 and 
02 were encoded, the bitmap would be 
000000000000000000000011 and the hex value 
of this field would be 000003.

Absolute positioning of data in DE 124 subfields is required. Subfields not containing values will 
be populated with spaces when they are followed by subfields that contain values. If one or 
more subfields at the end of the data element do not contain a value, the subfields will not be 
present and the total length of DE 124 will be reduced by the subfield lengths.

DE 124 Subfields in Authorization Request/0100 and Financial Transaction Request/0200 for 
ACN 


Subfield Name 
Reason Code 
Attributes 
ans-6 
Values/Comments 
The reason the account holder is being authenticated. The 
reason could impact the generation and validation of the 
code in various ways including but not limited to the time 
period of validity of the code and the number of attempts 
allowed to validate the code. New reason codes can be 
added at any time and should not result in a failure. 
Bit Position Meaning 
01 "ADD_CARD" - The account holder is being authenticated 
to verify account ownership at the time of adding a card in 
the consent requestor system 
NOTE: In the context of MDES, token might be in an active 
state. 
02 "VERIFY_ACCOUNT" - The account holder is being 
authenticated to verify account ownership to use a service 
03 OTHER - Requires Token Binding 
04 - PAYMENT_TRANSACTION – The account holder is being 
authenticated to initiate a payment transaction 
05 - TOKEN_BINDING – The account holder is being 
authenticated to bind a token to bind ID. 
06 - ACCOUNT_BINDING – The account holder is being 
authenticated to bind associated account with bind id 
(device) 
The data of this field is a hex-encoded bitmap, whereby each 
bit corresponds to a specific Reason Code. The bitmap is bigendian 
with the least significant bit corresponding to Reason 
Code 01, with the next least significant bit corresponding to 
Reason Code 02 and so on. For example, if Reason Codes 01 
and 02 were encoded, the bitmap would be 
000000000000000000000011 and the hex value of this 
field would be 000003. 
NOTE: This parameter is present only if an issuer has opted 
for Authentication Service for Click to Pay and Secure Card 
on File Tokens. 
Token Unique Reference 
ans-48, left-justified, 
padded with spaces 
Service-allocated unique reference to the token. 
NOTE: This parameter is present only if the issuer has 
opted for Authentication Service for Click to Pay and 
Secure Card on File Tokens.

Payment Channel (India 
only) 
an-3 
This field is present only if Tokenization Event Indicator 
contains value 2 (Payment Channel Preference Updated). 
The data of this field is a hex-encoded bitmap, whereby 
each bit corresponds to a specific payment channel 
disabled by the cardholder. 
The bitmap is big-endian with the least significant bit 
corresponding to Payment Channel 01, with the next least 
significant bit corresponding to Payment Channel 02 and 
so on. For example, if Payment Channels 01, 03, and 05 
were encoded, the bitmap would be 0000 0001 0101 and 
the hex value of this field would be 15. 
MDES will pass 0 if all payment channels are enabled. 
Bit Position and Payment Channel 
1 = Contactless 
2 = Merchant Presented QR (MPQR) 
3 = Customer Presented QR (CPQR) 
4 = Digital Secure Remote Payment (DSRP) In-App 
5 = Person to Person (P2P) 
6 = Dynamic Magnetic Stripe Data (DMSD) 
7 to 12 = Reserved for future use

Activation Code Notification 


Field 
ID 
Field Name 
Attributes 
Values/Comments 
10 
Reason Code 
ans-6 
The reason the account holder is being authenticated. The 
reason could impact the generation and validation of the 
code in various ways including but not limited to the time 
period of validity of the code and the number of attempts 
allowed to validate the code. New reason codes can be 
added at any time and should not result in a failure. 
Bit Position Meaning 
01 ADD_CARD - The account holder is being authenticated 
to verify account ownership at the time of adding a card in 
the consent requestor system 
NOTE: In the context of MDES - token might be in an 
active state. 
02 VERIFY_ACCOUNT - The account holder is being 
authenticated to verify account ownership to use a service 
03 OTHER 04 
PAYMENT_TRANSACTION - The account holder is being 
authenticated to initiate a payment transaction 
05 TOKEN_BINDING - The account holder is being 
authenticated to bind a token to bind ID. 
06 ACCOUNT_BINDING - The account holder is being 
authenticated to bind associated account with bind ID 
(device). 
The data of this field is a hex-encoded bitmap, whereby 
each bit corresponds to a specific Reason Code. The bitmap 
is big-endian with the least significant bit corresponding to 
Reason Code 01, with the next least significant bit 
corresponding to Reason Code 02 and so on. For example, if 
Reason Codes 01, and 02 the bitmap would be 
000000000000000000000011 and the hex value of this 
field would be 000003. 
NOTE: This parameter is present only if an issuer has 
opted for Authentication Service for Click to Pay and 
Secure Card on File Tokens.

Token Unique 
Reference

Mastercard Digital Transaction Insights service 


Mastercard’s Digital Transaction Insights service provides issuers an improved risk assessment, 


enabling issuers to make more advanced and intelligent risk-based authorization decisions. 


Mastercard Digital Transaction Insights integrates the authentication and authorization 
systems to help eliminate the differences that exist between card present and e-commerce 
approval/fraud rates while facilitating a better customer experience. 


Comprised of three different insights, Digital Transaction Insights may help issuers increase 


approvals and reduce false declines of genuine e-commerce transactions without increasing risk 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1773 



Services or products leveraging the system 
Mastercard Fraud Services 


exposure. It may also help reduce financial losses and associated costs from fraud and 
chargebacks. By facilitating the exchange and normalization of consumer account and device 
data provided by participating merchants, the Digital Transaction Insights Service gives issuers a 
level of assurance that consumers are transacting using attributes—such as account, device, and 
other valuable information as a part of the EMV 3-D secure standard. As a result, issuers can 
make more informed decisions for card-not-present transactions. For more information, please 
refer to the Mastercard Identity Check Program Guide. 

Mastercard Fraud Services 


Mastercard fraud notification service 


The fraud notification service (FNS) helps to detect fraud and ensures that chargebacks are 
properly submitted by the issuer. 


Overview 


The fraud notification service supports processing of Cirrus, Maestro, Mastercard, and Debit 
Mastercard transactions. Issuers can provide a card expiration date in Single Message 
Transaction Manager to be used in chargeback processing of transactions. 


FNS tracks each unique combination of a PAN, PAN expiration date, and token or Virtual Card 
Number (VCN), as applicable when applying the existing thresholds for blocking of fraud-related 
chargebacks in FNS. 


Mastercard requires all acquiring and issuing processors to code for support and integrate into 
their systems the data elements, subelements, and values associated with Mastercard Fraud 
Notification Service. 


NOTE: Mastercard does not require acquirers or issuers to enroll in these optional products and 
services, but they must code their systems to support these fields to leverage such product and 
services in a timely manner in the event of a security issue. 


Refer to the Mastercard Security Solutions Guide for Issuers for more information. 


Mastercard fraud services 


Debit Mastercard issuers can use the suite of Mastercard fraud services to make authorization 
decisions and minimize the risk of potentially fraudulent transactions. 


Mastercard Decision Intelligence 


Mastercard decision intelligence is a real-time authorization decisioning solution that applies 
thousands of data points and sophisticated modeling techniques to each transaction, 
simplifying these insights into a single transaction decision score that helps issuers to fine-tune 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1774 



Services or products leveraging the system 
How it works 


their authorization decisions with the goal of approving genuine transactions and declining 
fraudulent ones. 


Decision intelligence enables smarter decisioning by giving issuers a multi-dimensional 
authorization tool to assess both the risk and rewards of every transaction, so they can enhance 
the consumer experience by approving more genuine transactions without increasing risk. 
Decision Intelligence evaluates information about consumers, merchants, and issuers during the 
shopping experience to help issuers decide whether a transaction makes sense and if it should 
be approved or declined for a particular consumer 


Decision Intelligence ultimately shifts transaction decisioning from the basis of a risk score to a 
decision score that is based on both the fraud risk and rewards of approving a transaction. With 
a more comprehensive analysis of the risk and reward factors, Decision Intelligence assesses 
both negative and positive data points to calculate a single score that shows where the 
transaction falls on a scale from decline to approve, thus helping issuers authorize more 
transactions with confidence, increase their profitability, and improve the cardholder experience. 


Mastercard will require all acquiring and issuing processors to code for, support, and integrate 
into their systems the data elements, subelements, and values associated with Decision 
Intelligence. 


NOTE: Mastercard does not require issuers or acquirers to enroll in these optional products and 
services, but they must code their systems to support these fields to leverage such product and 
services in a timely manner in the event of a security issue.

Authorization IQ 


Authorization IQ is a feature of Decision Intelligence that can help issuers increase approvals 
and ensure a more satisfying consumer experience without incurring greater risk. 


Authorization IQ gives issuers targeted, real-time segmentation insights to help them identify 
best-spending or most frequent-spending cardholders who show the greatest revenue 
opportunity at the time of card usage. 


In addition to assessing authorization decisions based on the risk profile of how the cardholder 
originated the transaction (such as via magstripe, EMV2, or tokenization), Authorization IQ 
provides a complementary set of data points that help bring focus to the importance of the 
individual cardholder at the time of the transaction. 


Mastercard will require all acquiring and issuing processors to code for, support, and integrate 
into their systems the data elements, subelements, and values associated with Decision 
Intelligence: Authorization IQ feature. 


NOTE: Mastercard does not require acquirers or issuers to enroll in these optional products and 
services, but they must code their systems to support these fields to leverage such product and 
services in a timely manner in the event of a security issue.

Fraud rule manager 


As an integral part of a rules-based authorization strategy, fraud rule manager enables issuers 
to automate precise, highly variable fraud decisions during authorization in order to quickly and 
easily respond to evolving fraud trends. 


Fraud rule manager provides 


• 
network fraud monitoring that silently scans global authorization activity, monitoring for 
highly abnormal activity to identify and limit fraud losses from large-scale fraud events, and 
• 
customized fraud rule management utilizing individual data elements within the 
authorization message as well as Mastercard-defined variables to automate precise, highly 
variable fraud decisions during authorization and enable appropriate actions based on issuer 
specifications. 
Mastercard will require all issuing and acquiring processors to code for, support, and integrate 
into their systems the data elements, subelements, and values associated with fraud rule 
manager. 


NOTE: Mastercard does not require acquirers or issuers to enroll in these optional products and 
services, but they must code their systems to support these fields to leverage such product and 
services in a timely manner in the event of a security issue.

Mastercard In Control services 


Mastercard In Control services 


The Mastercard In Control platform provides several advanced transaction routing and alert 
controls designed to assist issuers in launching new and enhanced payment products. 


Mastercard In Control fully integrates patented payment technologies with unparalleled global 
processing capabilities. With the integration of this capability into Mastercard core processing, 
issuers can benefit from cost efficiencies and speed to market for new product development. 
Participation in Mastercard In Control is optional. For more information, refer to the Mastercard 
In Control Program Guide, Mastercard In Control for Mobile Payments Issuer Implementation 
Guide, Mastercard In Control for Business Travel, and Mastercard In Control for Commercial 
Payments Quick Start Guide. 


Mastercard Identity Check 


The Mastercard Identity Check™ program encompasses varying solution-oriented protocols that 
build upon the infrastructure requirements for channel encryption with the additional benefit of 
cardholder authentication. When used with components of the Mastercard Dual Message 
Authorization System, this program provides a mechanism for online merchants to potentially 
receive an enhanced payment guarantee similar to what retailers receive with qualifying 
physical point-of-sale transactions. 


When participating in the Mastercard Identity Check program, the SLI and UCAF data must be 
included in the authorization to the issuer when it is available in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private 
Use), subelement 42 (Electronic Commerce Indicators) and 43 (Universal Cardholder 
Authentication Field [UCAF]). It is a variable length (maximum 32 characters) field with a 
flexible data structure that can be tailored to support the needs of issuer security and 
authentication approaches. Mastercard AAV UCAF data is always a base64 value with a length 
of 28 characters. 


For more information on the Mastercard Identity Check program, refer to the Mastercard 
Identity Check Program Guide.

Transaction Processing Rules 
Gaming and Gambling Program 


The Program facilitates Domestic Gaming Payment Transactions and, where permitted, Cross-
border Gaming Payment Transactions to Mastercard and Maestro® branded Card Accounts, 
with some limitations. 


A Gaming Payment Transaction is a type of Payment Transaction that transfers winnings or 
value usable for gambling or gaming to a Mastercard or Maestro Account and that is effected 
pursuant to, and subject to, the Gaming and Gambling Payments Standards. The funds are 
transferred by an Originating Institution, as defined in the Mastercard Rules, which must be an 
acquirer, referred to in this guide as an Originating Institution or OI to the Recipient’s Receiving 
Account at the Receiving Institution, as defined in the Mastercard Rules which must be an issuer, 
referred to in this guide as a Receiving Institution or RI. It is not a merchant return credit that 
reverses a previous purchase of goods or services. 


A Gaming Payment Transaction falls within the category of disbursements of winnings or value 
usable from gambling, lottery and games of skill. A game of skill means: (a) game participants 
pay a game entry fee, (b) the outcome of the game is determined by the skill of the participant 
rather than by chance, (c) the winner of the game receives a prize of monetary value; and (d) a 
non-participant in the game does not receive a prize of monetary value in relation to the game. 


Gaming Payment Transactions serve the growing demand by Originating Institutions and 
Receiving Institutions for fast, secure, and convenient ways to provide to their customers the 
respective payment services to enable them to send and receive gaming payments, respectively. 


Mastercard requires the use of a Transaction Type Identifier, sometimes also referred to as 
Payment Type Indicator, in all Gaming Payment Transactions to identify the purpose of the 
transfer of funds to support transaction monitoring by Participating Customers and 
authorization decisions by Receiving Institutions. 


Refer to Mastercard Gaming and Gambling Payments Program Standards for more information.

System edits: sender address data 


The Single Message System will perform the following system edits on Financial Transaction 
Request/0200 messages to determine whether a transaction meets the criteria for sender 
address data. 


NOTE: Transaction will be declined if the sender Country is subject to comprehensive geographic 
sanctions published by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), http://www.treasury.gov/ 
resource-center/sanctions/Pages/default.aspx. The current list of countries subject to such sanctions 
is Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Syria; however, this list is subject to change.

Mastercard transit transactions 


The demands of the transit environment make it different from the traditional retail payment 
environment. 


Specifically, the transit environment requires: 


• 
Fast and secure access to the transit system. Control of access to the transit system 
(generally referred to as "permission to travel"). Ticketing - beyond simple system access, 
ticket inspection establishes that the individual is authorized to take a specific trip. A flexible 
relationship between access and payment, as the final transaction amount is often not 
known until the journey is complete. 
• 
Mastercard delivers on all of these requirements through a range of transit models and 
related business rules that support acceptance of a broad range of contactless cards. 
Pre-funded transit transactions 


A pre-funded transit transaction occurs when the cardholder purchases value redeemable for 
future travel with a transit merchant. The purchased value is held by the transit merchant in an 
account linked to the cardholder’s card or device. Any usage of the card or device following the 
purchase of value will reduce the value held with the transit merchant. 


The transit merchant follows its usual authorization procedures by generating an Authorization 
Request/0100 message for the full amount of the transaction. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1795 



Services or products leveraging the system 
Real-time authorized transit transactions 


Real-time authorized transit transactions 


A real-time authorized transit transaction occurs when the transit merchant generates an 
Authorization Request/0100 message each time a cardholder uses his or her card or device at 
the transit merchant’s terminal. 


The transit merchant follows its usual authorization procedures by generating an Authorization 
Request/0100 message for the full amount of the transaction. 


Post-authorized aggregated contactless transit transactions 


A post-authorized aggregated contactless transit transaction occurs when the transit merchant 
generates a First Presentment/1240 message combining one or more contactless taps 
performed with one contactless account number and occurring with one transit merchant. 


For the contactless transit merchant to receive chargeback protection all of the following must 
occur: 


• 
The transit merchant must send a properly identified Authorization Request/0100 message, 
which can be for any amount not exceeding the cardholder verification method (CVM) limit 
amount, as published in the Chargeback Guide on the day of the transaction. 
• 
The issuer must have approved the transaction. 
• 
The combined amount of the contactless taps must be equal to, or less than, the cardholder 
verification method (CVM) limit amount, as published in the Chargeback Guide . 
• 
The maximum time period from the first contactless tap until the First Presentment/1240 
message is generated must be 14 calendar days or less. 
NOTE: These transit transactions are limited to MCCs 4111, 4131, and 4784. 


Upon the cardholder’s request, the transit merchant must provide a list of the contactless taps 
that were combined into a First Presentment/1240 message. 


NOTE: The phrases "tap the contactless card or device" and "contactless tap" refer to the same series 
of actions: a cardholder touching the contactless card or device to a contactless terminal, the 
contactless terminal reading the card data, and then the contactless terminal flashing a light and 
making a sound to indicate the outcome of the tap to the cardholder. 


Authorized-aggregated split clearing transactions 


An authorized-aggregated split clearing transaction is subject to the following restrictions. 


NOTE: Applies only to domestic United Kingdom (U.K.) transactions. 


• 
The contactless-enabled card or device must indicate that an M/Chip profile is supported. 
• 
Tag 5F28 (Issuer Country Code) must have a value of 826. 
© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1796 



Services or products leveraging the system 
Post-authorized aggregated Maestro contactless transit transactions 


• 
The denominated primary currency is GBP. 
• 
The transaction is properly identified in the same manner as described in Post-authorized 
Aggregated Contactless Transit Transactions, with the exception that the value in the transit 
indicator field is value 4, instead of value 3. 
Post-authorized aggregated Maestro contactless transit 
transactions 


A post-authorized aggregated Maestro contactless transit transaction occurs when the acquirer 
generates an Authorization Request/0100 message for an estimated or maximum amount in 
connection with the use of one Maestro contactless account number at one transit merchant. 


The transit merchant may combine multiple Maestro contactless taps into a single transaction 
amount and reverse any unused funds by the cardholder at the end of the aggregation time 
period. 


The transactions are processed as follows: 


• 
The transit merchant sends an Authorization Request/0100 (Europe-acquired only) message 
containing value 06 in DE 48, subelement 64, subfield 1 (Transit Transaction Type Indicator) 
for an estimated or maximum amount not to exceed the applicable contactless transit 
aggregated CVM amount. 
• 
The issuer must have approved the transaction. 
• 
The cardholder may make subsequent taps for additional rides. These taps will not be sent to 
the issuer for authorization. The combined amount of the taps must be equal to or less than 
the applicable contactless aggregated CVM limit amount. 
• 
When the authorized amount is reached or within 3 calendar days (3 days in Mexico), the 
transit merchant totals the value of all taps and generates a partial Reversal Request/0400 
or an Authorization Advice/0120 message to reverse any unused funds. The Authorization 
Advice/0120 message option is only available for Europe region acquirers. 
The transaction is properly identified in the same manner as described in Post-authorized 
Aggregated Contactless Transit Transactions, with the exception that the transit transaction 
type identifier (DE 48, subelement 64) value is 06.

Debt recovery transactions 


Mastercard Rules allow transit merchants to recover an amount owed to them (a transit debt 
recovery transaction) following a declined authorization request. 


A transit debt recovery transaction occurs when transit fare spend has been incurred, in 
granting a contactless card access to travel, and as a result of the issuer declining the 
authorization request, the transit merchant is initially unable to collect payment for the fare 
spend. When this situation occurs, the transit merchant can add the card to a Deny List, thereby 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1798 



Services or products leveraging the system 
Debt recovery transactions 


blocking that card from access to travel until such time as the money owed by the cardholder 
has been recovered. 


A mechanism in which a cardholder’s debt is cleared in order for the cardholder to access the 
transit system to resume travel is through debt recovery transactions. Two contactless transit 
rules create the opportunity for this situation to arise: post-authorized aggregated (Global) and 


• authorized aggregated split clearing (U.K. and Republic of Ireland only) There are several 
methods of debt recovery that a transit merchant can implement. Each method allows debt 
recovery transactions to recover a debt from a Mastercard credit, debit, or prepaid card or from 
a Maestro debit or prepaid card. 
Customer impact 


Mastercard transit transactions impact acquirer and issuers. 


Acquirers 


Acquirers of transit transactions must be able to support DE 48, subelement 64 (Transit 
Program) in: 


• 
Financial Transaction Request/0200. 
• 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220 messages. 
Contactless chip acquirers that acquire transit transactions must be able to support 
Transaction Certificates in online financial transaction messages. 


Acquirers supporting merchants from acceptor business codes (MCCs) 4111, 4131, 4784, and 
7523 must support and transfer data related to PAN mapping information to their merchants 
when available in the response messages. 


Acquirers that process for merchants that belong to MCC 4111 and 4131 that are 
implementing transit aggregation transactions must: 


• 
Prepare their systems to support a post-authorized aggregated Maestro contactless transit 
transaction. 
• 
Update their systems to support value 06 (Post-Authorized Aggregated Maestro) in DE 48 
(Additional Data), subelement 64 (Transit Program), subfield 1 (Transit Transaction Type 
Indicator) within the Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages in order to properly 
identify post-authorized aggregated Maestro contactless transit transactions. 
Acquirers supporting merchants that implement the Mastercard contactless aggregated 
models can support zero amount Application Transaction Counter (ATC) update Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 messages to notify issuers of the most recent ATC values for the 
offline cardholder aggregation activity. 


Acquirers that process for transit merchants can submit processing of mail order/telephone 
order (MOTO) and key-entered transactions for Maestro contactless products. 


When submitting these transactions, acquirers must properly identify these transactions as 
debt recovery transactions where DE 48 (Additional Data), subelement 64 (Transit Program), 
subfield 1 (Transit Transaction Type Indicator) contains value 07 (Debt Recovery) in Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 messages.

Issuers 


Issuers must be able to support DE 48, subelement 64 (Transit Program) in: 


• 
Financial Transaction Request/0200 and Financial Transaction Advice/0220. 
• 
Financial Transaction Advice/0220: Debit Mastercard Stand-In messages. 
Contactless chip issuers that currently participate in the M/Chip Cryptogram Pre-validation 
service or the Combined Service Option should be aware that Mastercard has updated its 
systems to allow for the presence of Transaction Certificates in online authorization and 
financial transaction messages. 


Contactless chip issuers that do not participate in either the M/Chip Cryptogram Pre-validation 
service or the Combined Service Option must be able to support the presence of Transaction 
Certificates in online financial transaction messages. 


All Mastercard contactless issuers performing their own PAN mapping must provide the 
association between PANs in Financial Transaction Request Response/0210 messages for all 
transactions originated from MCC 4111, 4131, 4784, and 7523. 


Issuers of contactless cards or devices must be prepared to support zero amount ATC update 
Financial Transaction Request/0200 messages that provides the most recent ATC value of 
contactless cards or devices. 


Issuers of Maestro contactless cards or devices must prepare their systems to process a 
postauthorized aggregated Maestro contactless transit transaction. These transactions will be 
identified with value 06 (Post-Authorized Aggregated Maestro) in DE 48, subelement 64, 
subfield 1 (Transit Transaction Type Indicator) within the Financial Transaction Request/0200 
messages. 


Issuers of contactless cards or devices must be able to properly process such transactions 
regardless of the amount indicated in the authorization request message. As per the rule, the 
transaction amount must not exceed the chargeback protection amount published by 
Mastercard in the Chargeback Guide on the day of the transaction. 


Mastercard requires the use of specific transaction type identifiers to clearly differentiate 
aggregated transit transactions from all other transactions. Issuers must be prepared to 
correctly process authorization messages containing these identifiers. 


Issuers that issue Maestro contactless cards and support processing of transit transactions 
must prepare their systems to accept and process mail order/telephone order (MOTO) and cardnot-
present key-entered transit transactions as well as e-commerce and card present for 
Maestro contactless products, provided these transactions are properly identified as debt 
recovery transactions (DE 48 [Additional Data], subelement 64 [Transit Program], subfield 1 
[Transit Transaction Type Indicator] contains value 07 [Debt Recovery]) in the Financial 
Transaction Request/0200 messages. 


All issuers that issue contactless cards or devices must support changes made to the criteria of 
post-authorized aggregated authorizations. DE 22 (Point-of-Service [POS] Entry Mode), 
subfield 1 (POS Terminal PAN Entry Mode), value 82 (PAN Auto Entry via Server [issuer, acquirer,

Name Validation Service 


The Name Validation Service is a service to validate the name provided by a registered user 
matches the name associated to the card at the issuer. Customers can validate cardholder 
name information by including a name validation request in an ASI message. 


Participation requirements 


Acquirers and Originating Institutions should be aware that name validation can be included in 
an ASI message. 


Issuers will receive ASI service messages with a request for cardholder name validation and 
must validate the name information provided in the request message and respond with a result 
indicating a likelihood of a match. 


For more information 


Acquirers looking to use the Name Validation Service, and for further information, must contact 
their account team or refer to the Name Validation Service Issuer Name Matching Guide.

Payment Cancelation Service 


Payment Cancelation Service 


Single Message System issuers can use the Payment Cancelation Service to have Mastercard 
block unwanted card-not-present (CNP) transactions at the PAN level to improve cardholder 
satisfaction. 


Payment Cancelation Service is available to issuers for CNP transactions, these include: 


• 
Debit Mastercard issuers processing on the Single Message System 
• 
Maestro issuers processing on the Single Message System 
• 
Debit Mastercard and Europe Maestro issuers processing on the Dual Message System 
Issuers create listings in the Payment Cancelation Service (PCS) database identifying the 
cardholder, acquirer, merchant, and optionally the transaction amount or transaction amount 
range. Mastercard checks the PCS database for entries and CNP transactions are stopped 
when a match is found. Issuer account ranges/BINs must be enrolled for PCS before using the 
service. 


To enroll, all issuers must complete the Payment Cancelation Service Enrollment Form (Form 
0832) located on Mastercard Connect. After the BINs are enrolled, issuers can follow the steps 
outlined in the form to set up the bulk file. Issuer participation in the PCS is optional.

Character sets 


Character sets define how letters, numbers, symbols, and special characters are displayed in 
computer text. 


Which character sets does Mastercard support? 


Mastercard supports ASCII (ISO 8859-1) and EBCDIC (Code Page 1047) code pages for both 
standard and extended character sets. 


Mastercard supports standard EBCDIC formatted messages and bulk files. In addition to standard 
EBCDIC, Mastercard supports the extended EBCDIC format as well as the standard and extended 
ASCII format for both authorization messages and selected bulk files. Customers using the MIP to 
transmit bulk files still need to adhere to the existing Mastercard File Transfer Protocol format, that 
is, EBCDIC (for Header and Trailer information). 


NOTE: Extended characters: Within the full character set, the alphabet is represented as used in the English 
language (with no character enhancements) and characters that may be found, for example, in the Spanishalphabet where the tilde is used over the Ã. 


Mastercard uses extended EBCDIC as the default character set type for sending messages unless 
otherwise specified by the customer. 


Customers also have the option to send and receive either standard or extended character sets for 
both ASCII and EBCDIC formats in specific data elements that contain text. Following are examples 
of some data elements that may contain standard or extended text characters: 


• 
DE 42 (Acceptor ID) 
• 
DE 43 (Acceptor Name and Location) 
• 
DE 120 (Record Data) 
• 
DE 123 (Receipt Free Text) 
• 
DE 124 (Member-defined Data) 
The following bulk files will be supported in ASCII: 
• 
R311: AMS File Updates 
• 
R361: AMS File Updates (TEST) 
Customers that want to receive messages in standard EBCDIC or extended or standard ASCII must 
inform Mastercard. 


Character sets 


The following tables contain valid ASCII to EBCDIC character sets. 


NOTE: For ISO 8583, the <space> character is treated as a special character (attribute "s"). It may, 
however, also be used in fields designated as alphanumeric (attribute "an") but only in the form of trailing 
spaces used to pad out significant data to fill a fixed-length field.

System access information 
Mastercard interface processor 


Accessing the Single Message System 


To process authorization activity, acquirers and issuers must access the Mastercard Network. This 
network is the path by which they send and receive financial transaction messages and related data. 


Selecting a particular processing access method depends on several factors, including: 


• 
Physical installations present at the point-of-interaction and at the customer site 
• 
Volume of incoming and outgoing authorizations 
• 
Customer locations 
For help in selecting an appropriate access method, contact a Customer Implementation Services 
specialist. 


Mastercard interface processor 


Customers connect to the Mastercard Network through at least two MIP, which serves as a 


front-end communications processor. The MIP is located onsite at the customer facility. 


The MIP provides the hardware and software at the customer site that allows the customer 


host system to interface with the Mastercard Network in a standard, efficient manner. 


The MIP also permits distributed data processing functions to support the financial service 


applications of Mastercard. 


NOTE: Throughout this manual, references to online mean that an acquirer or issuer is directly 
connected to a Mastercard MIP, and such references are not intended to imply that the acquirer or 
issuer is connected through any web-based means. 


The required customer communication protocol for online debit processing is Transmission 
Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP). The precise configuration at a given customer site 
is engineered jointly by the customer and the Mastercard Network Engineering Group. Historical 
or anticipated transaction volume is the basis for the MIP configuration. 


Batch file transmission 


Customers requiring complex-to-complex (CTC) batch file transmissions will need to be able to 
connect to the Mastercard Network using TCP/IP. File transfer communications will use the 
Mastercard Service Delivery Point (SDP). Mastercard offers multiple batch file delivery options. 
Contact your Implementation Specialist for a full list of offerings. 


Related documentation 


Refer to the Secured Data Communications Guide for further information.

Appendix E Message timer table 


The Single Message Systems defines a maximum response time for the messages transmitted across 
the system.

Transaction Response/0210 messages

transaction flow. Once a cardholder initiates a transaction, the Single Message System expects the 
following time intervals for processing a transaction.

Transaction research information 
Request the Transaction Research tool 


Customers can use the Transaction Research Request (Form 074) to request the Global Customer 
Service team to perform research for you. 


If you submit a transaction research request by completing and sending the Transaction Research 
Request (Form 074) to Mastercard, Mastercard sends you a letter, with the authorization 
information, that you can use for chargeback purposes. If you request the services informally via a 
customer representative, you will not receive a letter. 


Request the Transaction Research tool 


Complete the following steps to request the Transaction Research Tool. 


About this task 


If you submit a transaction research request by completing and sending the Transaction 
Research Request (Form 074) to Mastercard, Mastercard sends you a letter, with the 
authorization information, that you can use for chargeback purposes. If you request the services 
informally via a customer representative, you will not receive a letter. 


Complete the following steps to request the Transaction Research Tool. 


Procedure 


1. 
Log on to Mastercard Connect. 
2. 
Enter your User ID and Password. 
3. 
Click Store on the main menu (located in the upper right corner) on the Mastercard Connect 
home page. 
4. 
Scroll to or search for Transaction Research. 
5. 
Click Add to Cart (a confirmation message appears). 
6. 
Click Cart to display the cart, and then click Check Out to display the Order Details window. 
7. 
Under Order Details, click Review Order > Place Order. 
8. 
Once the Security Administrator approves the request, Transaction Research will appear 
under the Applications menu on the Mastercard Connect home page. 
How to Access the Transaction Research Tool 


About this task 


Complete the following steps to access the Transaction Research Tool. 


Procedure 


1. 
Log on to Mastercard Connect. 
2. 
On the Applications menu, click Transaction Research. The Mastercard Authorization 
Transaction Research page appears.

1830 



Transaction research information 
Submit an Authorization request 


Submit an Authorization request 


Complete the following steps to submit a request through the Transaction Research Tool. 


Procedure 


1. 
In the Card Number box, enter the cardholder account number that you want to research. 
NOTE: Mastercard uses the optional ICA number for your tracking purposes only. If you enter an 


ICA number, it appears on your billing report to help you identify transactions. 


2. 
In the Date Range area, enter a starting transaction date and an ending transaction date 
using a MM/DD/YYYY format or click the Calendar link to select a date. 
3. 
To identify a transaction more specifically by its approval code, enter the Authorization 
Code. 
4. 
To identify a transaction more specifically by its amount, select one of the following options: 
– 
Click All Transactions to retrieve all transactions. 
– 
Click Single Transaction, and then enter the amount in U.S. dollars to identify a single 
transaction. 
– 
Click Transaction Range, and then enter a starting transaction amount in U.S. dollars 
and the ending transaction amount in U.S. dollars to identify a range of transactions. 
5. 
To view recurring payments only, select the View Only Recurring Payments check box. 
6. 
Click Search. The search results page displays. 
7. 
To display the detailed results for a specific transaction, select the transaction you want, 
and then click Detail. 
Results 


The Authorization Transaction Research tool displays a presence indicator for the following data 
elements in which they are present: DE 35 (Track 2 Data), DE 45 (Track 1 Data), and CVC 2 
values in DE 48 (Additional Data: Private Use), subelement 92 (CVC 2).

Transaction data classifications table 


Appendix G Transaction data classifications table 


The following table describes the transaction data classification categories used to define data 
elements. 


Category One: Transaction data that, when received by a customer or Service Provider, must only be 
used, or disclosed by the customer or Service Provider for the purpose of carrying out the customer’s 
issuing program, acquiring program, or digital activities (for example, as relating to digital wallets and 
tokenization). 


Category Two: Transaction data that, when received by a customer or Service Provider, must only be 
used, or disclosed in connection with the specific purpose for which it was provided (for example, as 
relating to participation in a program or service).

Glossary 
acceptor 


acceptor 


A person or entity that agrees to accept payment cards or devices bearing a particular brand or 
in respect to an agreement with the issuer. Also referred to as a merchant, ATM, bank, merchant 
ATM, or other entity authorized to accept brand transactions. 


Plural Form: acceptors 


acceptance brand 


Acceptance brands are Mastercard and other private label brands, such as cards specific to a 
particular department store or airline. 


Plural Form: acceptance brands 


acquirer 


A licensed Mastercard customer that acquires the data relating to a transaction from the 
acceptor and submits that data for authorization. The acquirer also supports clearing and 
settlement functions to exchange funds between the issuer and the acceptor. Also referred to as 
an acquiring bank, acquirer bank, merchant bank, or acquiring financial institution. 


Plural Form: acquirers 


acquirer host 


A term referring to customer host processing at the acquirer’s location. 


advice message 


A message that notifies a party of an action that has been taken, requiring no response. 
Plural Form: advice messages 


advisement 


A message that identifies the net settlement position of one or more ICA numbers (or 
customers) and is transmitted to the destination specified by the member Net Settlement 
Agreement (NSA) form. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1860 



Glossary 
alternate issuer host 


Plural Form: advisements 


alternate issuer host 


Alternate issuer authorization route used instead of the Stand-In Authorization; available in 
Europe region. 


Authorization 


Real-time communication between acquirers and issuers to approve or decline the use of a 
Mastercard-branded card, access device, or account to conduct a transaction. Approval from 
issuers will create a financial obligation from the issuer to the acquirer (for a transaction that 
debits funds from a cardholder's account) or from the acquirer to the issuer (for a transaction 
that credits funds to a cardholder's account). 


authorization request 


A request by an acquirer for issuer approval to complete a transaction involving a payment card. 
Plural Form: authorization requests 


back-office process 


Non-client-facing tasks that keep the business running and provide support for front-end 
operations. 


batch processing 


A type of data processing operation and data communications transmission where related 
transactions are grouped together and transmitted for processing, usually by the same 
computer and under the same application; generally regarded as non–real-time data traffic 
comprising large files; type of data traffic where response time is not critical. 


cardholder 


A cardholder is an authorized person to whom a payment card or a device payment has been 
issued. Also referred to as a consumer or account holder. 


Plural Form: cardholders 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

1861 



Glossary 
Clearing 


Clearing 


Multiple clearing batch processes per day (that is, clearing cycles) determine and calculate 
processing costs, resulting in one net amount per acquirer and issuer per clearing cycle. 


Dual Message Authorization System 


The Mastercard Dual Message Authorization System is a global real-time message processing 
system and is a component of the Mastercard Network. The Mastercard Network supports realtime 
authorization processing followed by batch reconciliation leading to settlement of funds 
between acquirers and issuers. 


The Authorization System processing is integrated with the acquirer and issuer processing 
system communicates in real time to process authorization data to get an issuer decision. 


Mastercard acquirers and issuers leverage the Authorization System to exchange financial 
transaction data captured at the point-of-interaction device to obtain an authorization 
decision. 


The Authorization System consists of both hardware and software components. The physical 
computing infrastructure includes servers, routers, switches, and cabling. This hardware is 
configured with Mastercard's proprietary technology, which makes it a Mastercard interface 
processor (MIP) and is physically set up and connected with an acquirer or issuer processing 
system in their data centers. 


Plural Form: Dual Message Authorization System 


Dual Message Clearing System 


The Dual Message Clearing System or Mastercard Global Clearing Management System 
(GCMS) is a component of the Mastercard Network that provides a central mechanism for the 
exchange of offline financial clearing messages. All participants are both senders and receivers 
of clearing data. 


echo 


Data repeated back to the sender by the recipient to verify that it was received correctly 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1862 



Glossary 
encryption 


encryption 


The process by which data is translated into secret code. Encryption is the most effective way to 
secure data. To read an encrypted file, the user must have access to a key or password that 
enables them to decrypt it. 


exception processing 


A procedure for managing transactions that cannot be processed or which are interrupted. 


fraud 


A deception deliberately practiced to secure unlawful gain. 


fraudulent transaction 


A transaction effected using a cardholder’s account number which is not engaged in or 
authorized by the cardholder. Such transactions are categorized as lost, stolen, not received, 
issued on a fraudulent application, counterfeit, fraudulent processing of transactions, account 
takeover (ATO), or other fraudulent conditions. 


Plural Form: fraudulent transactions 


host 


An intelligent processor or device that is connected to a network and satisfies the needs of 
remote users. 


International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 


International Organization for Standardization 8583:1987 


The international standard for bankcard-originated messages and interchange message 
specifications. 
Plural Form: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 8583:1987 
Abbreviation: ISO 8583:1987 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1863 



Glossary 
issuer 


issuer 


An issuer is a licensed Mastercard customer that issues cards or accounts and is responsible for 
approving or declining authorization requests. The issuer also bills cardholders and supports 
clearing and settlement functions to exchange funds between the cardholders account and the 
acquirer. Also referred to as an issuing bank, issuer bank, cardholder bank, or issuing financial 
institution. 


Plural Form: issuers 


issuer host 


A term referring to customer host processing at the issuer's location. 


Mastercard Network 


The computer hardware and software operated by and on behalf of the Corporation for the 
routing, processing, and settlement of Transactions and PTA Transactions including, without 
limitation, the Mastercard Network, the Mastercard ATM Network, the Dual Message System, 
the Single Message System, the Global Clearing Management System (GCMS), the Settlement 
Account Management (SAM) system, and the China Switch system. 


Plural Form: Mastercard Network 


Mastercard interface processor (MIP) 


Front-end communications processor placed on-site at a Mastercard customer’s facility or at a 
processor or hub site. The MIP provides access to the Mastercard Network. 
Plural Form: Mastercard interface processors 
Abbreviation: MIP 


Network 


See Switch. 


Network Enablement Partner 


A service provider that has a direct agreement with Mastercard and performs certain functions 
on behalf of one or more customers. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved.

Glossary 
primary issuer 


Plural Form: Network Enablement Partners 


primary issuer 


Banking primary issuer, also known as an issuing bank or card issuer, is a financial institution 
that provides a cardholder with a payment card 


processor 


A processor provides authorization, clearing, or settlement services on behalf of a customer. Also 
referred to as a third-party processor or payment processor. 


Plural Form: processors 


reason code 


Also known as message reason code. For each chargeback, an issuer selects and submits a 
numeric reason code. This code assist the merchant and acquirer diagnose errors and improve 
customer experience. 


Plural Form: reason codes 


receipt 


A hard copy document recording a transaction that took place at the point of interaction, with a 
description that usually includes the date, merchant name/location, primary account number, 
amount, and reference number. 


reconciliation 


Process by which settlement payments are balanced against amounts and totals as provided by 
the association’s processing systems. 


request 


A message originated an interactive series of messages. 
Plural Form: requests 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1865 



Glossary 
response code 


response code 


Response codes indicate the disposition of a previous message or an action taken as a result of 
receipt of a previous message. 


Plural Form: response codes 


response time 


The elapsed time between the generation of the last character of a message at a terminal and 
the receipt of the first character of the reply. it includes terminal delay and network delay. 


Plural Form: response times 


reversal message 


A message relating to a reversal. 
Plural Form: reversal messages 


service provider 


A person or entity that is registered with Mastercard by a customer to perform services related 
to the customers issuing or an acquiring activity. 


Plural Form: service providers 


Settlement 


Aggregates financial positions from all clearing settlement information into one overall daily net 
settlement amount for each acquirer and issuer. Creating and distributing advisements 
(notifications) to acquirers and issuers along with Transfer Funds Orders to Settlement Banks 
for amounts to be transferred to or collected from acquirers and issuers. 


Single Message System 


A global real-time message processing system and is a component of the Mastercard Network. 
The Mastercard Network supports real-time authorization processing followed by batch 
reconciliation leading to settlement of funds between acquirers and issuers. 


© 2024–2026 Mastercard. Proprietary. All rights reserved. 
Mastercard Network Processing—Single Message System Guide • 2 June 2026 
1866 



Glossary 
Stand-In Authorization 


Mastercard acquirers and issuers leverage the Single Message System to exchange financial 
transaction data captured at the point-of-interaction device. The Single Message System, 
through a single financial message interaction, fulfills authorization processing, reconciliation, 
and settlement functions. 


The Single Message System consists of both hardware and software components. The physical 
computing infrastructure includes servers, routers, switches, and cabling. This hardware is 
configured with Mastercard's proprietary technology, which makes it a Mastercard interface 
processor (MIP) and is physically set up and connected with an acquirer or issuer processing 
system in their data centers. 


Plural Form: Single Message System 


Abbreviation: Single Message System 


Stand-In Authorization 


Authorization processing provided by Mastercard for online issuers that are unavailable or that 
cannot be reached. 


Switch 


The computer hardware and software operated by and on behalf of a payment scheme for the 
routing, processing, and settlement of transactions bearing the payment scheme brand in 
accordance with such payment scheme’s rules and regulations, and which may also be used to 
route transactions to another payment scheme’s switch or to route, process, and settle nonbranded 
(also called private label) transactions as agreed by the participating parties. Also 
called a Network. 


Plural Form: Switches 


Dual Message Switch 


A Switch used to process transactions for which authorization and clearing occurs separately in 
a dual message format. The Mastercard Dual Message System (both authorization and 
clearing) is a Dual Message Switch. 


Single Message Switch 


A Switch used to process transactions for which authorization and clearing occurs in a single 
message format. The Mastercard Single Message System is a Single Message Switch.

Glossary 
X-Code, X-Code Processing 


X-Code, X-Code Processing 


A system that performs issuer functions by receiving and responding to authorization requests 
at the acquirer Mastercard interface processor (MIP).

DE 1 (Bit Map, Secondary)
